quote: Paths are made by walking them.
author: Antonio Machado
source_work: Antonio Machado, "Proverbios y cantares" XXIX, in Campos de Castilla (1912)
notes: English rendering of "se hace camino al andar"; commonly misattributed to Kafka, Nietzsche or Kästner. Renders the source loosely: Checked the Campos de Castilla text in the Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes: the poem reads "caminante, no hay camino, / se hace camino al andar", of which the bank line is a faithful English condensation.

quote: Year by year, it takes less time to get across the ocean, but more time to get to the office.
notes: Attributed to Unknown in source. Attribution unverified: Searched TIME magazine commuting coverage of 1960 ("Those Rush-Hour Blues" and the 8 February 1960 letters column) and the New Yorker archive of the same period without finding this quip; it appears only on anonymous quotation aggregators.

quote: Movement is everything, direction is what matters.
author: Manfred Hinrich
notes: Attribution unverified: The German aphorism circulates under Hinrich's name on German quotation sites but no primary publication of his roughly 30000 aphorisms could be located, so the attribution stays unconfirmed.

quote: Some of the most rewarding goals in life are achieved through detours.
author: Francis Paul Wilson
notes: Attribution unverified: No occurrence of this sentence in F. Paul Wilson interviews or in the bibliographic entries for him (the St. James Guide entry reproduced at Encyclopedia.com, the SF Encyclopedia, the fan-maintained Wilson wiki); it surfaces only on quotation aggregators.

quote: It's the unknown around the corner that turns my wheel.
author: Heinz Stucke
source_work: Heinz Stücke's personal motto, painted on his bicycle and printed in his self-published travel booklet (1992; text reproduced at bikechina.com)
notes: Wording as collected was: It's the unknown waiting around the next corner that pushes my wheels forward. Wording corrected against the source: Stucke's motto, reproduced from his own booklet at bikechina.com and quoted in the Adventure Cycling Association obituary, runs "Be carefree, be mad, be a little bit bad. It is the unknown around the corner that turns my wheel"; the bank rewrites it as "waiting around the next corner" and "pushes my wheels forward".

quote: Transportation is the centre of the world. It is the glue of our daily lives. When it goes well, we don't see it. When it goes wrong, it negatively colours our day, makes us feel angry and curtails our possibilities.
author: Robin Chase
source_work: Robin Chase, interviewed by Dan Schawbel, "How Robin Chase Reinvented the Transportation Industry", Forbes, 22 June 2012
notes: Renders the source loosely: The Forbes interview reads "Transportation is the center of the world! It is the glue of our daily lives. When it goes well, we don't see it. When it goes wrong, it negatively colors our day, makes us feel angry and impotent, curtails our possibilities."; the bank drops "and impotent" and anglicises the spelling but misstates nothing.

quote: A developed country is not a place where the poor have cars. It's where the rich use public transportation.
author: Enrique Peñalosa
source_work: Entretien avec l'agence EFE, publié dans Semana, 13 décembre 2010
notes: Former mayor of Bogota and president of Colombia. Previously attributed to Gustavo Petro. Reattributed: Spanish Wikiquote sources it to Peñalosa via Semana, and kottke.org documents that the Petro attribution stems from a viral 2012 tweet; the English is itself a loose rendering.

quote: Humanity has advanced, when it has advanced, not because it has been sober, responsible, and cautious, but because it has been playful, rebellious, and immature.
author: Tom Robbins
source_work: Tom Robbins, Still Life with Woodpecker (Bantam, 1980), the passage defining "neoteny"
notes: Verified: Checked against the text of Still Life with Woodpecker, where the sentence closes Robbins's paragraph on neoteny ("Humans are the most advanced of mammals ... because they seldom grow up"); the wording matches the bank exactly.

quote: Wunder erleben nur diejenigen, die an Wunder glauben.
author: Erich Kästner
notes: Attribution unverified: Not found in Kästner's writings; the attribution appears only in unsourced quotation collections, and neither Zitatforschung nor the Kästner bibliography knows of any evidence.

quote: On ne voit bien qu'avec le cœur. L'essentiel est invisible pour les yeux.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Verified: Matches the fox's farewell speech in the French text.

quote: Man sieht nur mit dem Herzen gut. Das Wesentliche ist für die Augen unsichtbar.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: German translation of the French original. Verified: Matches the standard German translation by Grete and Josef Leitgeb.

quote: Mais si tu m'apprivoises, nous aurons besoin l'un de l'autre. Tu seras pour moi unique au monde. Je serai pour toi unique au monde.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Verified: Matches the fox's explanation of apprivoiser in the French text.

quote: Je me demande, dit-il, si les étoiles sont éclairées afin que chacun puisse un jour retrouver la sienne.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Wording as collected was: Les étoiles sont éclairées pour que chacun puisse un jour retrouver la sienne. Wording corrected against the source: The original is a tentative question introduced by "Je me demande si" with "afin que", not an affirmative maxim.

quote: Toutes les grandes personnes ont d'abord été des enfants. Mais peu d'entre elles s'en souviennent.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
source_work: Le Petit Prince, dedication to Léon Werth (1943)
notes: Verified: Matches the dedication; the original places the second sentence in parentheses.

quote: Alle großen Leute sind einmal Kinder gewesen (aber wenige erinnern sich daran).
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
source_work: Le Petit Prince, dedication to Léon Werth (1943)
notes: German translation of the French original. Verified: Matches the Leitgeb German translation of the dedication.

quote: Il est bien plus difficile de se juger soi-même que de juger autrui.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Verified: Matches the king's speech in the French text.

quote: Es ist viel schwerer, sich selbst zu verurteilen, als über andere zu richten.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: German translation of the French original. Verified: Matches the Leitgeb German translation of the king's speech in chapter X.

quote: Les hommes n'ont plus le temps de rien connaître. Ils achètent des choses toutes faites chez les marchands. Mais comme il n'existe point de marchands d'amis, les hommes n'ont plus d'amis.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Verified: Matches the fox's speech on friendship in the French text.

quote: Les baobabs, avant de grandir, ça commence par être petit.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Verified: Matches the little prince's remark on baobabs in the French text.

quote: Ce n'était qu'un renard semblable à cent mille autres. Mais j'en ai fait mon ami, et il est maintenant unique au monde.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Wording as collected was: Ce n'était qu'un renard semblable à cent mille autres. Mais j'en ai fait mon ami, et il est maintenant unique. Wording corrected against the source: The bank drops "au monde"; the prince's speech to the roses ends "unique au monde".

quote: Was vergangen ist, ist vergangen, und du weißt nicht, was die Zukunft dir bringen mag. Aber das Hier und Jetzt, das gehört dir.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Attributed to Le Petit Prince in source. Attribution unverified: German Wikiquote lists this exact sentence under "Fälschlich zugeschrieben" and confirms it appears nowhere in Le Petit Prince.

quote: Zuweilen macht es ja wohl nichts aus, wenn man seine Arbeit auf später verschiebt.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Verified: Located in the baobab passage of ch. 5 in three independent full-text editions including the Gutenberg Australia text.

quote: Du weißt doch, wenn man recht traurig ist, liebt man Sonnenuntergänge.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Verified: Confirmed verbatim in ch. 6 (the forty-three sunsets passage) across four independent full-text editions.

quote: We are what we think. All that we are arises with our thoughts. With our thoughts we make the world. Speak or act with an impure mind and trouble will follow you as the wheel follows the ox that draws the cart. Speak or act with a pure mind and happiness will follow you as your shadow, unbreakable.
author: Buddha
notes: An abbreviated version appears in another note. Renders the source loosely: Thomas Byrom's loose rendering of Dhammapada 1-2; fakebuddhaquotes.com treats "with our thoughts we make the world" as a mistranslation of manomayā.

quote: The root of suffering is attachment.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Bodhipaksa (fakebuddhaquotes.com) confirms this as a genuine canonical line, rendered by Bhikkhu Bodhi as "attachment is the root of suffering".

quote: Nothing is forever except change.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Not in any Buddhist scripture; fakebuddhaquotes.com lists the variant "Nothing remains without change" as fake and the epigram echoes a loose paraphrase of Heraclitus.

quote: Do not look for a sanctuary in anyone except yourself.
author: Buddha
source_work: Samyutta Nikaya 22.43 (Attadipa Sutta); parallel at Digha Nikaya 16.2.26
notes: Renders the source loosely: Modern loose rendering of the canonical "be your own island, your own refuge"; fakebuddhaquotes.com shows how this passage was Christianised into "do not depend on others" style quotes.

quote: If you find no one to support you on the spiritual path, walk alone.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Bodhipaksa calls the "walk alone" quotes an interpretive paraphrase rather than a translation of these Dhammapada verses.

quote: All that we are is the result of what we have thought.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Max Müller's 1881 rendering of Dhammapada 1; the Pali says experiences are preceded by and made by mind, not that we are the result of our thoughts.

quote: Radiate boundless love towards the entire world.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Standard rendering of the Karaniya Metta Sutta verse, Pali per SuttaCentral's Mahāsaṅgīti edition.

quote: May all beings have happy minds.
author: Buddha
source_work: Sutta Nipata 1.8 (Metta Sutta) v. 3 and v. 5
notes: Verified: Renders sabbasattā bhavantu sukhitattā from the Metta Sutta refrain, verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: True love is born from understanding.
author: Buddha
notes: Source had a stray 'tl' appended. Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa (fakebuddhaquotes.com) found no canonical source and notes it merely sounds like Thich Nhat Hanh, whose nearest lines are differently worded.

quote: Be where you are; otherwise you will miss your life.
author: Jack Kornfield
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Bodhipaksa traces it to page 80 of Kornfield's Buddha's Little Instruction Book (1994), which he calls the single largest source of fake Buddha quotes.

quote: What you are is what you have been. What you'll be is what you do now.
author: Sogyal Rinpoche
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Per fakebuddhaquotes.com the earliest known appearance is Sogyal Rinpoche's The Tibetan Book of Living and Dying (1992), apparently his own paraphrase of karma doctrine.

quote: Irrigators channel waters; fletchers straighten arrows; carpenters bend wood; the wise master themselves.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Accurate rendering of Dhammapada 80, Pali confirmed on SuttaCentral.

quote: An idea that is developed and put into action is more important than an idea that exists only as an idea.
author: Edward de Bono
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Bodhipaksa traced it to page 47 of de Bono's Serious Creativity; it has no scriptural source.

quote: To be idle is a short road to death and to be diligent is a way of life. Foolish people are idle, wise people are diligent.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Dwight Goddard's deliberately Christianised rendering of Dhammapada 21, per fakebuddhaquotes.com, which turns appamada into "diligence" and adds "short road".

quote: Being deeply learned and skilled, being well trained and using well-spoken words: this is good luck.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Faithful rendering of the Mangala Sutta verse on learning, skill, training and good speech, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: Ardently do today what must be done. Who knows? Tomorrow, death comes.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Thanissaro's rendering of the Bhaddekaratta verse; Bodhipaksa cites the same line as genuine.

quote: As a water bead on a lotus leaf, as water on a red lily, does not adhere, so the sage does not adhere to the seen, the heard, or the sensed.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Thanissaro's translation of Sn 4.6, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Ceasing to do evil, cultivating the good, purifying the heart: this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Accurate rendering of the famous Ovada Patimokkha verse, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: A disciplined mind brings happiness.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Condenses cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ of Dhammapada 35, verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: All experiences are preceded by mind, having mind as their master, created by mind.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Gil Fronsdal's accurate rendering of the opening line of Dhammapada 1, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: If anything is worth doing, do it with all your heart.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Eknath Easwaran's rendering of Dhammapada 313, which Bodhipaksa judges close enough to the Pali to count as genuine.

quote: Even death is not to be feared by one who has lived wisely.
author: Jack Kornfield
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Bodhipaksa found it on page 88 of Kornfield's Buddha's Little Instruction Book, loosely paraphrasing AN 4.184.

quote: Nothing can harm you as much as your own thoughts unguarded.
author: Buddha
notes: A variant appears in another note. Renders the source loosely: Bodhipaksa calls this a close enough paraphrase of the Anguttara passage on the unguarded mind that it would be unfair to call it fake.

quote: It is a man's own mind, not his enemy or foe, that lures him to evil ways.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Loose English rendering of Dhammapada 42, whose Pali says a wrongly directed mind harms one more than any enemy could.

quote: Everything in moderation, including moderation.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator finds no support for any famous attribution and traces the earliest English form to a 1927 verse collection; it has no Buddhist source whatsoever.

quote: There is no fear for one whose mind is not filled with desires.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Partial and loose rendering of Dhammapada 39, which speaks of a mind unsoaked by desire and of one who is wakeful having no fear.

quote: Work out your own salvation. Do not depend on others.
author: Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Bodhipaksa traced this exact wording to a 1961 interview with D. T. Suzuki in James Nelson's Wisdom For Our Time, itself a simplification of Paul Carus's Christianising rendering of Digha Nikaya 16.

quote: Pain is certain; suffering is optional.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa places its origin in the twelve-step tradition with the earliest attribution (1983) to M. Kathleen Casey; the idea parallels SN 36.6 but the words are not the Buddha's.

quote: Love is a gift of one's inner most soul to another so both can be whole.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Listed as fake by fakebuddhaquotes.com; the appeal to an innermost soul contradicts the Buddha's teaching of anatta.

quote: You, yourself, as much as anybody in the entire universe, deserve your love and affection.
author: Sharon Salzberg
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Bodhipaksa traced it to Salzberg's Lovingkindness (1995) and a 1989 magazine piece, derived from Mahasi Sayadaw's rendering of Udana 5.1 but with its meaning reversed.

quote: The way is not in the sky. The way is in the heart.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Thomas Byrom's invention loosely occasioned by Dhammapada 254, which says only that there is no track in the sky and no ascetic outside the teaching; Bodhipaksa calls it utterly fake.

quote: Your work is to discover your work and then with all your heart to give yourself to it.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Anne Bancroft's very free rendering of Dhammapada 166, a verse about not neglecting one's own welfare that says nothing about work; judged fake by fakebuddhaquotes.com.

quote: Understanding is the heartwood of well-spoken words.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Thanissaro's translation of Sn 2.9 on Access to Insight, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Just as a mother would protect her only child with her life, even so let one cultivate a boundless love towards all beings.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Acharya Buddharakkhita's rendering of the Metta Sutta mother simile, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: Let all-embracing thoughts for all beings be yours.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Renders the Metta Sutta line on unfolding a boundless heart toward all beings, verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Hatred does not cease by hatred, but only by love; this is the eternal rule.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Max Müller's translation of Dhammapada 5, which fakebuddhaquotes.com lists among genuine quotes, though "love" renders averena, non-hatred.

quote: We will develop and cultivate the liberation of mind by loving kindness, make it our vehicle, make it our basis, stabilize it, exercise ourselves in it, and fully perfect it.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Bhikkhu Bodhi's translation of SN 20.3, confirmed genuine by fakebuddhaquotes.com and Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Speak only endearing speech, speech that is welcomed. Speech, when it brings no evil to others, is a pleasant thing.
author: Vangisa
source_work: Sutta Nipata 3.3 (Subhasita Sutta) v. 454; also Samyutta Nikaya 8.5 and Theragatha 21.1
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Genuinely canonical but spoken by the monk Vangisa, not the Buddha, as SuttaCentral's text of Sn 3.3 makes clear.

quote: One moment can change a day, one day can change a life, and one life can change the world.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Listed as fake on fakebuddhaquotes.com; a modern inspirational formula with no scriptural basis.

quote: Live every act fully, as if it were your last.
author: Jack Kornfield
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Not in the canon; it appears in Kornfield's Buddha's Little Instruction Book, which fakebuddhaquotes.com identifies as the main source of fake Buddha quotes.

quote: Offend in neither word nor deed. Eat with moderation. Live in your heart. Seek the highest consciousness. Master yourself according to the law. This is the simple teaching of the awakened.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Thomas Byrom's loose rendering of Dhammapada 185, where "live in your heart" stands for the Pali's remote lodgings and "seek the highest consciousness" for adhicitta.

quote: Everything is based on mind, is led by mind, is fashioned by mind. If you speak and act with a polluted mind, suffering will follow you, as the wheels of the oxcart follow the footsteps of the ox.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: An accurate translation of Dhammapada 1 including the ox-cart simile, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: Better it is to live one day seeing the rise and fall of things than to live a hundred years without ever seeing the rise and fall of things.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Faithful rendering of Dhammapada 113, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Should you find a wise critic to point out your faults, follow him as you would a guide to hidden treasure.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Accurate rendering of Dhammapada 76 on the wise critic as a guide to hidden treasure, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: In separateness lies the world's greatest misery; in compassion lies the world's true strength.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa found no canonical basis and notes the Buddha never used the language of "separateness"; earliest full appearance is a 2002 memoir quoting it as a Buddha saying.

quote: Don't rush anything. When the time is right, it'll happen.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Absent from the canon; fakebuddhaquotes.com treats the near-identical "Be patient, everything comes to you in the right moment" as an internet-borne fake of unknown authorship.

quote: The world is afflicted by death and decay. But the wise do not grieve, having realized the nature of the world.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Close rendering of Sn 3.8 verse 8, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased. This is a law eternal.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Acharya Buddharakkhita's literal translation of Dhammapada 5, listed among genuine quotes by fakebuddhaquotes.com.

quote: Anger will never disappear so long as thoughts of resentment are cherished in the mind. Anger will disappear just as soon as thoughts of resentment are forgotten.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Modern loose paraphrase matching no standard translation, but structurally the Dhammapada 3-4 teaching that enmity persists only while such thoughts are harboured.

quote: The instant we feel anger we have already ceased striving for the truth, and have begun striving for ourselves.
author: Thomas Carlyle
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Bodhipaksa traced it to Carlyle's 1829 essay "Voltaire", where he quotes it as from "a wise man", possibly the Rev. Archibald Alison.

quote: Know from the rivers in clefts and in crevices: those in small channels flow noisily, the great flow silent. Whatever's not full makes noise. Whatever is full is quiet.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Thanissaro's rendering of the Buddha's advice to Nalaka, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: There is no fire like passion. There is no shark like hatred. There is no snare like folly. There is no torrent like greed.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Rendering of Dhammapada 251, where "shark" interprets gaho (a seizer or grasping) and "torrent" renders nadī, river.

quote: Not by rituals and resolutions, nor by much learning, nor by celibacy, nor even by meditation can you find the supreme, immortal joy of nirvana until you extinguish your self-will.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Eknath Easwaran's free rendering of Dhp 271-272, where "extinguish your self-will" stands for appatto āsavakkhayaṃ (not having reached the destruction of the taints); Pali checked against the Mahasangiti edition.

quote: All tremble at violence; all fear death. Putting oneself in the place of another, one should not kill nor cause another to kill.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Close and complete translation of Dhp 129, verified line by line against the Pali Dhammapada.

quote: Conquer anger with non-anger. Conquer badness with goodness. Conquer meanness with generosity.
author: Buddha
notes: 2024 file has typo 'Conqur badness'. Verified: Accurate rendering of the first three clauses of Dhp 223; only the fourth (conquer the liar with truth) is dropped.

quote: To be angry is to let others' mistakes punish yourself.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Modern self-help aphorism with no canonical source, closely related to the fake "You will not be punished for your anger" that Bodhipaksa traces to Western writers of 1905-1927.

quote: He who can curb his wrath as soon as it arises, as a timely antidote will check snake's venom that so quickly spreads -- such a monk gives up the here and the beyond, just as a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Piyadassi Thera's translation of the opening verse of the Uraga Sutta; Pali confirmed on SuttaCentral and in Anandajoti's edition.

quote: There is no path to happiness. Happiness is the path.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa traces this exact formulation to Paul Ferrini (1992) riffing on A. J. Muste's credo "There is no way to peace; peace is the way", with no canonical basis.

quote: One who acts on truth is happy in this world and beyond.
author: Buddha
source_work: Dhammapada 169 (Lokavagga); the same line closes verse 168
notes: Renders the source loosely: Condensation of the verse's second half, loosening dhammacārī ("one who lives by the Dhamma") into "one who acts on truth".

quote: Thousands of candles can be lighted from a single candle, and the life of the candle will not be shortened. Happiness never decreases by being shared.
author: Buddha
source_work: Sutra of Forty-Two Sections, section 10 (the torch simile)
notes: Renders the source loosely: Bodhipaksa rates this "fakeish": the wording is from the modern Japanese compilation The Teaching of Buddha, loosely reworking the sutra's torch simile, and I could not verify the Chinese original.

quote: If with a pure mind a person speaks or acts, happiness follows him like his never-departing shadow.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Buddharakkhita's translation of the second half of Dhp 2, verified against the Pali.

quote: Our life is shaped by our mind. We become what we think. Joy follows a pure thought like a shadow that never leaves.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Eknath Easwaran's rendering of Dhp 1-2, which Bodhipaksa lists among mistranslations because manopubbaṅgamā dhammā says experiences are preceded by mind, not that we become our thoughts.

quote: Health is the greatest gift, contentment the greatest wealth, faithfulness the best relationship.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Faithful to Dhp 204 except that the fourth clause (Nibbana the highest happiness) is omitted and vissāsa/ñāti is softened to "faithfulness the best relationship".

quote: Drop by drop is the water pot filled. Likewise, the wise man, gathering it little by little, fills himself with good.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Buddharakkhita's translation of Dhp 122 minus its opening line ("Think not lightly of good"), verified against the Pali.

quote: All conditioned things are impermanent -- when one sees this with wisdom, one turns away from suffering.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Standard translation of Dhp 277, with only the closing "this is the path to purification" left off.

quote: Happiness will never come to those who fail to appreciate what they already have.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: No canonical source: absent from the Pali canon, not even catalogued by Bodhipaksa, and traceable only to modern quote aggregators.

quote: Whatever is not yours: let go of it. Your letting go of it will be for your long-term happiness and benefit.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Thanissaro Bhikkhu's translation of the "whatever is not yours" passage of MN 22, verified against the Pali text.

quote: Delight in meditation and solitude. Compose yourself, be happy. You are a seeker.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Thomas Byrom's very free rendering of Dhp 362, in which "You are a seeker" stands for tamāhu bhikkhuṃ and "solitude" for eko.

quote: Those who are free of resentful thoughts surely find peace.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Bodhipaksa traces this to Eknath Easwaran's Words to Live By (1990) and calls it a good paraphrase of Dhp 4, which speaks of stilling hatred rather than finding peace.

quote: Do not overrate what you have received, nor envy others. He who envies others does not obtain peace of mind.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Bodhipaksa rates this "fakeish" because nātimaññeyya means "should not despise" rather than "overrate"; he finds it first in Joseph Gaer's The Wisdom of the Living Religions (1956).

quote: He who sits alone, sleeps alone, and walks alone, who is strenuous and subdues himself alone, will find delight in the solitude of the forest.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Close translation of Dhp 305, verified against the Pali.

quote: Don't run after pleasure and neglect the practice of meditation. If you forget the goal of life and get caught in the pleasures of the world, you will come to envy those who put meditation first.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Eknath Easwaran's expansive rendering of Dhp 209, which literally contrasts exerting oneself in the wrong thing with pursuing the goal.

quote: A man is not called wise because he talks and talks again. But if he is peaceful, loving, and fearless, then he is in truth called wise.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Accurate translation of Dhp 258, where khemī averī abhayo gives "peaceful, loving, and fearless".

quote: A mind unruffled by the vagaries of fortune, from sorrow freed, from defilements cleansed, from fear liberated -- this is the greatest blessing.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Narada Thera's translation of this Mangala Sutta verse; Pali confirmed on SuttaCentral and in the Aimwell exposition.

quote: Meditate. Do not delay, lest you later regret it.
author: Buddha
source_work: Majjhima Nikaya 8 (Sallekha Sutta); same formula at MN 19 and SN 43.1
notes: Verified: Bodhipaksa's Real Buddha Quotes confirms this as genuine, from the Sallekha Sutta; the Pali stock exhortation is attested at MN 19 and throughout SN 43.

quote: Better than a thousand hollow words, is one word that brings peace.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Faithful condensation of Dhp 100, "one useful word, hearing which one attains peace".

quote: Resolutely train yourself to attain peace.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Precisely John D. Ireland's translation of daḷhaṃ sikkhatha santiyā in Snp 2.10, with the Pali as printed by the Vipassana Research Institute.

quote: Give, even if you only have a little.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Renders only the middle clause of Dhp 224 (dajjā appampi yācito, "give even a little when asked"), dropping the qualifier "when asked" and the rest of the verse.

quote: If you knew what I know about the power of giving, you would not let a single meal pass without sharing it in some way.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Loose rendering of Itivuttaka 26, where the Buddha says beings who knew the fruit of giving as he knows it would not eat without having shared.

quote: To live a pure unselfish life, one must count nothing as one's own in the midst of abundance.
author: Buddha
notes: 2026 file has 'ones own'. Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa shows this comes from the modern Japanese compilation The Teaching of Buddha, not from any Buddhist scripture.

quote: The greatest gift is to give people your enlightenment, to share it. It has to be the greatest.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: No canonical source; the colloquial phrasing is modern, and the idea that one's own enlightenment is the greatest gift belongs to Osho's talks rather than the canon.

quote: Teach this triple truth to all: A generous heart, kind speech, and a life of service and compassion are the things which renew humanity.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa finds no scriptural source (earliest instance Elaine Parke, 2001) and notes that "renew humanity" is alien to canonical idiom, though the triad echoes the sangaha-vatthus of the Sigalovada Sutta (DN 31).

quote: If we fail to look after others when they need help, who will look after us?
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Loose rendering of the Buddha's rebuke over the monk with dysentery, "If you don't tend to one another, who then will tend to you?"; I located the passage but could not verify its Pali wording, so the original text is left blank.

quote: Whatever words we utter should be chosen with care for people will hear them and be influenced by them for good or ill.
author: Dwight Goddard
source_work: Dwight Goddard, A Buddhist Bible (1932), within his version of the Kakacupama Sutta (MN 21)
notes: Previously attributed to Buddha. Reattributed: Bodhipaksa identifies these as Goddard's own commentary, blended undifferentiated into his rendering of MN 21 and thereafter quoted as the Buddha's words.

quote: True charity occurs only when there are no notions of giving, giver, or gift.
author: Buddha
notes: 2023 file has typo 'Trtrue charity'. Renders the source loosely: Modern summary of the Mahayana threefold emptiness of giving taught in Diamond Sutra chapter 4 ("a bodhisattva should not give abiding in any notion whatsoever"); nothing corresponds in the Pali canon and I did not verify the Sanskrit or Chinese wording.

quote: Before giving, the mind of the giver is happy; while giving, the mind of the giver is made peaceful; and having given, the mind of the giver is uplifted.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Accurate rendering of the donor's three factors in AN 6.37, verified against SuttaCentral's Pali; only the closing "this is the success of the offering" is omitted.

quote: To support mother and father, to cherish wife and children, and to be engaged in peaceful occupation -- this is the greatest blessing.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Narada Thera's translation of this Mangala Sutta verse; Pali confirmed on SuttaCentral and in the Aimwell exposition.

quote: When watching after yourself, you watch after others. When watching after others, you watch after yourself.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Thanissaro Bhikkhu's translation of the conclusion the Buddha draws from the acrobat simile in SN 47.19.

quote: Just as a solid rock is not shaken by the storm, even so the wise are not affected by praise or blame.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Buddharakkhita's translation of Dhp 81, verified against the Pali.

quote: Endurance is one of the most difficult disciplines, but it is to the one who endures that the final victory comes.
author: Buddha
source_work: Dhammapada 184 (Buddhavagga); second half cf. a Samyutta Nikaya verse on patience as victory
notes: Renders the source loosely: Bodhipaksa rates this "fakeish": The Teaching of Buddha welds Dhp 184 ("enduring patience is the highest austerity") to a Samyutta verse making patient endurance the true victory, whose Pali I did not verify.

quote: No one saves us but ourselves. No one can and no one may. We ourselves must walk the path.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Bodhipaksa traces the wording to Paul Carus's rhymed Karma: A Story of Buddhist Ethics (1894), a very free version of Dhp 165 in which "no one may" was added to fit the rhyme.

quote: The one who has conquered himself is a far greater hero than he who has defeated a thousand times a thousand men.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Faithful rendering of Dhp 103, verified against the Pali.

quote: Be a lamp for yourselves. Be your own refuge. Seek for no other. All things must pass. Strive on diligently. Don't give up.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Conflates two separate passages of DN 16, the "be lamps unto yourselves" exhortation and the Buddha's last words, into a single quotation.

quote: Wear your ego like a loose fitting garment.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa finds this to be a recent internet coinage, probably adapted from the mid-20th-century idiom "wearing life like a loose garment".

quote: What we are today comes from our thoughts of yesterday, and our present thoughts build our life of tomorrow: our life is the creation of our mind.
author: Buddha
notes: Renders the source loosely: Bodhipaksa identifies this as Juan Mascaro's Penguin translation of Dhp 1, which he classes among mistranslations rather than as the Buddha's words.

quote: Meditation brings wisdom; lack of meditation leaves ignorance. Know well what leads you forward and what hold you back, and choose the path that leads to wisdom.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Substantially faithful to the whole of Dhp 282, with yoga rendered "meditation" as in most published translations.

quote: You yourself must strive. The Buddhas only point the way.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Exactly Buddharakkhita's translation of the first half of Dhp 276, verified against the Pali.

quote: As an elephant in the battlefield withstands arrows shot from bows all around, even so shall I endure abuse.
author: Buddha
notes: Verified: Buddharakkhita's translation of Dhp 320, omitting only the closing "there are many, indeed, who lack virtue".

quote: Do not dwell in the past, do not dream of the future, concentrate the mind on the present moment.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa traces the wording to The Teaching of Buddha (1934) and rates it fake, since its third clause reverses Dhammapada 348, which says to let go of the present rather than concentrate on it.

quote: Before enlightenment; chop wood, carry water. After enlightenment; chop wood, carry water.
notes: Zen proverb traced to a verse by Layman Pang (8th c.); often misattributed to Buddha. Attribution unverified: The Zen ancestor is Layman P'ang's verse in the Jingde Chuandeng Lu ("my miraculous power and marvellous activity: drawing water and carrying firewood"), discussed in Tricycle's "Green Koans Case 36: P'ang Splits Wood", but the "before enlightenment / after enlightenment" formulation cannot be traced to any Zen text or named teacher.

quote: Your worst enemy cannot harm you as much as your own unguarded thoughts.
author: Buddha
notes: Variant of 'Nothing can harm you as much as your own thoughts unguarded.' Renders the source loosely: Thomas Byrom's rendering of Dhp 42; Bodhipaksa accepts the near-identical "nothing can harm you as much as your own unguarded thoughts" as a fair paraphrase, citing an Anguttara parallel on the unguarded mind.

quote: You will not be punished for your anger, you will be punished by your anger.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa finds no canonical source, tracing the "punished by, not for" formula to W. P. Burke (1905) and Elbert Hubbard (1927) and its Buddhist dress to Eknath Easwaran's paraphrase.

quote: Remembering a wrong is like carrying a burden on the mind.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa rates this fake, judging it non-canonical on linguistic grounds and finding no instance earlier than 2006.

quote: Genius is the recovery of childhood at will.
author: Charles Baudelaire
source_work: Le Peintre de la vie moderne (1863), III "L'artiste, homme du monde, homme des foules et enfant"
notes: Compare Baudelaire variant 'Le genie, c'est l'enfance retrouvee a volonte.' Previously attributed to Arthur Rimbaud. Reattributed: The line is Baudelaire's, not Rimbaud's, per the critical text of Le Peintre de la vie moderne (Wuppertal lyriktheorie edition and Wikisource).

quote: Le génie, c'est l'enfance retrouvée à volonté.
author: Charles Baudelaire
source_work: Le Peintre de la vie moderne, III L'artiste, homme du monde, homme des foules et enfant (1863)
notes: Compare Rimbaud variant in English. Renders the source loosely: Condenses Baudelaire's sentence, which reads in full: Mais le génie n'est que l'enfance retrouvée à volonté, l'enfance douée maintenant, pour s'exprimer, d'organes virils et de l'esprit analytique qui lui permet d'ordonner la somme de matériaux involontairement amassée. The short form is the one that circulates, and is kept deliberately.

quote: Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life. Don't be trapped by dogma - which is living with the results of other people's thinking. Don't let the noise of other's opinions drown out your own inner voice. And most important, have the courage to follow your heart and intuition. They somehow already know what you truly want to become. Everything else is secondary.
author: Steve Jobs
source_work: Steve Jobs, Commencement address, Stanford University, 12 June 2005 (official transcript, news.stanford.edu)
notes: Verified: from Steve Jobs's 2005 Stanford Commencement Address; unattributed in the original source file. Verified: Matches the official Stanford transcript word for word, apart from the bank's "other's" for "others'" opinions.

quote: Beyond a certain point there is no return. This point has to be reached.
author: Franz Kafka
source_work: Betrachtungen über Sünde, Leid, Hoffnung und den wahren Weg (Zürauer Aphorismen, 1917/18), Nr. 5
notes: Verified: Verified verbatim as aphorism 5 in the digitised text of Kafka's Zürau aphorisms (digbib.org edition).

quote: Plant your own garden and decorate your own soul, instead of waiting for someone to bring you flowers.
author: Veronica A. Shoffstall
notes: Renders the source loosely: The poem reads "So you plant your own garden and decorate your own soul, instead of waiting for someone to bring you flowers"; the bank only drops the opening "So you". Shoffstall has publicly confirmed writing the poem in 1971, and it is frequently misattributed to Jorge Luis Borges.

quote: Winning isn't everything.. It's the only thing.
author: Henry 'Red' Sanders
source_work: Henry 'Red' Sanders, speech to the Birmingham Quarterback Club, reported in The Birmingham News, 9 November 1948; also quoted in the Los Angeles Times, 18 October 1950
notes: Coined by football coach Henry 'Red' Sanders (1948); widely misattributed to Vince Lombardi, and in the source file to van Gogh. Verified: Quote Investigator and the Yale Book of Quotations both credit Sanders rather than Vince Lombardi, so the bank attribution is right; the punctuation should be "Winning isn't everything; it's the only thing."

quote: Never put off till tomorrow what you can do the day after tomorrow.
author: Mark Twain
source_work: Mark Twain, "The Late Benjamin Franklin", The Galaxy, July 1870
notes: Renders the source loosely: Quote Investigator's article on this quip gives Twain's original mock-Franklin maxim as "Never put off till to-morrow what you can do day after to-morrow just as well.-B. F."; the bank keeps a smoothed, shortened form of it.

quote: Failure is the condiment that gives success its flavor.
author: Truman Capote
source_work: Truman Capote, "Self-Portrait" (1972), collected in Truman Capote: Conversations, ed. M. Thomas Inge (University Press of Mississippi, 1987), p. 189
notes: Verified: Wikiquote's sourced section for Capote assigns the line to "Self-Portrait" (1972) in the Conversations volume, and the page reference matches.

quote: What's the greater risk? Letting go of what people think or letting go of how I feel, what I believe, and who I am?
author: Brené Brown
source_work: Brené Brown, The Gifts of Imperfection (Hazelden, 2010), introduction
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the text of The Gifts of Imperfection, in the introduction's discussion of Wholehearted living ("However afraid we are of change, the question that we must ultimately answer is this: What's the greater risk?").

quote: Your fears, your critics, your heroes, your villains: They are fictions you perceive as reality. Choose to see through them. Choose to let them go.
author: Isaac Lidsky
source_work: Isaac Lidsky, "What reality are you creating for yourself?", TED Talk, TED2016 (posted June 2016), closing passage
notes: Renders the source loosely: The TED transcript reads "Your fears, your critics, your heroes, your villains - they are your excuses, rationalizations, shortcuts, justifications, your surrender. They are fictions you perceive as reality. Choose to see through them. Choose to let them go."; the bank elides the middle clause without altering the sense.

quote: Don't use all-or-nothing thinking. Take each day as its own day, and don't worry about it if you mess up one day. The most important thing you can do is just get back up on the horse.
author: Henry Cloud
notes: Attribution unverified: Searched the texts of Boundaries for Leaders, 9 Things You Simply Must Do to Succeed in Love and Life, and What to Do When You Don't Know What to Do without finding this passage; it circulates only on aggregator sites.

quote: We lose ourselves in the things we love. We find ourselves there, too.
author: Dale Partridge
notes: Attribution unverified: No occurrence in Partridge's published books or talks; the line circulates unsourced on aggregators and is also credited there to Kristin Martz, and neither attribution has a printed source behind it.

quote: Successful people appear to be traveling along one continual, successful road. What is not apparent is the perseverance it takes following each defeat to keep you on that road. No one I know of has ever experienced one success after another without defeats, failures, disappointments, and frustrations galore along the way. Learning to overcome those times of agony is what separates the winners from the losers.
author: G. Kingsley Ward
source_work: G. Kingsley Ward, Letters of a Businessman to His Son (1985; 1988 printing)
notes: Verified: Quoted verbatim by Karlo Zorec working from his own copy of the 1988 edition; the wording matches the bank exactly, sentence for sentence.

quote: Das Wort stirbt, wenn wir es nicht mit anderen teilen.
author: Tschingis Aitmatow
source_work: Begegnung am Fudschijama. Ein Dialog mit Daisaku Ikeda (Unionsverlag 1992), aus dem Russischen von Friedrich Hitzer
notes: Kyrgyz writer. Verified: Unionsverlag, the German publisher, quotes exactly this sentence for that book, but it is Hitzer's German translation and the Russian original wording could not be located, so it is left blank.

quote: Ihr Lächeln war von der echten Art. Es geschah weniger mit den Lippen als mit den Augen; das ganze Gesicht, Stirn und Wangen glänzten innig mit, und es sah aus wie ein tiefes Verstehen und Liebhaben.
author: Hermann Hesse
source_work: Heumond (1905), in: Diesseits. Erzählungen, S. Fischer 1907
notes: Renders the source loosely: Faithfully shortened: the original (Projekt Gutenberg 47818) reads "denn ihr Lächeln war von der echten, schönen, gottgeschenkten Art", and the rest matches word for word.

quote: Nur das Denken, das wir leben, hat einen Wert.
author: Hermann Hesse
source_work: Demian (1919), Drittes Kapitel "Der Schächer", Demian zu Sinclair
notes: Verified: Attested word for word in the text (Project Gutenberg 41907).

quote: Es ist gut, alles selber zu kosten, was man zu wissen nötig hat.
author: Hermann Hesse
notes: Verified: Attested word for word (Project Gutenberg 2499); in the original it is set as a thought: "Es ist gut, dachte er, alles selber zu kosten ...".

quote: Wissen kann man mitteilen, Weisheit aber nicht. Man kann sie finden, man kann sie leben, man kann von ihr getragen werden, man kann mit ihr Wunder tun, aber sagen und lehren kann man sie nicht.
author: Hermann Hesse
notes: Verified: The wording matches the text of the novel exactly (Project Gutenberg 2499).

quote: Tu den Schritt und wirf einmal alles weg, so wirst du plötzlich die Welt wieder mit hundert schönen Dingen auf dich warten sehen.
author: Hermann Hesse
source_work: Roßhalde (1914), 6. Kapitel, Otto Burkhardt zu Veraguth
notes: Verified: Attested word for word (Project Gutenberg 64466); the Wikipedia synopsis paraphrases it wrongly as "hundert schönen Farben".

quote: Es ist so gut, das zu wissen: daß in uns drinnen einer ist, der alles weiß, alles will, alles besser macht als wir selber.
author: Hermann Hesse
source_work: Demian (1919), Viertes Kapitel "Beatrice", Demian zu Sinclair
notes: Verified: Attested word for word in the text (Project Gutenberg 41907).

quote: Mochte es mir gehen, wie es wollte, ich war selig, diese Frau in der Welt zu wissen, ihre Stimme zu trinken und ihre Nähe zu atmen.
author: Hermann Hesse
notes: Verified: Attested word for word in the text (Project Gutenberg 41907).

quote: Das Ausgelachtwerden riskiert ein jeder, der sich einem Mädchen nähert; das ist der Einsatz. Also riskiere, und im schlimmsten Fall laß dich eben auslachen.
author: Hermann Hesse
source_work: Der Steppenwolf (1927), Hermine zu Harry Haller
notes: Renders the source loosely: Faithfully shortened: the original (Project Gutenberg 75802) reads "Also riskiere, Harry, und im schlimmsten Fall laß dich eben auslachen - sonst ist es mit meinem Glauben an deinen Gehorsam vorbei."

quote: Wünsche sollte man sich stets erfüllen. Denn sehen Sie: damit sind sie erledigt. Und was erledigt ist, das plagt uns nicht mehr.
author: Hermann Hesse
notes: Attribution unverified: No work by Hesse called "Jenseits der Mauer" can be traced; the sentence circulates only in unsourced quotation lists.

quote: Träume sind Lichter, die dem Menschen leuchten, sie sind Helligkeit, die ihn umgibt, ohne sie herrscht Finsternis; du weißt also, was kommt, wenn du aufhörst zu träumen, du weißt, woher die Finsternis im Herzen des Menschen kommt.
author: Jón Kalman Stefánsson
source_work: Das Herz des Menschen (dt. 2013), Übersetzung von Hjarta mannsins (2011)
notes: Verified: The German sentence is attested verbatim as a quotation from the novel, but it is the German translation and the Icelandic original wording could not be located, so it is left blank.

quote: the universe took its time on you / crafted you to offer the world / something different from everyone else / when you doubt / how you were created / you doubt an energy greater than us both
author: Rupi Kaur
source_work: Rupi Kaur, "irreplaceable", in the sun and her flowers (Andrews McMeel, 2017), the "blooming" chapter
notes: Wording as collected was: The universe took its time on you crafted you precisely so you could offer the world something distinct from everyone else so when you doubt how you were created you doubt an energy greater than us both. Wording corrected against the source: The poem belongs to the sun and her flowers, not milk and honey, and reads "crafted you to offer the world / something different from everyone else" (confirmed against the book text quoted in Germ Magazine's review of the collection); the bank's "crafted you precisely so you could offer the world something distinct" is a rewrite.

quote: Ich werde das Herz nehmen, denn Verstand macht einen nicht glücklich, und Glück ist die beste Sache der Welt.
author: L. Frank Baum
source_work: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), Kapitel 5 "The Rescue of the Tin Woodman", der Blechholzfäller
notes: Spoken by the Tin Man. Verified: A faithful translation of "I shall take the heart; for brains do not make one happy, and happiness is the best thing in the world." (Project Gutenberg 55).

quote: I shall take the heart. For brains do not make one happy, and happiness is the best thing in the world.
author: L. Frank Baum
source_work: L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), ch. 5, "The Rescue of the Tin Woodman"
notes: Spoken by the Tin Man; English version. Verified: Checked against the public-domain 1900 text: the Tin Woodman replies "I shall take the heart; for brains do not make one happy, and happiness is the best thing in the world."

quote: Allen großen Veränderungen geht ein Chaos voraus.
author: Deepak Chopra
source_work: Deepak Chopra, Beitrag des Chopra Center auf Facebook, 8. November 2017
notes: Verified: A line Chopra circulates himself, as "All great changes are preceded by chaos" on deepakchopra.com; the German version renders it faithfully.

quote: With courage you will dare to take risks, have the strength to be compassionate, and the wisdom to be humble. Courage is the foundation of integrity.
author: Keshavan Nair
notes: Attribution unverified: Not found in the excerpt digests of Nair's A Higher Standard of Leadership (Berrett-Koehler, 1994) at getAbstract and Capital Ideas Online, which quote the book's treatment of moral courage at length; the sentence appears only on aggregators.

quote: Regardless of how you feel inside, always try to look like a winner. Even if you are behind, a sustained look of control and confidence can give you a mental edge that results in victory.
author: Arthur Ashe
source_work: Arthur Ashe, quoted in the Ashe estate's "In His Words" Black History Month calendar (arthurashe.org, February 2009), entry for 16 February
notes: Verified: The official estate site carries the sentence word for word, including the second half about a sustained look of control and confidence giving a mental edge.

quote: Auch aus Steinen, die einem in den Weg gelegt werden, kann man Schönes bauen.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
notes: Attribution unverified: Zitatforschung (Krieghofer) lists this as a Kuckuckszitat: it was first put into Goethe's mouth in the Bundestag in 1986, and probably grew out of a 1974 aphorism by Robert Lembke.

quote: Für die Welt bist du irgendjemand, aber für mich bist du die Welt.
notes: Attributed to Unknown in source. Collected with a second variant of the saying run onto the end of it ("aber für irgendjemand bist du die Welt"); that variant is held as its own entry, so the trailing copy was removed here. Attribution unverified: A German version of the anonymous English saying "To the world you may be one person, but to one person you may be the world", which is credited without evidence to Dr. Seuss, Bill Wilson and Goethe.

quote: Was ich habe, will ich nicht verlieren, aber wo ich bin, will ich nicht bleiben, aber die ich liebe, will ich nicht verlassen, aber die ich kenne, will ich nicht mehr sehen, aber wo ich lebe, da will ich nicht sterben, aber wo ich sterbe, da will ich nicht hin: Bleiben will ich, wo ich nie gewesen bin.
author: Thomas Brasch
source_work: Lied, in: Kargo. 32. Versuch auf einem untergehenden Schiff aus der eigenen Haut zu kommen (1977)
notes: Verified: The wording matches the poem as documented at planetlyrik exactly; set as verse in the original and as prose in the bank.

quote: Act as if what you do makes a difference. It does.
author: William James
source_work: William James, correspondence with Helen Keller, 1908; The Correspondence of William James, Vol. 12: April 1908-August 1910 (University of Virginia Press, 2004), p. 135
notes: Verified: Wikiquote's sourced section cites the scholarly Virginia edition of James's correspondence with a page reference, so this is not the unsourced modern coinage it is often taken for.

quote: Our doubts are traitors and make us lose the good we often might win, by fearing to attempt.
author: William Shakespeare
source_work: William Shakespeare, Measure for Measure (c. 1604), Act I, Scene iv
notes: Previously attributed to Jane Addams. Reattributed: The lines are Lucio's in Measure for Measure - "Our doubts are traitors, / And make us lose the good we oft might win / By fearing to attempt" - so the attribution to Jane Addams is wrong; the bank also modernises "oft" to "often".

quote: I believe that a simple and unassuming manner of life is best for everyone, best both for the body and the mind.
author: Albert Einstein
source_work: Wie ich die Welt sehe, in: Mein Weltbild (1934)
notes: Verified: Found in a parallel German-English edition of the 1930/1934 essay Wie ich die Welt sehe, where the stored English is the standard translation with the sentence order rearranged.

quote: Be happy while you are living, for you are a long time dead.
notes: Scottish proverb. Attribution unverified: Wiktionary documents the shorter English phrase "you're a long time dead" with printed citations from Sean O'Casey onward, but this fuller "Scottish proverb" form appears only in modern quotation collections with no printed source behind it.

quote: How about I allow the world to live as it chooses, and I allow me to live as I choose.
author: Richard Bach
source_work: Richard Bach, Illusions: The Adventures of a Reluctant Messiah (Delacorte, 1977)
notes: Wording as collected was: Allow the world to live as it chooses, and allow yourself to live as you choose. Wording corrected against the source: In the text of Illusions the narrator offers this as a description of his own practice; the bank converts a first-person resolution into a general command to the reader.

quote: People seldom notice old clothes if you wear a big smile.
author: Lee Mildon
notes: Attribution unverified: No trace of Lee Mildon beyond quotation aggregators; no book, article or periodical carrying this sentence could be found.

quote: Imagination is everything. It is the preview of life's coming attractions.
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Attribution unverified: No source exists in Einstein's writings; Quote Investigator and Zitatforschung show it as a late embellishment of the sourced 1929 Viereck line Imagination is more important than knowledge.

quote: Only when we are no longer afraid do we begin to live.
author: Dorothy Thompson
source_work: Dorothy Thompson, The Courage to Be Happy (Houghton Mifflin, 1957)
notes: Renders the source loosely: Wikiquote's sourced section assigns the line to the 1957 book, where the full sentence runs "Only when we are no longer afraid do we begin to live in every experience, painful or joyous, to live in gratitude for every moment, to live abundantly"; the bank keeps only the opening clause.

quote: Love vanquishes time. To lovers, a moment can be eternity, eternity can be the tick of a clock.
author: Mary Parrish
notes: Attribution unverified: Attributed to a "Mary Parrish" on aggregator sites only; no book, story or article by any writer of that name carrying the sentence could be located.

quote: Bloom where you are planted.
notes: Attributed to Unknown in source. Attribution unverified: A modern motto popularised in the 1970s and 1980s and often credited to Francis de Sales, though it is absent from his writings; no earlier printed source of any kind could be found.

quote: Through the darkness of future past, / the magician longs to see, / one chants out between two worlds: / Fire, walk with me.
author: MIKE
source_work: Twin Peaks, Episode 2, "Zen, or the Skill to Catch a Killer" (ABC, 19 April 1990), written by Mark Frost and David Lynch; MIKE's verse in Cooper's dream
notes: Verse; line breaks rendered with ' / '. Wording as collected was: Fire walk with me / Through the darkness of future past / The magician longs to see. / One chants out between two worlds / Fire walk with me. Wording corrected against the source: Episode transcripts give four lines beginning "Through the darkness of future past"; the bank prepends an extra opening "Fire walk with me" line that the One-Armed Man never speaks.

quote: Prediction is very difficult, especially if it is about the future.
source_work: Danish saying of unknown authorship, current in Denmark by the mid-twentieth century; quoted by Karl Kristian Steincke in his memoirs Farvel og Tak (1948)
notes: Danish proverb; earliest record in K.K. Steincke's memoirs (1948); popularly attributed to Niels Bohr or Storm P. (Robert Storm Petersen). Verified: Quote Investigator traces the saying to Danish sources and finds no support for the common Niels Bohr attribution, so the bank's "Unknown" is the correct attribution.

quote: The best answer to anger is silence.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Attribution unverified: Absent from the Long, Hays and Hammond translations of the Meditations, his only work; it circulates only on modern quotation sites.

quote: The more we value things outside our control, the less control we have.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Attribution unverified: Found in none of the four complete Meditations translations searched, and unsourced on Wikiquote; a modern Stoicism-blog formulation.

quote: How ridiculous and how strange to be surprised at anything which happens in life.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Verified: Long renders this sentence almost verbatim; Greek from the Perseus text of the Meditations.

quote: You have power over your mind - not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Attribution unverified: Wikiquote states it is from no known translation of the Meditations and traces it to a 2006 self-help book. Also collected as: You have power over your mind - not outside events. Realise this, and you will find strength. The same pseudo-Marcus line twice, differing only in Realize against Realise.

quote: The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Verified: Hammond translates this chapter word for word as given; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Accept the things to which fate binds you, and love the people with whom fate brings you together, but do so with all your heart.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Verified: This is Gregory Hays’s translation of 6.39; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Confine yourself to the present.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Verified: Long has "Confine thyself to the present" in this chapter; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: When you arise in the morning, think of what a precious privilege it is to be alive - to breathe, to think, to enjoy, to love.
author: Elbert Hubbard
notes: Previously attributed to Marcus Aurelius. Reattributed: Wikiquote traces the wording to Hubbard’s magazine The Fra; nothing resembling it occurs in the Meditations.

quote: You can commit injustice by doing nothing.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Verified: Hays: "And you can also commit injustice by doing nothing"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Verified: A circulating form of Hays’s 10.16 ("stop talking about what the good man is like, and just be one"); Greek from Perseus.

quote: Each day provides its own gifts.
author: Martial
source_work: Martial, Epigrams, in W. C. A. Ker’s 1920 Loeb translation
notes: Previously attributed to Marcus Aurelius. Reattributed: The English wording is Ker’s Loeb Martial; Latinists at Textkit confirmed the phrase is nowhere in the Meditations.

quote: Give yourself a gift, the present moment.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Verified: Hays: "Give yourself a gift: the present moment"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: The only wealth which you will keep forever is the wealth you have given away.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Attribution unverified: Absent from all four Meditations translations searched; the underlying sentiment is Mark Antony’s in Plutarch, but this wording has no ancient source.

quote: Have I been made for this, to lie under the blankets and keep myself warm?
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Verified: Long’s text reads "to lie in the bedclothes and keep myself warm"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Conceal a flaw, and the world will imagine the worst.
author: Martial
notes: Previously attributed to Marcus Aurelius. Reattributed: A smoothed English version of Martial 3.42, whose Latin reads Quod tegitur magnum creditur esse malum; Latin left out of ORIG_TEXT as it is not Greek.

quote: Life is neither good or evil, but only a place for good and evil.
author: Seneca the Younger
notes: Previously attributed to Marcus Aurelius. Reattributed: Verified in the Latin Library text of Epistle 99, Vita nec bonum nec malum est boni ac mali locus est; Latin omitted from ORIG_TEXT as it is not Greek.

quote: I cannot escape death, but at least I can escape the fear of it.
author: Epictetus
notes: Previously attributed to Marcus Aurelius. Reattributed: Long’s Discourses 1.27 has "I cannot escape from death. Shall I not escape from the fear of death?"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: How trivial the things we want so passionately are.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Verified: Exactly Hays’s wording in the Fabius Catullinus chapter; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Settle on the type of person you want to be and stick to it, whether alone or in company.
author: Epictetus
notes: Previously attributed to Marcus Aurelius. Reattributed: This is Robert Dobbin’s Penguin rendering of Enchiridion 33; Greek from the Perseus text of the Enchiridion.

quote: Consider at what price you sell your integrity, but please, for God's sake, don't sell it cheap.
author: Epictetus
notes: Previously attributed to Marcus Aurelius. Reattributed: Long: "consider at what price you sell your own will ... sell it not for a small sum"; no comparable passage in the Meditations.

quote: Die Welt, wie wir sie geschaffen haben, ist ein Prozess unseres Denkens. Sie kann nicht verändert werden, ohne unser Denken zu verändern.
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Attribution unverified: Not in Einstein's writings and not in Calaprice, The Ultimate Quotable Einstein; the earliest trace is a 1970 formulation of Ram Dass's that was later put into Einstein's mouth.

quote: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: Gummere's exact published wording; Latin confirmed in the Latin Library and Tesserae text of Ep. 13.4.

quote: Ignorance is the cause of fear.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: Genuine clause per Latin Wikisource and Dickinson College Commentaries, but the popular Latin "Timendi causa est nescire" is a modern rearrangement.

quote: While we wait for life, life passes.
author: Seneca
notes: Renders the source loosely: Looser rendering of the same sentence as Q0201 in the Latin Library and Tesserae texts, where "differtur" means postponed rather than awaited.

quote: Life is long, if you know how to use it.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: The Latin Library text of De Brevitate Vitae 2.1 matches this rendering word for word.

quote: Hurry up and live.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: Renders "propera... vivere" in the Tesserae text of Ep. 101.10; compare "protinus vive" at De Brevitate Vitae 9.1.

quote: Cease to hope and you will cease to fear.
author: Hecato of Rhodes
source_work: quoted in Seneca, Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium 5.7
notes: Previously attributed to Seneca. Reattributed: Seneca expressly credits Hecato ("apud Hecatonem nostrum inveni"), the same ground on which Wikiquote lists "Si vis amari, ama" as misattributed.

quote: Wealth is the slave of a wise man and the master of a fool.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: The Latin Library text of De Vita Beata 26.1 is the source of this standard English rendering.

quote: Only time can heal what reason cannot.
author: Seneca
notes: Renders the source loosely: The Latin Library text says delay "often" heals rather than "only" time, and the line belongs to the Nurse in the tragedy.

quote: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: Gummere's published wording as given on Wikiquote for Letter I; the Latin Library prints the sentence at the head of 1.3.

quote: Life, if well lived, is long enough.
author: Seneca
notes: Renders the source loosely: Condensation of the Latin Library text, whose condition is that life be well invested rather than well lived.

quote: Hang on to your youthful enthusiasms, you will be able to use them better when you are older.
author: Seneca
notes: Attribution unverified: No source in Seneca's corpus and quote-verification sites such as PastWisdom flag it as unverified, with the phrasing being modern self-help English.

quote: He who is brave is free.
author: Seneca
notes: Renders the source loosely: Truncates "sine timore est" (free from fear) in a Stoic syllogism Seneca reports, per the Latin Library and IntraText texts of Ep. 85.24.

quote: It is a rough road that leads to the heights of greatness.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: The Tesserae text of Ep. 84.13 has this exact Latin, matching Wikiquote's translation.

quote: It is more civilized to make fun of life than to bewail it.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: The Latin Library text of De Tranquillitate Animi 15.2 matches this rendering closely.

quote: Difficulty comes from our lack of confidence.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: Confirmed in the Tesserae and Latin Library texts of Ep. 104.26, which Gummere renders just as here.

quote: Life is very short and anxious for those who forget the past, neglect the present, and fear the future.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: Basore's Loeb rendering of the Latin Library text of De Brevitate Vitae 16.1.

quote: What really ruins our character is the fact that none of us looks back over his life.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: The Tesserae and Latin Library texts of Ep. 83.2 carry this sentence verbatim.

quote: Religion is regarded by the common people as true, by the wise as false, and by rulers as useful.
author: Edward Gibbon
source_work: The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, Vol. I, Ch. 2
notes: Previously attributed to Seneca. Reattributed: Wikiquote's Disputed section finds no such passage anywhere in Seneca and traces the line to Gibbon's sentence on the various modes of worship.

quote: It does not matter how many books you have, but how good are the books which you have.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: The Tesserae text of Ep. 45.1 shows the subject really is Lucilius's shortage of books.

quote: When a person spends all his time in foreign travel, he ends by having many acquaintances, but no friends.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: Gummere's wording, with the Latin confirmed in the Tesserae and Latin Library texts of Ep. 2.2.

quote: For many men, the acquisition of wealth does not end their troubles, it only changes them.
author: Epicurus
source_work: quoted in Seneca, Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium 17.11
notes: Previously attributed to Seneca. Reattributed: Seneca introduces it with "ab Epicuro mutuum sumam" in the Latin Library text, so the Latin is his rendering of Epicurus.

quote: The greatest remedy for anger is delay.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: Confirmed in the Latin Library text of De Ira 2.29.1, where the same maxim recurs as "maximum remedium irae dilatio est" at 3.12.4.

quote: Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.
author: Seneca
notes: Widely attributed to Seneca; not traced to his surviving works. Attribution unverified: Wikiquote's Disputed section finds no Senecan source, records a 1912 unattributed version in The Youth's Companion, and dates the Seneca attribution to 1990s quote books.

quote: We have two ears and one mouth so that we can listen twice as much as we speak.
author: Zeno of Citium
notes: Previously attributed to Epictetus. Reattributed: Diogenes Laertius credits the two-ears saying to Zeno rebuking a chattering youth, not to Epictetus; Greek from Perseus.

quote: No man is free who is not master of himself.
author: Epictetus
notes: Verified: English is Crossley’s Golden Sayings XV; Greek is Fragment 35 in Schenkl, though Oldfather groups it among the doubtful fragments.

quote: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the view which they take of them.
author: Epictetus
notes: Verified: The opening sentence of Enchiridion 5; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: It is difficulties that show what men are.
author: Epictetus
notes: Verified: The standard translation of the chapter’s opening sentence; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens.
author: Epictetus
notes: Verified: Elizabeth Carter’s rendering; Long has "make the best use that we can of the things which are in our power".

quote: A ship should not ride on a single anchor, nor life on a single hope.
author: Epictetus
notes: Verified: English is Crossley’s Golden Sayings XVI; Greek is Fragment 30 in Schenkl, classed by Oldfather among the doubtful fragments.

quote: No great thing is created suddenly.
author: Epictetus
notes: Verified: The grape-and-fig passage in Arrian’s Discourses; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Know, first, who you are, and then adorn yourself accordingly.
author: Epictetus
notes: Verified: Word for word the standard translation of 3.1.24; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: It is the nature of the wise to resist pleasures, but the foolish to be a slave to them.
author: Epictetus
source_work: Epictetus, Fragments in George Long’s edition
notes: Attribution unverified: Long prints this among the unnumbered late-florilegia fragments that Schenkl’s critical collection excludes, so its authenticity cannot be settled.

quote: First learn the meaning of what you say, and then speak.
author: Epictetus
notes: Attribution unverified: Quotation sites cite the 1807 Works of Epictetus, but I could not find it in the Discourses, Enchiridion or Fragments in Long’s or Schenkl’s texts.

quote: If you want something good, get it yourself.
author: Epictetus
notes: Verified: Long: "If you would have any thing good, receive it from yourself"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: All the good are friends of one another.
author: Zeno
notes: Zeno of Citium. Verified: Wikiquote sources this Zeno testimonium to Clement; I could not obtain the Greek of that passage, so ORIG_TEXT is left empty.

quote: No loss should be more regrettable to us than losing our time, for it's irretrievable.
author: Zeno
notes: Zeno of Citium. Attribution unverified: Diogenes Laertius 7.23 has Zeno say we need nothing so much as time, but this wording about irretrievable loss is untraceable to any ancient source.

quote: Extravagance is its own destroyer.
author: Zeno
notes: Zeno of Citium. Attribution unverified: Appears only in modern compilations; nothing corresponding in Diogenes Laertius book 7 or in Wikiquote’s sourced Zeno list.

quote: Man conquers the world by conquering himself.
author: Zeno
notes: Zeno of Citium. Attribution unverified: Wikiquote traces it to a 2015 tweet and suggests it garbles Plato, Laws 626e; no ancient source exists.

quote: Steel your sensibilities, so that life shall hurt you as little as possible.
author: Zeno
notes: Zeno of Citium. Attribution unverified: Found only in modern quotation compilations, with no trace in Diogenes Laertius, Stobaeus or the Stoic fragment collections.

quote: Better to trip with the feet than with the tongue.
author: Zeno
notes: Zeno of Citium. Verified: Hicks’s Loeb wording exactly, though Diogenes Laertius adds that some credit the saying to Socrates; Greek from Perseus.

quote: A bad feeling is a commotion of the mind repugnant to reason, and against nature.
author: Zeno
notes: Zeno of Citium. Verified: The older English rendering of Zeno’s definition of passion, which Cicero also reports at Tusculans 4.6; Greek from Perseus.

quote: We begin to lose our hesitation to do immoral things when we lose our hesitation to speak of them.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Verified: Greek from Hense’s 1905 Teubner edition, where the word prattein is Gaisford’s supplement printed in angle brackets.

quote: Humanity must seek what is not simple and obvious using the simple and obvious.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Verified: Lutz: "Man must needs seek to find out that which is not plain nor self-evident through the medium of the plain and obvious"; Greek from Hense.

quote: Since every man dies, it is better to die with distinction than to live long.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Verified: Greek from Hense’s Fragmenta minora; Cynthia King renders it closely as given.

quote: Only by exhibiting actions in harmony with the sound words which he has received will anyone be helped by philosophy.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Verified: The closing sentence of Discourse 1 in Hense; Lutz translates "only in this way will philosophy be of profit to anyone".

quote: Thus whoever destroys human marriage destroys the home, the city - the whole human race.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Verified: Lutz’s translation of Discourse 14 matches almost word for word; Greek from Hense.

quote: He with the most who is content with the least.
author: Diogenes
notes: Attribution unverified: Not in Diogenes Laertius book 6, in Hard’s Sayings and Anecdotes, or in Wikiquote’s sourced list; often given to Socrates instead.

quote: The foundation of every state is the education of its youth.
author: Diogenes
notes: Attribution unverified: Standard in nineteenth-century quotation dictionaries but absent from Diogenes Laertius book 6 and from the Stobaeus material on Wikiquote.

quote: Blushing is the color of virtue.
author: Diogenes
notes: Renders the source loosely: The real anecdote has Diogenes tell a blushing youth "Courage, that is the hue of virtue"; the epigram is a later compression.

quote: Dogs and philosophers do the greatest good and get the fewest rewards.
author: Diogenes
notes: Attribution unverified: No trace in Diogenes Laertius book 6, in Hard’s Sayings and Anecdotes, or in the Stobaeus excerpts collected on Wikiquote.

quote: I am not an Athenian or a Greek, but a citizen of the world.
author: Diogenes
notes: Renders the source loosely: Diogenes’ attested answer is the single word kosmopolites; the longer "not an Athenian or a Greek" form comes from Plutarch’s On Exile, where it is Socrates’.

quote: The mob is the mother of tyrants.
author: Diogenes
notes: Attribution unverified: Diogenes Laertius 6.24 and 6.41 call demagogues the mob’s lackeys, but this exact maxim appears in no ancient source I could locate.

quote: Poverty is a virtue which one can teach oneself.
author: Diogenes
notes: Verified: Wikiquote gives this precise Stobaeus citation; I could not obtain the Greek of the passage, so ORIG_TEXT is left empty.

quote: Ugh, gunpowder in my hourglass / I got some weight on my shoulders, to me it's like feathers
author: Lil Wayne
source_work: Lil Wayne, "Blunt Blowin'", Tha Carter IV (Young Money/Cash Money, 2011), verse 1
notes: Lyrics from Lil Wayne, 'Blunt Blowin'' (Tha Carter IV, 2011); original line reads 'to me it's like feathers'. Wording as collected was: Gunpowder in my hourglass. I've got some weight on my shoulders, to me it's all feathers. Wording corrected against the source: The lyric reads "to me it's like feathers", not "all feathers", confirmed against the transcription of Wayne's handwritten lyric sheet reproduced in his prison memoir Gone 'Til November and quoted by Vice; the two lines also stand eight bars apart in the verse.

quote: Wenn du dich mit dem Teufel einlässt, verändert sich nicht der Teufel - der Teufel verändert dich.
notes: Attributed to Unknown in source. Attribution unverified: No first attestation and no author could be found; the sentence circulates only as an anonymous saying.

quote: Ich spreche normalerweise frei, habe es mir heute aber einmal aufgeschrieben; damit ich hinterher weiß was ich gesagt habe.
notes: Anonymous speaker's quip; no attribution found in German quotation collections or parliamentary records. Attribution unverified: A widespread speaker's joke with no traceable first attestation; the attributions to individual politicians are all unsourced.

quote: Ein Glück das schnell vergeht nennt man Vergnügen.
notes: Attributed to Unknown in source. Attribution unverified: No author and no source could be found; it appears only in anonymous collections of aphorisms.

quote: Good things come to good hearts.
notes: Attributed to Unknown in source. Attribution unverified: Not a recorded proverb: Tilley's dictionary of sixteenth- and seventeenth-century proverbs has "A good heart conquers ill fortune" but nothing matching this phrasing, which appears only in modern inspirational blogs.

quote: Everybody ends up somewhere, I just take my time to get there.
notes: Attributed to Unknown in source. Attribution unverified: No printed, recorded or broadcast source found; the line circulates only as an unattributed social-media caption.

quote: Never forget the one-thousand-year view.
author: Shodo Harada Roshi
