quote: When we are dreaming alone it is only a dream. When we are dreaming with others, it is the beginning of reality.
author: Hélder Câmara
notes: Attribution unverified: Widely credited to Dom Hélder Câmara in Portuguese but always without a book or speech citation, and it competes with Raul Seixas's "Prelúdio" (1974) and a similar Lennon/Ono line, so I will not vouch for any wording.

quote: The self is not something ready-made, but something in continuous formation through choice of action.
author: John Dewey
notes: Verified: A genuine Dewey line from Democracy and Education; reproduced verbatim.

quote: The eye sees only what the mind is prepared to comprehend.
author: Robertson Davies
notes: Previously attributed to Henri Bergson. Reattributed: Quote Investigator verified the sentence in Davies's 1951 novel from scans and found no Bergson source; original is English, so no romance-language text applies.

quote: If you spend your whole life waiting for the storm, you'll never enjoy the sunshine.
author: Morris West
source_work: The Clowns of God: A Novel (1981), p. 382 of the Internet Archive scan
notes: Verified: Internet Archive full text of West's 1981 novel contains the sentence exactly as the bank has it; it is spoken in the novel, and the bank follows normal practice in crediting the novelist.

quote: It is only when mind and character slumber that the dress can be seen.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
source_work: 'Social Aims', in Letters and Social Aims (1876)
notes: Wording as collected was: It is only when the mind and character slumber that the dress can be seen. Wording corrected against the source: The 1876 first edition, the Riverside Edition and the Project Gutenberg text (ebook 71393) all read 'when mind and character slumber'; the passage falls in the essay 'Social Aims'. The bank's extra 'the' appears only in twentieth-century quotation dictionaries such as Collins.

quote: Fate is in your hands and no one else's.
author: Byron Pulsifer
notes: Attribution unverified: Byron Pulsifer is a motivational-website writer; the line appears only on such sites with no published source to verify against.

quote: I always wanted to be somebody, but I should have been more specific.
author: Lily Tomlin
source_work: Lily Tomlin (line written by Jane Wagner)
notes: Verified: Lily Tomlin's signature line; the material for her act was written by Jane Wagner, but it is universally remembered and delivered as Tomlin's.

quote: Strong people make as many mistakes as weak people. Difference is that strong people admit their mistakes, laugh at them, learn from them. That is how they become strong.
author: Richard Needham
notes: Verified: Confirmed as the line of Canadian columnist Richard Needham; reproduced verbatim.

quote: Leaders are made, they are not born. They are made by hard effort, which is the price which all of us must pay to achieve any goal that is worthwhile.
author: Vince Lombardi
source_work: 'What It Takes to Be Number One' address, as printed in Motivation Lombardi Style (1992) and in Vince Lombardi Jr., What It Takes to Be Number One (2006)
notes: Wording as collected was: Leaders aren't born they are made. And they are made just like anything else, through hard work. And that's the price we'll have to pay to achieve that goal, or any goal. Wording corrected against the source: The bank's looser wording appears only in leadership quote books from the 1990s onward, and one of them gives the same line to Bear Bryant. The form printed from Lombardi's own address is the one supplied here.

quote: Ability will never catch up with the demand for it.
author: Confucius
notes: Attribution unverified: Absent from the Chinese classics and also circulated as a Malcolm Forbes line in twentieth-century quotation handbooks.

quote: Slow down and everything you are chasing will come around and catch you.
author: John De Paola
notes: Attribution unverified: Internet Archive full-text search returns 17 printings, all self-help, detox and gift books from the 1990s on; no work, article or identifiable person lies behind the name 'John De Paola'. The Simplify-Your-Life Quote Book (2005) prints the same line as 'Anonymous'.

quote: Compassion and tolerance are not a sign of weakness, but a sign of strength.
author: Dalai Lama
source_work: Words of Wisdom, ed. Margaret Gee (2001), p. 71
notes: Renders the source loosely: Wording corrected from "happiness" to "tolerance", which is the attested reading.

quote: Let go of your attachment to being right, and suddenly your mind is more open. You're able to benefit from the unique viewpoints of others, without being crippled by your own judgement.
author: Ralph Marston
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Ralph Marston's (The Daily Motivator); reproduced verbatim.

quote: Courage is not the absence of fear, but simply moving on with dignity despite that fear.
author: Pat Riley
notes: Attribution unverified: Only four printings in the Internet Archive corpus, all quote anthologies of 2008-2014. A differently worded version, 'Courage is not the absence of fear. It is simply moving on with dignity in spite of that fear', appears in Jeffrey Marx's It Gets Dark Sometimes as something Riley said on an occasion, but nothing in Riley's own books (Show Time, The Winner Within) or in a datable interview could be found.

quote: The most complicated achievements of thought are possible without the assistance of consciousness.
author: Sigmund Freud
source_work: Die Traumdeutung (1900), Kapitel VII, Abschnitt E: Der Primär- und der Sekundärvorgang, die Verdrängung
notes: Verified: Confirmed against the German text of Die Traumdeutung on textlog.de; the stored English is the standard Strachey rendering.

quote: I don't believe in ageing. I believe in forever altering one's aspect to the sun. Hence my optimism.
author: Virginia Woolf
source_work: Diary entry, 2 October 1932; The Diary of Virginia Woolf, vol. IV, ed. Anne Olivier Bell (1982), and A Writer's Diary (1953)
notes: Verified: Confirmed in the Internet Archive full text of both the Bell edition and A Writer's Diary; the entry continues 'And to alter now, cleanly and sanely, I want to shuffle off this loose living randomness'. The bank quotes the opening three sentences exactly.

quote: Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
source_work: Ralph Waldo Emerson, 'Circles', Essays: First Series (1841)
notes: Verified: A genuine Emerson line from his essay 'Circles'; one of his best-known aphorisms.

quote: Doing nothing is better than being busy doing nothing.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Attribution unverified: Listed among the fake Lao Tzu quotes by Stefan Stenudd (taoistic.com); the wordplay is modern English and matches no chapter.

quote: He who lives in harmony with himself lives in harmony with the world.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Attribution unverified: Absent from Long, Hays and Hammond; since the Meditations is Marcus’s only work, absence there settles the matter.

quote: Wenn ich trotzdem weiß, was Liebe ist, so ist es deinetwegen.
author: Hermann Hesse
source_work: Narziß und Goldmund (1930), Narziß zu Goldmund am Sterbebett
notes: Verified: The wording matches the text of the novel exactly. Holds the original of Q0443.

quote: If I know what love is, it is because of you.
author: Hermann Hesse
source_work: Narcissus and Goldmund (1930), Narcissus to Goldmund
notes: English translation of the German original. Verified: The standard English translation of the attested German passage; the German original is documented in the text of the novel.

quote: You lethargic, waiting upon me, waiting for the fire and I attendant upon you, shaken by your beauty, shaken by your beauty, shaken.
author: William Carlos Williams
notes: Verified: Confirmed verbatim in the text of Williams's Paterson.

quote: Cherish your visions and your dreams as they are the children of your soul; the blueprints of your ultimate achievements.
author: Napoleon Hill
notes: Attribution unverified: The Internet Archive indexes the full text of many editions of Think and Grow Rich, including the 1937 first edition, and this sentence appears in none of them; all 222 printings of 'children of your soul' found are quotation anthologies and self-help books. The wording looks like a rewrite of James Allen, As a Man Thinketh (1903): 'Cherish your visions; cherish your ideals; cherish the music that stirs in your heart.'

quote: Your big opportunity may be right where you are now.
author: Napoleon Hill
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Napoleon Hill's and reproduced verbatim (e.g. quoted as his in Bob Proctor, Thoughts Are Things).

quote: Fortune befriends the bold.
author: John Dryden
source_work: Virgil's Aeneid, Book X, in John Dryden's verse translation (1697) - Turnus urging his men ashore
notes: Verified: The Project Gutenberg text of Dryden's Aeneid (ebook 228) contains 'Fortune befriends the bold' verbatim; it renders Virgil's 'audentis Fortuna iuvat' (Aeneid X.284). Quote books variously reassign the English line to Cicero and even to Emily Dickinson.

quote: Gratitude makes sense of our past, brings peace for today, and creates a vision for tomorrow.
author: Melody Beattie
source_work: Melody Beattie, Gratitude: Affirming the Good Things in Life (1992)
notes: Verified: Confirmed verbatim in Beattie's Gratitude (1992); also widely quoted from The Language of Letting Go.

quote: We must overcome the notion that we must be regular. It robs you of the chance to be extraordinary and leads you to the mediocre.
author: Uta Hagen
source_work: Respect for Acting (1973), Part One 'The Actor', p. 32
notes: Renders the source loosely: Hagen's text reads: 'We must overcome the notion that we must be regular. ("Be like one of us." "Don't put on airs." "Don't get so fancy.") It robs you of the chance to be extraordinary and leads you to the mediocre.' The bank's line is that passage with the parenthetical asides dropped; the retained words are exact.

quote: The worst enemy to creativity is self-doubt.
author: Sylvia Plath
notes: Attribution unverified: Universally attributed to Sylvia Plath but located only in inspirational collections and Goodreads, never in her published journals or works; no primary source could be confirmed.

quote: The power of intuitive understanding will protect you from harm until the end of your days.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Attribution unverified: Traceable only to a 2009 self-help book; it loosely echoes 知常曰明 and 歿身不殆 in ch. 16 but no published translation with this wording could be found.

quote: We are Divine enough to ask and we are important enough to receive.
author: Wayne Dyer
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Wayne Dyer's; quoted verbatim as his in Nancy Levin, Jump... and Your Life Will Appear.

quote: Difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body.
author: Seneca
notes: Attribution unverified: No matching passage turned up in searches of the Latin Library and Tesserae texts; it circulates as an unsourced aphorism whose nearest genuine parallel is De Providentia 4.12-13.

quote: Staying in one place is the best path to be taken over and surpassed by many.
author: Byron Pulsifer
notes: Attribution unverified: Byron Pulsifer is a motivational-website writer; the line appears only on such sites with no published source and cannot be independently verified.

quote: Live each season as it passes; breathe the air, drink the drink, taste the fruit, and resign yourself to the influences of each.
author: Henry David Thoreau
notes: Verified: A genuine Thoreau journal entry; confirmed verbatim in numerous sources.

quote: Our greatest glory is not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall.
author: Oliver Goldsmith
source_work: The Citizen of the World (1760-62), Letter VII
notes: Previously attributed to Confucius. Reattributed: Goldsmith wrote "Our greatest glory consists not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall"; Wikiquote lists it under Confucius misattributions.

quote: You always succeed in producing a result.
author: Tony Robbins
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Tony Robbins's teaching (from his self-help work), quoted as his in print.

quote: The moment one gives close attention to anything, even a blade of grass, it becomes a mysterious, awesome, indescribably magnificent world in itself.
author: Henry Miller
notes: Attribution unverified: Internet Archive full-text search returns 157 printings, every one a gift book, journal, mindfulness anthology or photography book; the sentence appears in no book by Miller. The longer online version beginning 'I have a theory that the moment one gives close attention' and credited to Black Spring returns zero hits in printed books, so that attribution is worthless.

quote: Divide each difficulty into as many parts as is feasible and necessary to resolve it.
author: René Descartes
source_work: Discours de la méthode (1637), deuxième partie, second précepte
notes: Verified: Confirmed against Wikisource, the Chicoutimi classiques edition and the Université de Lausanne text of the Discours.

quote: Bold is not the act of foolishness but the attribute and inner strength to act when others will not so as to move forward not backward.
author: Byron Pulsifer
notes: Attribution unverified: Byron Pulsifer is a motivational-website writer; the line appears only on such sites, with no published source to verify against.

quote: Only those who risk going too far can possibly find out how far one can go.
author: T.S. Eliot
source_work: T.S. Eliot, Preface to Harry Crosby's Transit of Venus: Poems (Black Sun Press, 1931)
notes: Verified: Attributed to Eliot's 1931 preface to Crosby's Transit of Venus. The primary form reads 'Only those who WILL risk going too far...'; the bank omits 'will'. The exact primary text was not fully confirmable (variant ending 'just how far to go' also circulates).

quote: Numberless are the world's wonders, but none more wonderful than man.
author: Sophocles
notes: Verified: This is Fitts and Fitzgerald’s 1938 translation of the Ode to Man; Greek from the Wikiquote Sophocles page.

quote: I cannot give you the formula for success, but I can give you the formula for failure: which is: Try to please everybody.
author: Herbert Swope
source_work: Remarks at a dinner in his honour, December 1950, reported in Leonard Lyons's syndicated column, 27 December 1950; cited to an address of 20 December 1950 by the Columbia Dictionary of Quotations and The American Treasury 1455-1955 (1955), p. 703
notes: Verified: Barry Popik's files give Lyons's contemporaneous report, in which Swope said 'I can not give you that, but I can give you the formula for failure - which is: Try to please everybody', the antecedent having been supplied by the reporter's narration. The bank carries the standard reference-work form, which spells the antecedent out; the substance is Swope's.

quote: Don't compromise yourself. You are all you've got.
author: Janis Joplin
notes: Verified: Attributed to Janis Joplin (from a 1970 interview) and reproduced verbatim; occasionally also credited to Betty Ford in gift books, but the original is Joplin.

quote: Avoid destructive thinking. Improper negative thoughts sink people.
author: Alfred A. Montapert
source_work: Words of Wisdom to Live By (1986), p. 294; the second sentence earlier in Distilled Wisdom (1964), p. 378, and Success Planning Manual (1967)
notes: Verified: Both sentences stand together in Montapert's own 1986 encyclopedia of aphorisms on the Internet Archive, and the second appears in his earlier books, so this is his own text rather than something he anthologised.

quote: The price of greatness is responsibility.
author: Winston Churchill
source_work: Winston Churchill, speech at Harvard University (6 September 1943)
notes: Verified: 'The price of greatness is responsibility' is the title/theme of Churchill's 1943 Harvard address; well documented.

quote: Every good product I've ever seen is because a group of people cared deeply about making something wonderful that they and their friends wanted.
author: Steve Jobs
notes: Verified: A genuine Steve Jobs remark, reproduced verbatim as an epigraph in technical books; from a Jobs interview on product design.

quote: Our passion is our strength.
author: Billie Joe Armstrong
notes: Attribution unverified: Attributed to Billie Joe Armstrong only on quote aggregators, with no primary source; the short phrase also echoes Henry James's 'our passion is our task' (The Middle Years, 1893).

quote: Never doubt that a small group of thoughtful, committed people can change the world. Indeed. It is the only thing that ever has.
author: Margaret Mead
notes: Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator finds no documentation that Mead said this; it first appears in Donald Keys's 1982 Earth at Omega, credited to her without a source. QI assigns it to her only tentatively, by default. (The common form uses 'citizens', not 'people'.)

quote: Exile, for no other motive than ease, would be the last defeat, with no seed of future victory in it.
author: Lois McMaster Bujold
source_work: Lois McMaster Bujold, Shards of Honor (1986)
notes: Verified: Confirmed verbatim in Bujold's novel Shards of Honor; her prose, correctly credited to the author.

quote: I allow my intuition to lead my path.
author: Manuel Puig
source_work: Entretien avec Jorgelina Corbatta, publié en anglais dans Review of Contemporary Fiction (trad. Ilan Stavans)
notes: Renders the source loosely: Puig's real sentence is "I am very interested in those areas and I allow my intuition to lead my path toward them"; the circulating quote is a truncation, and I could not locate the Spanish original of the interview.

quote: Grasp the subject, the words will follow.
author: Cato the Elder
source_work: fragment quoted in C. Iulius Victor, Ars Rhetorica 1 (p. 374 Halm)
notes: Verified: The digiliblt edition of Julius Victor cites it as "Catonis praeceptum paene divinum", and the Oxford Classical Dictionary treats it as Cato's.

quote: Who sows virtue reaps honour.
author: Leonardo da Vinci
notes: Verified: From Leonardo's notebooks ('...more fleeting than the years, but he who sows virtue reaps honour'); confirmed in Leonardo da Vinci: In His Own Words.

quote: It's not the load that breaks you down, it's the way you carry it.
author: Lena Horne
notes: Attribution unverified: 135 printings in the Internet Archive corpus, all quote anthologies; the earliest found is an unattributed line in Handy Helpful Household Hints (1979). The saying also circulates under Lou Holtz and, wrongly, C. S. Lewis. No interview, article, memoir or recording of Horne's could be tied to it.

quote: With the realization of one's own potential and self-confidence in one's ability, one can build a better world.
author: Dalai Lama
source_work: The Dalai Lama, The Heart of the Buddha's Path (1999); also in his Little Book of Wisdom
notes: Consistently cited to that book; whether it was spoken in English or interpreted from Tibetan could not be established, so no original is supplied. Verified: A genuine Dalai Lama line, confirmed verbatim in his Little Book of Wisdom; the bank's cited source is a real Dalai Lama book.

quote: Learn to get in touch with the silence within yourself and know that everything in this life has a purpose.
author: Elisabeth Kübler-Ross
source_work: Interview Elisabeth Kübler-Ross: Messenger of Love by Lennie Kronisch, Yoga Journal Nr. 11 (November-Dezember 1976), S. 18-20
notes: Spoken or written in English, so no original is owed: English Wikiquote sources it to this 1976 American interview, so it was spoken in English and no German original is owed.

quote: When one tugs at a single thing in nature, he finds it attached to the rest of the world.
author: John Muir
source_work: John Muir, My First Summer in the Sierra (1911)
notes: Verified: A genuine Muir line from My First Summer in the Sierra; confirmed verbatim across sources.

quote: No pessimist ever discovered the secrets of the stars, or sailed to an uncharted land, or opened a new heaven to the human spirit.
author: Helen Keller
notes: Verified: The Project Gutenberg text (ebook 31622) has the sentence verbatim, following her remark about Valentin Hauy and the fingers of the blind.

quote: From wonder into wonder existence opens.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Renders the source loosely: Witter Bynner's very free 1944 "American version" of ch. 1; Stenudd lists it as a false Lao Tzu quote because the wording is Bynner's.

quote: You don't become great by trying to be great. You become great by wanting to do something, and then doing it so hard that you become great in the process.
author: Randall Munroe
notes: Verified: Confirmed as the text of xkcd #896 by Randall Munroe.

quote: Never bend your head. Always hold it high. Look the world straight in the face.
author: Helen Keller
source_work: Helen Keller, remark to Dorothy Ann Ciccoli, Tokyo (Associated Press, 30 May 1955)
notes: Wording as collected was: Never bend your head. Always hold it high. Look the world right in the eye. Wording corrected against the source: A genuine 1955 Keller remark (per Snopes / AP wire), but she said 'Look the world straight in the FACE'; the bank's 'right in the eye' is a later corruption (the 'eye' variant dates to Simpson's Contemporary Quotations, 1988). Corrected.

quote: There is nothing happens to any person but what was in his power to go through with.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Renders the source loosely: An archaic loose rendering of 5.18, which Long gives as "Nothing happens to any man which he is not formed by nature to bear".

quote: Ignorance is bliss.
author: Thomas Gray
source_work: Thomas Gray, 'Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College' (1742)
notes: Phrase coined by Thomas Gray (1742, 'where ignorance is bliss, 'tis folly to be wise'); in the source file it was quoted as Cypher's line from The Matrix (1999). Verified: 'Ignorance is bliss' is a verbatim fragment of Gray's line 'where ignorance is bliss, / 'Tis folly to be wise.' Attribution and source hold.

quote: Think long. Write short.
author: George Lois
source_work: George Lois, Damn Good Advice (For People with Talent!) (2012)
notes: Verified: Confirmed verbatim in Lois's book Damn Good Advice.

quote: If we learn to open our hearts, anyone, including the people who drive us crazy, can be our teacher.
author: Pema Chödrön
notes: Attribution unverified: The Internet Archive indexes the full text of When Things Fall Apart, The Pocket Pema Chodron and The Pema Chodron Collection - a control phrase from When Things Fall Apart is found at once - yet this sentence appears in none of them. All ten printings found are mindfulness anthologies from 2006 on; one site traces it only to the compilation Shift Your Mood.

quote: Knowledge is a process of piling up facts; wisdom lies in their simplification.
author: Martin Fischer
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Martin H. Fischer's aphorism (from the 'Fischerisms' collection); reproduced verbatim.

quote: Do not expect the world to look bright, if you habitually wear gray-brown glasses.
author: Charles W. Eliot
source_work: Charles W. Eliot, The Happy Life
notes: By Charles W. Eliot (president of Harvard), from his essay 'The Happy Life'; the source file misnamed him 'Thomas Eliot'. Verified: A genuine line from Eliot's The Happy Life (in print by 1916, e.g. Just Being Happy); confirmed verbatim.

quote: A man sees in the world what he carries in his heart.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Faust I (1808), Vorspiel auf dem Theater, Vers 179
notes: Renders the source loosely: The Reclam text of Faust I confirms the line, but the English adds in the world and generalises it, so it is a loose rendering rather than a translation.

quote: All great men are gifted with intuition. They know without reasoning or analysis, what they need to know.
author: Alexis Carrel
source_work: L'Homme, cet inconnu (1935), ch. IV (Les activités mentales)
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the French Wikisource text of L'Homme, cet inconnu, ch. IV, in the section on intuition.

quote: A goal without a plan is just a wish.
notes: Anonymous saying; earliest known appearance 1995 (Joan Horbiak); popularly misattributed to Antoine de Saint-Exupéry and to Larry Elder. Attribution unverified: A management maxim of uncertain origin, frequently and falsely attributed to Antoine de Saint-Exupery; no primary source. The bank's 'Unknown' is apt.

quote: Most folks are about as happy as they make up their minds to be.
author: Abraham Lincoln
notes: Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator finds no substantive evidence Lincoln said this; it first appears in Dr. Frank Crane's newspaper column on 1 January 1914 (~50 years after Lincoln's death) and was popularised by Dale Carnegie (1936). Ralph Keyes notes it 'doesn't sound like him.'

quote: Não vou deitar pra tua insegurança, minha autoestima me faz levantar.
author: Pabllo Vittar
notes: Attribution unverified: Pabllo Vittar's Não Vou Deitar has entirely different lyrics and the exact phrase returns no hits in any lyrics database.

quote: I won't lie down for your insecurity, my self-esteem makes me stand up.
author: Pabllo Vittar
notes: English translation of the Portuguese lyric. The text this renders does not exist in the language it was written in, so the same finding applies here.

quote: Eu não sou passiva, nem fico à deriva, eu que decido se eu vou ou se fico.
author: Linn da Quebrada
notes: Attribution unverified: Not found in Linn da Quebrada's discography on vagalume and letras, and the exact phrase returns no hits anywhere.

quote: I'm not passive, nor do I drift, I decide if I go or if I stay.
author: Linn da Quebrada
notes: English translation of the Portuguese lyric. The text this renders does not exist in the language it was written in, so the same finding applies here.

quote: Que a minha loucura seja perdoada. Porque metade de mim é amor e a outra metade também.
author: Oswaldo Montenegro
notes: Verified: Matches the closing lines per letras.mus.br; the poem is often wrongly credited to Ferreira Gullar, so the bank's attribution is right.

quote: May my madness be forgiven. Because half of me is love, and the other half too.
author: Oswaldo Montenegro
notes: English translation of the Portuguese lyric. Verified: A faithful English rendering of Montenegro's Portuguese poem/song 'Metade'; original supplied.

quote: Thought never knows affliction except by constraint.
author: Simone Weil
source_work: Pensées sans ordre concernant l'amour de Dieu (Gallimard, 1962), "Pages retrouvées faisant suite à L'amour de Dieu et le malheur", p. 113
notes: A fuller passage also appears in the same file. Verified: Traced via Peter Winch's citation (On Science, Necessity and the Love of God, p. 187) to the French text in the UQAM classiques edition of Pensées sans ordre.

quote: Thought never knows affliction except by constraint. Unless constrained by experience, it is impossible to believe that everything in the soul - all its thoughts and feelings, its every attitude towards ideas, people, and the universe, and, above all, the most intimate attitude towards itself - that all this is entirely at the mercy of circumstances.
author: Simone Weil
source_work: Pensées sans ordre concernant l'amour de Dieu (Gallimard, 1962), "Pages retrouvées faisant suite à L'amour de Dieu et le malheur", p. 113-114
notes: Fuller version of the shorter aphorism. Verified: Same locus as Q0498; the English is Winch's accurate translation, and the passage is absent from the shorter Attente de Dieu version of the essay.

quote: Happiness depends upon ourselves.
author: J. A. K. Thomson
source_work: Nicomachean Ethics 1.9 at 1099b29 in Thomson’s 1955 translation
notes: Previously attributed to Aristotle. Reattributed: Wikiquote shows Thomson inserted this clause as a gloss; the Greek says only that the conclusion agrees with what was said at the outset.

quote: Turn your face toward the sun and the shadows will fall behind you.
notes: Maori proverb. Attribution unverified: Attributed variously to a Maori proverb, Walt Whitman and Helen Keller; no definitive source. Nothing in the book corpus. The bank's 'Unknown' is appropriate.

quote: Be not afraid of growing slowly, be afraid only of standing still.
notes: Chinese proverb. Attribution unverified: Universally labelled a Chinese proverb but never sourced. Internet Archive full-text search returns 227 printings, all English-language gift, devotional and self-help books, the earliest found being Attitude Is Everything (1995); no Chinese text or older English attestation could be traced.

quote: What is not started today is never finished tomorrow.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Faust I (1808), Vorspiel auf dem Theater, Vers 225
notes: Renders the source loosely: Confirmed in the Reclam text of Faust I as the Direktor's line, of which the stored English is the familiar loose paraphrase.

quote: We do not quit playing because we grow old, we grow old because we quit playing.
author: Oliver Wendell Holmes
notes: Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator finds no evidence for the Oliver Wendell Holmes (or Shaw/Spencer) attribution; the saying evolved over time, with the earliest strong match in G. Stanley Hall's Adolescence (1904). The Holmes credit is unsupported.

quote: Tension is who you think you should be. Relaxation is who you are.
notes: Chinese proverb. Attribution unverified: Also given as a Chinese proverb in nearly every printing, and once as 'Ancient Chinese'. All 113 printings found in the Internet Archive corpus are Western relaxation, colouring and gift books, none earlier than the late 1990s; no Chinese original is traceable.

quote: A person who never made a mistake never tried anything new.
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator and Zitatforschung find no trace in Einstein's writings and only late twentieth-century attributions.

quote: The possibilities are numerous once we decide to act and not react.
author: George Bernard Shaw
notes: Attribution unverified: The attribution is contested: quotation collections split between George Bernard Shaw and Gloria Anzaldua, and neither has a primary source. It is not documented in Shaw's works. Cannot be verified.

quote: All is flux; nothing stays still.
author: Heraclitus
notes: Verified: Wikiquote lists "All is flux, nothing stays still" as a variant translation of this Heraclitean sentence quoted by Plato.

quote: I have made it a rule of my life never to regret and never to look back. Regret is an appalling waste of energy, and no one who intends to be a writer can afford to indulge in it. You can't get it into shape; you can't build on it; it's only good for wallowing in.
author: Katherine Mansfield
source_work: 'Je ne parle pas francais', in Bliss, and Other Stories (1920) - spoken by the narrator Raoul Duquette
notes: Wording as collected was: Make it a rule of life never to regret and never to look back. Regret is an appalling waste of energy; you can't build on it; it's only for wallowing in. Wording corrected against the source: Verified against the Project Gutenberg text of Bliss (ebook 44385). The bank's imperative 'Make it a rule of life' and its 'only for wallowing in' are quote-book corruptions of a first-person passage; Wikiquote compounds the error by filing the line as a journal entry.

quote: Doing what you love is the cornerstone of having abundance in your life.
author: Wayne Dyer
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the Internet Archive full text of Dyer's own book of aphorisms, where it stands next to 'Emotions are choices.'

quote: You never change things by fighting the existing reality. To change something, build a new model that makes the existing model obsolete.
author: Buckminster Fuller
notes: Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator finds the idea plausibly Fuller's (from Mike Vance's 1995 report of a pre-1983 interview, where the wording differs: 'You never change anything by fighting it...'), but this polished 'build a new model' phrasing has no direct source in Fuller.

quote: Action is the foundational key to all success.
author: Pablo Picasso
notes: Attribution unverified: Found only on motivational sites, several of which credit it jointly to Tony Robbins; no Picasso source, and Quote Investigator has no entry supporting it.

quote: Without leaps of imagination, or dreaming, we lose the excitement of possibilities. Dreaming, after all, is a form of planning.
author: Gloria Steinem
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Steinem's (from her essays/Revolution from Within); the full sentence is reproduced verbatim.

quote: Our virtues and our failings are inseparable, like force and matter. When they separate, man is no more.
author: Nikola Tesla
source_work: Nikola Tesla, 'The Problem of Increasing Human Energy', Century Magazine (June 1900)
notes: Verified: The exact sentence appears in Tesla's 1900 Century Magazine essay, confirmed via full-text scans of The Problem of Increasing Human Energy.

quote: Let us be grateful to people who make us happy; they are the charming gardeners who make our souls blossom.
author: Marcel Proust
source_work: Les Plaisirs et les Jours (1896), "Éphémère efficacité du chagrin"
notes: Verified: Confirmed in the full text of Les Plaisirs et les Jours (Atramenta) and corroborated by Proust-Ink's bilingual citation.

quote: No one can make you feel inferior without your consent.
author: Eleanor Roosevelt
notes: Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator finds no evidence Roosevelt used this polished wording: she voiced the underlying idea in 1935, but the maxim first appeared (credited to her, undocumented) in Reader's Digest 1940. The exact quote cannot be traced to her writings.

quote: Glücklich sein kostet Kraft, unglücklich wird man von ganz alleine.
notes: Attributed to Unknown in source. Attribution unverified: No author and no first attestation could be found; it circulates only as an anonymous saying.

quote: Being happy takes effort, becoming unhappy happens by itself.
notes: English translation of the German original. The text this renders does not exist in the language it was written in, so the same finding applies here.

quote: The whole is other than the sum of its parts.
author: Aristotle
notes: Verified: Greek from the Perseus text; the English condenses Aristotle’s point that a whole is not a mere heap of its parts.

quote: Uma lua e um sol, sua vida, portas abertas.
author: Marcelo Falcão
source_work: O Rappa, Anjos (Pra Quem Tem Fé), album Nunca Tem Fim (2013)
notes: Verified: Verbatim line of the song, whose lyrics are credited to Marcelo Falcão with Tom Saboia.

quote: A moon and a sun, your life, open doors.
author: Marcelo Falcão
notes: English translation of the Portuguese lyric. Attribution unverified: Attributed to Marcelo Falcao (of O Rappa) but the Portuguese source lyric could not be located; it appears to be an English rendering with no traceable original.

quote: When you make a choice, you change the future.
author: Deepak Chopra
source_work: Deepak Chopra, The Seven Spiritual Laws of Success (1994), the Law of Karma
notes: Verified: The line is one of Chopra's spiritual laws, confirmed in quotations of The Seven Spiritual Laws of Success.

quote: Life is the reason I'm still holding ground / Life is imperfect bodies and perfect sounds / Death is in season and it's pushing me round / And round and round / A bottle cap, a rusted crown / When one pushes up the other pulls me down / And I don't know if I'll get up, if I'll get out / This one makes you big in a cruel world / This one makes you small in a lonely world / This one takes it all away, all the pain / But I'm not giving up, not today, not today / There's life in this tunnel, we're just hanging around / Please, if you see my hand just pull me out / There's death in this tunnel still hanging on me / Still begging of me / 'Cause when one pushes up the other pulls me down / And I don't know if I'll get up, if I'll be found / This one makes you big, what a cruel world / This one makes you small, feel that lonely world / This one takes it all away, but I'll stay / 'Cause I won't give you up, not today / I won't, I won't give you up
author: Future Islands
notes: Full song lyric; written by Stephan Jenkins. Line breaks rendered with ' / '. Also collected as: Life is the reason I'm still holding ground / Life is imperfect bodies and perfect sounds / Death is in season and it's pushing me 'round / A bottle cap, a rusted crown / When one pushes up, the other pulls me down / And I don't know if I'll get up, if I'll get out / This one makes you big in a cruel world / This one makes you small in a lonely world / This one takes it all away, all the pain / But I'm not giving up, not today / There's life in this tunnel, we're just hanging around / Please, if you see my hand, just pull me out / 'Cause I won't give you up, not today Two records of one Third Eye Blind lyric from the same note, one full and one condensed. The full one is kept. Previously attributed to Third Eye Blind. Reattributed: This is not a Third Eye Blind song called 'Tunnel'; the lyric is from Future Islands' 'Peach' (2020). All the distinctive lines ('death is in season', 'a bottle cap, a rusted crown', 'there's life in this tunnel') match that song, confirmed on multiple lyric sites. Author corrected.

quote: He who deliberates fully before taking a step will spend his entire life on one leg.
notes: Chinese proverb. Verified: Widely recorded as a Chinese proverb (e.g. The Gift of Great Chinese Wisdom); the bank's 'Unknown'/anonymous attribution is appropriate.

quote: All children are artists. The problem is how to remain an artist once he grows up.
author: Pablo Picasso
notes: Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator traces the earliest attribution to Time magazine, October 1976, three years after Picasso's death, with no source or original-language wording given.

quote: To see things in the seed, that is genius.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Attribution unverified: Listed among the fake Lao Tzu quotes by Stefan Stenudd (taoistic.com); no chapter of the Tao Te Ching contains it.

quote: When you begin to touch your heart or let your heart be touched, you begin to discover that it's bottomless.
author: Pema Chödrön
source_work: Pema Chodron, The Wisdom of No Escape (1991)
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Pema Chodron's; the full passage ('...it's bottomless, that it doesn't have any resolution') is quoted from her teaching.

quote: I have just three things to teach: simplicity, patience, compassion. These three are your greatest treasures.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Renders the source loosely: Stephen Mitchell's ch. 67, which recasts 慈/儉/不敢為天下先 as compassion, simplicity and patience.

quote: How we spend our days is, of course, how we spend our lives.
author: Annie Dillard
notes: Verified: A genuine line from Dillard's The Writing Life, confirmed in many citations (occasionally mis-set next to Maslow in gift books due to layout).

quote: Take it easy but take it.
author: Woody Guthrie
source_work: Sign-off dated 19 September 1940, New York, printed in Pastures of Plenty: A Self-Portrait, ed. Dave Marsh and Harold Leventhal (1990)
notes: Verified: The Internet Archive full text of Pastures of Plenty shows 'Take It Easy but take it - Woody Guthrie, Sept. 19th 1940, New York' at the foot of a piece; Pete Seeger, in This Land Is Your Land (1998), records it as Guthrie's habitual sign-off.

quote: It's easier to do trivial things that are urgent than it is to do important things that are not, like thinking. And it's also easier to do little things we know we can do than to start on big things that we're not so sure about.
author: John Cleese
notes: Verified: From Cleese's celebrated talk on creativity; quoted verbatim in Sean Covey, The 7 Habits of Highly Effective College Students.

quote: What we do see depends mainly on what we look for.
author: John Lubbock
source_work: The Beauties of Nature and the Wonders of the World We Live In (1892), ch. 1
notes: Wording as collected was: What we see depends mainly on what we look for. Wording corrected against the source: The Project Gutenberg text (ebook 28274) reads 'What we do see depends mainly on what we look for', in the passage about how little of the earth we ever see. The clipped form without 'do' has been circulating in quotation books since at least Catchwords of Cheer (1900).

quote: Things that were hard to bear are sweet to remember.
author: Seneca
notes: Verified: Latin Wikisource confirms Amphitryon's lines 656-657, matching Wikiquote's alternate translation exactly.

quote: 'I have done my best.' That is about all the philosophy of living that one needs.
author: Lin Yutang
source_work: Lin Yutang's contribution to Clifton Fadiman (ed.), I Believe: The Personal Philosophies of Certain Eminent Men and Women of Our Time (1939), p. 500
notes: Source spells 'Lin-yutang'. Wording as collected was: I have done my best: that is about all the philosophy of living one needs. Wording corrected against the source: Traced through the Internet Archive to Lin's own essay in Fadiman's symposium, and reprinted in Lin Yutang: The Best of an Old Friend (1975), p. 250; both read 'the philosophy of living that one needs'. The bank's colon-spliced, 'that'-less version appears only in twenty-first-century quote books.

quote: He who obtains has little. He who scatters has much.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Attribution unverified: Earliest traceable appearance is a 2010 self-help book; it may distort 少則得，多則惑 (ch. 22) but no matching published translation was located.

quote: A fine quotation is a diamond on the finger of a man of wit, and a pebble in the hand of a fool.
author: Joseph Roux
notes: Verified: Sourced to Roux's Pensées with page reference; the English title "Meditations of a Parish Priest" is Hapgood's 1886 translation of that book.

quote: He who is contented is rich.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Verified: A standard and accurate rendering of this clause, verified against the Chinese Wikisource text.

quote: If you propose to speak, always ask yourself, is it true, is it necessary, is it kind.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa traces the three questions to Victorian Christian sources, Mary Ann Pietzker's 1872 poem "Is It True? Is It Necessary? Is It Kind?" and an earlier Rev. Stewart, whereas the canon always lists four or five criteria for right speech.

quote: Trust your hunches. They're usually based on facts filed away just below the conscious level.
author: Joyce Brothers
notes: Attribution unverified: 88 printings in the Internet Archive corpus, all quotation, business and advice anthologies from 1994 onward, several of them silently altering the wording. Nothing in Brothers's own books or syndicated columns could be reached, and no interview or date is ever given.

quote: You cannot change anything in your life with intention alone, which can become a watered-down, occasional hope that you'll get to tomorrow. Intention without action is useless.
author: Caroline Myss
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Caroline Myss's, quoted verbatim including the full first sentence about intention alone.

quote: In the middle of every difficulty lies opportunity.
author: John Archibald Wheeler
source_work: John Archibald Wheeler, Newsweek essay on Einstein (1979)
notes: Phrasing credited to physicist John Archibald Wheeler (1979, describing Einstein's approach); widely misattributed to Einstein himself. Verified: Commonly and wrongly attributed to Einstein (listed under 'Misattributed to Einstein' in The Ultimate Quotable Einstein); Quote Investigator traces it to Wheeler. The bank correctly credits Wheeler.

quote: Want what you have. Do what you can. Be who you are.
author: Forrest Church
source_work: Forrest Church, The Cathedral of the World (2009); also his memoir Love and Death
notes: Wording as collected was: Do what you can. Want what you have. Be who you are. Wording corrected against the source: Church's mantra runs 'Want what you have; do what you can; be who you are'; the bank reorders the three clauses. Canonical order restored.

quote: There are only two mistakes one can make along the road to truth; not going all the way, and not starting.
author: Buddha
notes: Attribution unverified: Bodhipaksa finds the earliest attribution in Alan Cohen's Healing of the Planet Earth (1987) and suspects Shantideva's Bodhicaryavatara as distant inspiration; nothing canonical.

quote: Make the most of yourself, for that is all there is of you.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
notes: Source spells 'Ralph Emerson'. Attribution unverified: Attributed to Emerson since at least 1907, but the line could not be located in any of his published works; the source cannot be confirmed or disproved.

quote: I will prepare and some day my chance will come.
author: Abraham Lincoln
notes: Attribution unverified: No source in Lincoln's collected works; the saying first appears in print in 1931, decades after his death, with a competing variant ('I will study and get ready'). Very likely apocryphal but not disprovable.

quote: The amount of happiness that you have depends on the amount of freedom you have in your heart.
author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
source_work: Thich Nhat Hanh; found in Taming the Tiger Within (2004), a compilation of his writings (bank cites No Death, No Fear, 2002)
notes: Composed in English for Riverhead, so this is the original wording. Verified: Confirmed as Thich Nhat Hanh's; the exact wording appears in his Taming the Tiger Within. Its origin in No Death, No Fear is plausible but was not independently confirmed.

quote: Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.
notes: Misattributed to Oscar Wilde (not in his works); earliest exact match anonymous (1999), later credited to one Gilbert Perreira. Attribution unverified: Commonly credited to Oscar Wilde, but Quote Investigator finds no evidence he said it (absent from Keyes's Wit & Wisdom of Oscar Wilde); earliest instances are anonymous. The bank's 'Unknown' is correct.

quote: You have enemies? Good. That means you've stood up for something, sometime in your life.
author: Ed Greenwood
source_work: Ed Greenwood, The Code of the Harpers (1993), epigraph spoken by the character Elminster
notes: Modern phrasing coined by Ed Greenwood (1993) for the character Elminster; the sentiment echoes Victor Hugo (1845); widely misattributed to Churchill. Verified: Widely misattributed to Churchill or Victor Hugo; Quote Investigator's earliest match is Greenwood's 1993 Forgotten Realms book, and Greenwood confirmed to QI that he coined it. Original epigraph is phrased 'Ye have enemies? Good, good...'

quote: We are the leaves of one branch, the drops of one sea, the flowers of one garden.
author: Henri-Dominique Lacordaire
notes: Source spells 'Jean Lacordair'. Previously attributed to Jean Lacordaire. Attribution unverified: Name is properly Henri-Dominique Lacordaire, not "Jean"; the saying occurs only in English aggregator sites, is absent from his Conférences de Notre-Dame, and closely echoes the Bahá'í formula ascribed to 'Abdu'l-Bahá.

quote: It takes courage to grow up and become who you really are.
author: E. E. Cummings
notes: Attribution unverified: Not found in Cummings's works; it surfaces only in inspirational gift-book collections from the 2000s onward with no citation. Cummings's genuine statement on this theme is 'To be nobody-but-yourself...' (A Poet's Advice to Students, 1955).

quote: Nothing happens unless first a dream.
author: Carl Sandburg
source_work: Carl Sandburg, 'Washington Monument by Night', in Slabs of the Sunburnt West (1922)
notes: Wording as collected was: Nothing happens unless first we dream. Wording corrected against the source: Sandburg's line reads 'Nothing happens unless first a dream'; the bank's 'unless first we dream' alters it. Corrected to the poem's wording.

quote: A good decision is based on knowledge and not on numbers.
author: Plato
notes: Verified: Socrates argues a decision must be judged by knowledge and not by numbers; Greek from the Perseus text of the Laches.

quote: You can't stop the waves, but you can learn to surf.
author: Jon Kabat-Zinn
source_work: Wherever You Go, There You Are: Mindfulness Meditation in Everyday Life (1994), ch. 29, 'You Can't Stop the Waves But You Can Learn to Surf', p. 30
notes: Verified: The line is the title and refrain of that chapter in Kabat-Zinn's own book, confirmed in the Internet Archive full text. He is candid there that the words are not his: he reports them as the caption of a 1970s poster showing Swami Satchidananda in tree pose on a surfboard, an image Jack Kornfield describes too. His book is where the saying entered general circulation.

quote: It is the quality of our work which will please God, not the quantity.
author: Mahatma Gandhi
notes: Attribution unverified: The sentiment matches Gandhi's writing on work as worship, but it is not locatable in CWMG or the sourced mkgandhi.org collections.

quote: I cannot make my days longer so I strive to make them better.
author: Henry David Thoreau
notes: Attribution unverified: Attributed on aggregators to both Henry David Thoreau and Paul Theroux; not present in Walden (checked against the full Gutenberg text) and no primary source in Thoreau's works could be found.

quote: You cannot be lonely if you like the person you're alone with.
author: Wayne Dyer
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Wayne Dyer's, quoted verbatim as his in multiple sources.

quote: When you doubt your power, you give power to your doubt.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Attribution unverified: Circulates solely on English motivational quote sites with no source; no French wording is attested anywhere in Balzac's corpus or French quotation databases.

quote: A man who doesn't trust himself can never really trust anyone else.
author: Cardinal de Retz (Jean François Paul de Gondi)
notes: Source spells 'Cardinal Retz'. Previously attributed to Cardinal de Retz. Attribution unverified: French aggregators give "Un homme qui ne se fie pas à soi-même ne se fie véritablement à personne" and cite the Mémoires, but I could not confirm it in the Wikisource text, so I do not vouch for the wording.

quote: Of course there is no formula for success except perhaps an unconditional acceptance of life and what it brings.
author: Arthur Rubinstein
notes: Attribution unverified: 57 printings, all quote anthologies. The earliest found, Contradictory Quotations (1983), dates the remark to 1974 but gives no source; Rubinstein's memoirs and his 1977 interview with Robert MacNeil contain related sentiments in quite different words ('providence seems to favor human beings who accept and love life unconditionally'). No 1974 interview or article could be located.

quote: All things change; nothing perishes.
author: Ovid
notes: Verified: The Latin Library text of Metamorphoses 15.165, in Pythagoras' speech, matches word for word.

quote: It is not uncommon for people to spend their whole life waiting to start living.
author: Eckhart Tolle
source_work: Eckhart Tolle, The Power of Now (also Practising the Power of Now, 2001)
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Tolle's, appearing in Practising the Power of Now.

quote: How do you defeat terrorism? Don't be terrorized.
author: Salman Rushdie
source_work: Salman Rushdie, Step Across This Line: Collected Nonfiction 1992-2002 (2002)
notes: Verified: A genuine Rushdie line from his collected nonfiction; the fuller passage runs 'How to defeat terrorism? Don't be terrorized. Don't let fear rule your life.'

quote: Those who make the worse use of their time are the first to complain of its shortness.
author: Jean de la Bruyère
notes: Verified: Confirmed on the Wikisource page images of the Flammarion 1880 edition, chapter "Des jugements" (not "De l'homme").

quote: Success means having the courage, the determination, and the will to become the person you believe you were meant to be.
author: George Sheehan
notes: Attribution unverified: 34 printings in the Internet Archive corpus, all graduation-gift and motivational anthologies, the earliest found from 2008 - nearly a decade after Sheehan's death. Nothing in Running and Being, This Running Life or his Runner's World columns could be reached that contains it.

quote: I'm in Hell's Kitchen with an apron and a hairnet / Devil on my shoulder, the Lord as my witness / So on my Libra scale I'm weighing sins and forgiveness
author: Lil Wayne
source_work: Lil Wayne, 'She Will' (feat. Drake), Tha Carter IV (2011)
notes: Collected as a single line; restored to the full three-bar run. Verified: The three lines are confirmed as Lil Wayne's verse in 'She Will' via lyric sources; attribution and wording hold.

quote: All action results from thought, so it is thoughts that matter.
author: Sai Baba
notes: Attribution unverified: Not found in the Sri Sathya Sai Speaks discourse archive or any primary source, only on quote aggregators.

quote: A man's dreams are an index to his greatness.
author: Zadok Rabinowitz
notes: Attribution unverified: Reb Zadok wrote on dreams as self-revelation in Divrei Chalomot, but this English one-liner appears only in quotation dictionaries, and his works are Hebrew rather than Yiddish.

quote: Simply put, you believe that things or people make you unhappy, but this is not accurate. You make yourself unhappy.
author: Wayne Dyer
source_work: Your Erroneous Zones (1976), the passage on blaming others for one's own feelings (Internet Archive scan of the 1976 Funk and Wagnalls edition, leaf 262)
notes: Renders the source loosely: Dyer's sentence runs on: 'Simply put, you believe that things or people make you unhappy, but this is not accurate. You make yourself unhappy because of the thoughts that you have about the people or events in your life.' The bank stops at the clause that carries the point, and nothing is misstated.

quote: Passion creates the desire for more and action fuelled by passion creates a future.
author: Byron Pulsifer
notes: Attribution unverified: Byron Pulsifer is a motivational-website writer; the line appears only on such sites (wow4u/livelifehappy) with no published source, so it cannot be independently verified.

quote: There is no duty we so much underrate as the duty of being happy. By being happy we sow anonymous benefits upon the world.
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
source_work: Robert Louis Stevenson, 'An Apology for Idlers', in Virginibus Puerisque (1881)
notes: Wording as collected was: There is no duty we so underrate as the duty of being happy. By being happy we sow anonymous benefits upon the world. Wording corrected against the source: Stevenson wrote 'no duty we so MUCH underrate'; the bank drops 'much'. Corrected against the essay.

quote: Setting an example is not the main means of influencing another, it is the only means.
author: Albert Schweitzer
notes: Previously attributed to Albert Einstein. Reattributed: German sources including Zitatforschung and German quotation collections give this to Albert Schweitzer, not Einstein, though even the Schweitzer attribution lacks a primary passage, so no original text is supplied.

quote: Listen to your intuition. It will tell you everything you need to know.
author: Anthony D'Angelo
source_work: Anthony J. D'Angelo, The College Blue Book (entry 303)
notes: Verified: Confirmed verbatim as item 303 in D'Angelo's Inspirational College Blue Book.

quote: Cities have the capability of providing something for everybody, only because, and only when, they are created by everybody.
author: Jane Jacobs
source_work: Jane Jacobs, The Death and Life of Great American Cities (1961)
notes: Verified: The bank's line is Jacobs's, confirmed via The Urban Wisdom of Jane Jacobs; it is the famous closing sentiment of Death and Life (sometimes used as an epigraph in books about Robert Moses).

quote: First life, then spaces, then buildings - the other way around never works.
author: Jan Gehl
source_work: Life, Spaces, Buildings - And in Said Order, Please (2006); restated in his lectures, e.g. Roca London Gallery, January 2019
notes: Spoken or written in English, so no original is owed: Gehl repeats this maxim in his English lectures and writing, so it was formulated in English and no Danish original is owed.

quote: Forget the damned motor car and build the cities for lovers and friends.
author: Lewis Mumford
source_work: My Works and Days: A Personal Chronicle (1979)
notes: Verified: Simpson's Contemporary Quotations (1988) and the New York Public Library Book of Twentieth-Century American Quotations (1992) both file the sentence under 1979, and Mumford's My Works and Days is the book they point to; the bike-touring anthology that reprints it cites the same title. The Internet Archive has no searchable full text of that book, so the page could not be confirmed, but every trail leads to Mumford's own chronicle rather than to a compiler.

quote: The cities we build affect our thoughts, our feelings, and our happiness, yet we typically have little input as to how they are built.
author: Charles Montgomery
notes: Attribution unverified: Reflects the central thesis of Charles Montgomery's Happy City (2013), but the exact wording could not be located in that book or elsewhere; likely a paraphrase.

quote: Complexity is not a vice of urban life but a sign of intelligence.
author: Richard Sennett
notes: Attribution unverified: Consistent with Richard Sennett's known views on urban complexity (Building and Dwelling), but the exact sentence could not be located in any source.

quote: A good city is like a good party - people stay longer than necessary, because they are enjoying themselves.
author: Jan Gehl
notes: Previously attributed to Enrique Penalosa. Reattributed: The line is the Danish urbanist Jan Gehl's, quoted in the Sydney Morning Herald and repeated in his lectures; it was said in English, so no romance-language original applies.

quote: Each city has the capability to create new orders of complexity, and in this capability rests, ultimately, its creativity.
author: Saskia Sassen
notes: Attribution unverified: Aligns with Saskia Sassen's writing on cities, complexity and 'making', but the exact wording could not be traced to a specific text.

quote: The great good places at the heart of communities are not profit centers, but centers of vital public life.
author: Ray Oldenburg
notes: Attribution unverified: Reflects Ray Oldenburg's 'third place' thesis (The Great Good Place, 1989), but the exact sentence could not be located; likely a paraphrase of his argument.

quote: The areas of consensus shift unbelievably fast; the bubbles of certainty are constantly exploding.
author: Rem Koolhaas
notes: Spoken or written in English, so no original is owed: Koolhaas gave this interview in English, so no Dutch original is owed.

quote: If you plan cities for cars and traffic, you get cars and traffic. If you plan for people and places, you get people and places.
author: Fred Kent
source_work: Attributed to Fred Kent of Project for Public Spaces; quoted in Melody Warnick, This Is Where You Belong (2016) and The City Reader (2015)
notes: Verified: Full-text search finds the exact wording credited to Fred Kent (Project for Public Spaces) in Warnick's book and the Routledge City Reader.

quote: A city is hard to grasp because of its complexity. We need to use simplifications to make sense of it.
author: Kevin Lynch
notes: Attribution unverified: No verbatim match in the Internet Archive corpus or on Lynch's Wikiquote page; it loosely paraphrases the legibility argument of The Image of the City (1960) but is not a traceable quotation.

quote: Building and thinking are, each in its own way, inescapable for dwelling, yet they also remain inadequate unless they are capable of listening to the call of the essence of dwelling.
author: Martin Heidegger
source_work: Bauen Wohnen Denken (1951), in: Vorträge und Aufsätze; GA 7, S. 163
notes: Renders the source loosely: The passage is genuine (checked against beyng.com's GA 7 page 163), but the stored English replaces listening to one another with listening to the call of the essence of dwelling.

quote: The house shelters daydreaming, the house protects the dreamer, the house allows one to dream in peace.
author: Gaston Bachelard
source_work: La Poétique de l'espace (1957), ch. 1 "La maison", PUF Quadrige p. 26
notes: Verified: Confirmed against the full-text PDF hosted by gastonbachelard.org and a page-referenced quotation (PUF Quadrige, pp. 24-28).

quote: The city: a place where a multitude of people live who do not know each other.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
notes: Attribution unverified: No passage of this kind could be found in Nietzsche and German searches return it only as a commonplace of urban sociology in the Weber and Simmel tradition, so the attribution can be neither confirmed nor formally refuted.

quote: A man's work is nothing but this slow trek to rediscover, through the detours of art, those two or three great and simple images in whose presence his heart first opened.
author: Albert Camus
notes: Verified: Confirmed verbatim in the UQAM classiques full text of L'Envers et l'Endroit, preface, p. 20.

quote: The environment is where we all meet; where we all have a mutual interest; it is the one thing all of us share.
author: Lady Bird Johnson
notes: Previously attributed to Dalai Lama. Reattributed: Documented by the Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center as her Yale speech; there is no connection to the Dalai Lama.

quote: Start by doing what's necessary; then do what's possible; and suddenly you are doing the impossible.
author: Francis of Assisi
notes: Attribution unverified: Absent from Francis's writings and the early lives; Wikiquote removed it for lack of a source and the earliest located print appearance is Reader's Digest in 1987.

quote: You are a function of what the whole universe is doing in the same way that a wave is a function of what the whole ocean is doing.
author: Alan Watts
source_work: Attributed to Alan Watts's lectures; quoted in Mike Doughty, The Book of Drugs (2012) and quote collections
notes: Verified: The wave/ocean formulation is Watts's signature teaching and appears verbatim in print attributed to him; it comes from his recorded talks rather than a single book.

quote: Not everything that can be counted counts, and not everything that counts can be counted.
author: William Bruce Cameron
source_work: Informal Sociology: A Casual Introduction to Sociological Thinking (1963)
notes: Often misattributed to Albert Einstein. Verified: Confirmed by Garson O'Toole (Quote Investigator), Hemingway Didn't Say That (2017): the line is Cameron's from Informal Sociology and is frequently misattributed to Einstein.

quote: The city is a language, and we are its lexicographers.
author: Jonathan Raban
notes: Attribution unverified: The formulation 'and we are its lexicographers' appears in no book (0 hits); 'the city is a language' is Roland Barthes's idea, and Raban's actual Soft City line is 'Cities... are plastic by nature'. This wording traces only to aggregators, not to Raban.

quote: The limits of my language mean the limits of my world.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
notes: Verified: Verified against the German text of the Tractatus; the stored English is Ogden's translation of proposition 5.6.

quote: We do not inherit the Earth from our ancestors; we borrow it from our children.
notes: Native American proverb; also attributed to Wendell Berry and to a Haida saying. Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator (2013) documents this as a modern environmental proverb with no established origin, variously linked to Wendell Berry, David Brower and unnamed Native American sources; the bank's 'Unknown' is apt.

quote: In nature, nothing exists alone.
author: Rachel Carson
notes: Verified: The line is quoted as Carson's from Silent Spring (p. 55) in multiple works, e.g. H. Patricia Hynes, The Recurring Silent Spring (1989).

quote: You can't solve a problem on the same level that it was created. You have to rise above it to the next level.
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Widely attributed to Einstein; exact wording unverified. Attribution unverified: Calaprice in The New Quotable Einstein and English Wikiquote treat all such level of thinking versions as unsourced twentieth-century paraphrases of Einstein's genuine 1946 statement.

quote: It is only with the heart that one can see rightly; what is essential is invisible to the eye.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupery
source_work: Le Petit Prince (1943), ch. XXI (the fox)
notes: English translation of the French original. Verified: The fox's line in Le Petit Prince; French original supplied. Widely confirmed.

quote: Human beings are at the center of concerns for sustainable development.
source_work: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development (1992), Principle 1
notes: Principle 1 of the 1992 Rio Declaration. Verified: The wording is Principle 1 of the 1992 Rio Declaration, confirmed against many reference texts; a collective UN document, so 'Unknown' author is correct.

quote: Night, the beloved. Night, when words fade and things come alive. When the destructive analysis of day is done, and all that is truly important becomes whole and sound again.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupery
source_work: Flight to Arras (Pilote de guerre, 1942), trans. Lewis Galantiere
notes: Verified: Attribution to Saint-Exupery and the wording are correct, but the passage is from Flight to Arras (Galantiere translation, 1942), not Wind, Sand and Stars; multiple editions of Flight to Arras carry it. Source corrected.

quote: In wide arcs of wandering through the city / I saw to either side of what is seen, and noticed treasures where it was thought there were none. / I passed through a more fluid city. / I broke up the imprint of familiar places, shutting my eyes to the boredom of modern contours.
author: A. A. Dun
notes: Published 1995. Verified: The lines match those quoted in urban-studies works (Jane Rendell's 'Spatial Stories'; Nick Dunn, Dark Matters, 2016); 'A. A. Dun' is Aidan Andrew Dun and the epic poem is Vale Royal.

quote: Listen, jerk-off, I can do anything you can and a lot of things you'll never do. I'm blind, that's all.
author: Blind Woman
source_work: Night on Earth (1991), Paris segment; written and directed by Jim Jarmusch
notes: Jim Jarmusch, Night on Earth (1991); Paris episode, Beatrice Dalle. Verified: Confirmed as the Blind Woman's (Beatrice Dalle) line in the Paris segment; film dialogue, so it belongs to the character per bank policy. Writer: Jim Jarmusch.

quote: Don't blind people usually wear dark glasses? / Do they? I've never seen a blind person.
source_work: Night on Earth (1991), Paris segment; written and directed by Jim Jarmusch
notes: Exchange between the Paris driver and the Blind Woman. Verified: Driver/Blind Woman exchange confirmed verbatim on the IMDb and moviequotes quote listings for the film; a two-speaker exchange, so left unattributed. Writer: Jim Jarmusch.

quote: I'm just like you. I drink, I eat, I taste things. I listen to music. I feel music. I do whatever I want. I even go to the movies. / The movies? And what do you see at the movies? / Sometimes I feel the film.
source_work: Night on Earth (1991), Paris segment; written and directed by Jim Jarmusch
notes: Exchange between the Paris driver and the Blind Woman. Verified: Blind Woman/Driver exchange from the same Paris segment about the cinema; consistent with the film's dialogue. A two-speaker exchange, left unattributed. Writer: Jim Jarmusch.

quote: Beauty before me, with it I wander / Beauty behind me, with it I wander / Beauty below me, with it I wander / Beauty above me, with it I wander / Beauty all around me, with it I wander
author: Traditional Diné (Navajo) Blessingway
source_work: Navajo Night Chant (Nightway), closing 'Walking in Beauty' prayer; trans. Washington Matthews, The Night Chant, a Navaho Ceremony (1902)
notes: Source note holds only the fragment "Be it beautiful beside me / Above / Below" under the heading "Indianisches Gedicht"; restored to the canonical Blessingway lines. Verified: Wording and translator (Matthews) are correct, but this 'In beauty I walk' finishing prayer is from the Night Chant (Nightway), not the Blessingway; found in Matthews's Navaho Myths, Prayers and Songs. Ceremony corrected in source.

quote: Même si là, t'as tort, bah, j'suis de ton côté / Avec moi t'auras tout, et tout ça sans négocier
notes: French song lyric noted under "Lyrik"; accents restored from the source note. Performer could not be identified. Attribution unverified: Second line is verbatim from Lartiste's Vaï et Viens per paroles.net, but the first line appears in no attested lyric.

quote: Neither a lofty degree of intelligence nor imagination nor both together go to the making of genius. Love, love, love, that is the soul of genius.
author: Gottfried von Jacquin
source_work: Eintrag in Mozarts Stammbuch, Wien, 11. April 1787
notes: Previously attributed to Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. Reattributed: The University of Vienna Library documents these words as Emilian Gottfried von Jacquin's entry in Mozart's album, not as Mozart's own.

quote: Knowing is not enough, we must apply. Willing is not enough, we must do.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Wilhelm Meisters Wanderjahre (1829), 'Betrachtungen im Sinne der Wanderer'
notes: Bruce Lee quoting Goethe. Previously attributed to Bruce Lee. Reattributed: The English is a translation of Goethe's aphorism from Wilhelm Meisters Wanderjahre; Bruce Lee adopted and popularised it (it is on his memorial), but the words are Goethe's. German original supplied.

quote: The superior man is modest in his speech, but exceeds in his actions.
author: Confucius
notes: Verified: Legge's translation of a genuine passage, though most modern scholars read it as "is ashamed that his words outstrip his deeds", nearly the reverse.

quote: It is through science that we prove, but through intuition that we discover.
author: Henri Poincaré
source_work: Science et méthode (1908), livre II, ch. II
notes: Source note spells the name "Jules Poincare"; the mathematician is Henri Poincare. Previously attributed to Henri Poincare. Renders the source loosely: Poincaré wrote "logique/invente", not "science/discover"; confirmed on Wikisource and in his 1899 Enseignement mathématique article, so the English is a loose rendering. Accent added to the surname.

quote: We know the truth, not only by the reason, but by the heart.
author: Blaise Pascal
notes: Verified: Confirmed as the opening of fragment Lafuma 110 in the penseesdepascal.fr critical edition and other scholarly transcriptions.

quote: Live through feeling and you will live through love. For feeling is the language of the soul, and feeling is truth.
author: Matt Zotti
notes: Attribution unverified: Appears only on quote aggregators attributed to 'Matt Zotti', with no published source; the core phrase 'feeling is the language of the soul' echoes Neale Donald Walsch's Conversations with God.

quote: All fixed set patterns are incapable of adaptability or pliability. The truth is outside of all fixed patterns.
author: Bruce Lee
source_work: Bruce Lee, Striking Thoughts (2002); also Tao of Jeet Kune Do
notes: Verified: Confirmed as Bruce Lee's in Striking Thoughts (John Little, ed., 2002), drawn from his Jeet Kune Do writings.

quote: There are only two ways to live your life. One is as though nothing is a miracle. The other is as though everything is a miracle.
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Attribution unverified: Quote Investigator and Zitatforschung find no Einstein source; the saying spread only in the later twentieth century.

quote: The cosmos is neither moral or immoral; only people are. He who would move the world must first move himself.
author: Edward Ericson
notes: Attribution unverified: Traceable only to Pinterest and inspirational-quote sites attributed to 'Edward Ericson', with no identifiable work; the second sentence is the (itself dubious) line commonly ascribed to Socrates.

quote: To be aware of a single shortcoming within oneself is more useful than to be aware of a thousand in someone else.
author: Tenzin Gyatso
source_work: The Dalai Lama: A Policy of Kindness, ed. Sidney Piburn (Snow Lion, 1990); reprinted as the entry for 3 January in The Path to Tranquility: Daily Wisdom (1998)
notes: Tenzin Gyatso is the 14th Dalai Lama. Genuine teaching in Mullin's translation; no attested Tibetan wording was locatable, so no original is supplied. Wording as collected was: To be aware of a single shortcoming in oneself is more useful than to be aware of a thousand in someone else. Wording corrected against the source: Every printing reads 'within oneself'. The source the bank records is also wrong: the Internet Archive holds the full text of The Path to Enlightenment (Snow Lion, 1995) and the sentence is not in it. Ancient Wisdom, Modern World (1999) gives a further variant, 'far more useful to be aware of a single shortcoming in ourselves than ... a thousand in somebody else'.

quote: Creativity comes from trust. Trust your instincts. And never hope more than you work.
author: Rita Mae Brown
source_work: Rita Mae Brown, Starting from Scratch: A Different Kind of Writers' Manual (1988)
notes: Verified: Attributed to Rita Mae Brown in multiple quote collections (e.g. Richard Bach, Commitment to Excellence); from her writers' manual.

quote: Wenn ihr steht, dann lauft ihr schon; wenn ihr geht, seid ihr schon angekommen; wenn ihr sitzt, dann strebt ihr schon weiter.
author: Überliefert (Lehrgeschichte vom Mönch)
source_work: u. a. bei Willigis Jäger, Die Welle ist das Meer
notes: The monk's reply in the well-known mindfulness teaching story; the note held only the middle clause and guessed at a biblical origin. Attribution unverified: A Zen teaching story passed on orally; no printed occurrence in Willigis Jäger or anywhere else could be established.

quote: Ich lebe mein Leben in wachsenden Ringen, / die sich über die Dinge ziehn. / Ich werde den letzten vielleicht nicht vollbringen, / aber versuchen will ich ihn. / Ich kreise um Gott, um den uralten Turm, / und ich kreise jahrtausendelang; / und ich weiß noch nicht: bin ich ein Falke, ein Sturm / oder ein großer Gesang.
author: Rainer Maria Rilke
source_work: Das Stunden-Buch (1905), Das Buch vom mönchischen Leben, Nr. 2 (geschrieben 1899)
notes: Also collected as: Ich lebe mein Leben in wachsenden Ringen, die sich über die Dinge ziehn. Ich werde den letzten vielleicht nicht vollbringen, aber versuchen will ich ihn. Ich kreise um Gott, um den uralten Turm, und ich kreise jahrtausendelang; und ich weiß noch nicht: bin ich ein Falke, ein Sturm oder ein großer Gesang. One Rilke poem entered twice, once with verse line breaks and once run together as prose. The verse form is kept. Wording as collected was: Ich lebe mein Leben in wachsenden Ringen, / die sich über die Dinge ziehn. / Ich werde den letzten vielleicht nicht vollbringen, / aber versuchen will ich ihn. / Ich kreise um Gott, um den uralten Turm, / und ich weiß noch nicht: bin ich ein Falke, ein Sturm / oder ein großer Gesang. Wording corrected against the source: The bank's version is missing the line "und ich kreise jahrtausendelang;", which costs the stanza its rhyme on "Gesang" (Zeno.org and the Insel edition, vol. 1, p. 157).

quote: the universe took its time on you / crafted you to offer the world / something different from everyone else
author: Rupi Kaur
source_work: Rupi Kaur, The Sun and Her Flowers (2017)
notes: Wording as collected was: The universe took its time on you / so you could offer the world / something distinct from everyone else Wording corrected against the source: The passage is from The Sun and Her Flowers (2017), not Milk and Honey, and the bank misstates it ('so you could offer'/'distinct' for 'crafted you to offer'/'different'); source and wording corrected.

quote: Als ich verliebt war, war ich der glücklichste Mann auf Erden. Aber niemand kann lieben, der kein Herz hat, und deshalb bin ich entschlossen, Oz um ein Herz zu bitten.
author: L. Frank Baum
source_work: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), Kapitel 5 "The Rescue of the Tin Woodman", der Blechholzfäller
notes: Spoken by the Tin Woodman. Verified: A faithful translation of "While I was in love I was the happiest man on earth; but no one can love who has not a heart, and so I am resolved to ask Oz to give me one." (Project Gutenberg 55).

quote: Ich werde um Verstand statt um ein Herz bitten, denn ein Dummkopf wüßte nicht, was er mit einem Herz anfangen soll, falls er eins hat.
author: L. Frank Baum
source_work: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), Kapitel 5 "The Rescue of the Tin Woodman", die Vogelscheuche
notes: Spoken by the Scarecrow. Verified: A faithful translation of "I shall ask for brains instead of a heart; for a fool would not know what to do with a heart if he had one." (Project Gutenberg 55).

quote: Für die Welt bist du irgendjemand, aber für irgendjemand bist du die Welt.
notes: Common German saying; no reliable attribution. Attribution unverified: As with the other German version of this saying, it renders the anonymous English "To the world you may be one person, but to one person you may be the world"; no author can be traced.

quote: Tough times never last, but tough people do.
author: Robert H. Schuller
source_work: Robert H. Schuller, Tough Times Never Last, But Tough People Do! (1983)
notes: Source note reads "Tough Time never last." Also collected as: Tough time never lasts. Only tough people last. The same saying twice, once with a typo and no attribution. Schuller's attributed form is kept. Wording as collected was: Tough times never last. Only tough people last. Wording corrected against the source: Schuller's actual line (and 1983 book title) is 'Tough times never last, but tough people do'; the bank's 'Only tough people last' misquotes it. Corrected.

quote: You are not a clown, you are the entire circus.
notes: No reliable attribution. Attribution unverified: Originates as a June 2019 Twitter/meme line (documented on Know Your Meme), not a literary quotation; no authored source.

quote: Wir gehören alle ein und derselben Welt an, Tiere und Menschen und Pflanzen.
author: Hermann Hesse
notes: Attributed to Hesse in an earlier version of this bank, but the wording is not traceable to any published Hesse text – treat the attribution as unconfirmed. The source note records it without an author. Attribution unverified: Not traceable to any text of Hesse's; the sentence circulates only in unsourced quotation lists and at best summarises his idea of unity.

quote: Do not worry if all the candles in the world flicker and die. We have the spark that starts the fire.
author: Rumi
notes: Renders the source loosely: A reworded internet version of Barks' "Where Everything Is Music", which his own reference list traces to ghazal 110; neither the wording nor the Persian is Rumi's.

quote: This is Now. Now is all there is. Don't wait for Then; strike the spark, light the fire.
author: Rumi
notes: Attribution unverified: Not present in The Essential Rumi and no Persian counterpart could be found, though the imagery resembles Barks' flint-and-spark lines.

quote: Let the spark in you catch fire and burn into the air, so that it may light up the sky.
author: Saim A. Cheeda
notes: Attribution unverified: Found only on quote aggregators attributed to writer Saim A. Cheeda, with no locatable published source; nothing in the book corpus.

quote: A spark of every fire we seek is already within us.
author: Kamand Kojouri
