notes: Attribution unverified: Appears only on quote-aggregator sites (QuotesLyfe, Goodreads) attributed to Kamand Kojouri; no published source could be located.

quote: The smallest spark can become the greatest light.
author: George E. Miller
notes: Attribution unverified: Traceable only to quote-aggregator sites attributed to 'George E. Miller', with no identifiable work or date; nothing in the book corpus.

quote: A spark can become a flame, a flame a fire.
author: Kathryn Lasky
source_work: Kathryn Lasky, Lone Wolf (Wolves of the Beyond, Book 1, 2010)
notes: Verified: The exact line is confirmed in the text of Lasky's Lone Wolf via full-text search.

quote: He didn't create the spark, he set the fire.
author: Karolyn James
notes: Attribution unverified: Karolyn James is a real romance author with a book 'Stripped', but the line could not be located in the text or any reliable source, only aggregator-style listings.

quote: Every moment contains a spark of eternity.
author: Elie Wiesel
notes: Attribution unverified: Appears only on quote-aggregator sites with no book, essay or interview cited; nothing matching turns up in Wiesel's published works or the 92nd Street Y archive transcripts.

quote: Logic will get you from A to B. Imagination will take you everywhere.
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Widely attributed to Einstein; not found in his writings. Attribution unverified: No source in Einstein's writings according to Quote Investigator and Zitatforschung, which list it among the most common Einstein fakes.

quote: We work as an eco-system, not an ego-system. Our aim is to grow a positive heartprint, not only shrink the negative footprint.
author: Emil Boc
notes: Mayor of Cluj-Napoca. Attribution unverified: Boc's eco-system not ego-system formula is documented from his English-language appearances, but the second sentence about a positive heartprint could not be traced to him at all, so the quotation as stored is unconfirmed.

quote: I have been over into the future, and it works.
author: Lincoln Steffens
source_work: The Autobiography of Lincoln Steffens (1931), p. 799 - his 1919 exchange with Bernard Baruch on returning from the Bullitt mission to Soviet Russia
notes: Said in 1919 after visiting the Soviet Union; often quoted ironically. Wording as collected was: I have seen the future, and it works! Wording corrected against the source: Justin Kaplan's biography of Steffens cites Autobiography p. 799 directly: "'So you've been over into Russia?' said Bernard Baruch, and I answered very literally, 'I have been over into the future, and it works.'" 'I have seen the future' is the popular corruption, current since at least the 1960s.

quote: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.
author: Charles Goodhart
source_work: Goodhart's Law; this popular wording is Marilyn Strathern's restatement (1997)
notes: Known as Goodhart's Law, 1975; this phrasing is Marilyn Strathern's. Verified: Universally known as Goodhart's Law, but this pithy phrasing is Marilyn Strathern's 1997 restatement; Goodhart's own 1975 formulation is more technical. Attribution kept as conventional, with the nuance noted.

quote: If all you have is a hammer, everything looks like a nail.
author: Abraham Maslow
source_work: Abraham Maslow, The Psychology of Science (1966)
notes: Known as Maslow's Hammer, 1966. Renders the source loosely: A faithful condensation of Maslow's line: 'I suppose it is tempting, if the only tool you have is a hammer, to treat everything as if it were a nail.' Kept as collected per policy.

quote: Existence precedes essence.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre
notes: Verified: Confirmed in the standard French text of the 1946 lecture, where the formula is stated and then glossed at length.

quote: You act like a mortal in all that you fear, and an immortal in all that you desire.
author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
source_work: Seneca, On the Shortness of Life (De Brevitate Vitae), 3.4
notes: Verified: The English renders De Brevitate Vitae 3.4; the Latin original is confirmed in editions of Seneca's Opera. Latin supplied.

quote: There is no climate security for the world without a protected Amazon.
author: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
source_work: Discours à la COP27, Charm el-Cheikh, 16 novembre 2022
notes: Said at the COP27 climate summit. Verified: Confirmed in the full transcript of Lula's COP27 speech published by G1 and on lula.com.br; it is from COP27, not the 2023 inaugural address.

quote: We have plenty of matches in our house / we keep them on hand always. / Currently our favourite brand is Ohio Blue Tip, / though we used to prefer Diamond Brand. / That was before we discovered Ohio Blue Tip matches. / They are excellently packaged, sturdy little boxes / with dark and light blue and white labels / with words lettered in the shape of a megaphone, / as if to say even louder to the world, / "here is the most beautiful match in the world, / its one-and-a-half-inch soft pine stem capped / by a grainy dark purple head, so sober and furious / and stubbornly ready to burst into flame, / lighting, perhaps, the cigarette of the woman you love, / for the first time, and it was never really the same / after that. All this will we give you." / That is what you gave me, I / become the cigarette and you the match, or I / the match and you the cigarette, blazing / with kisses that smoulder towards heaven.
author: Ron Padgett
source_work: Ron Padgett, 'Love Poem', in New & Selected Poems (1995); used in the film Paterson (2016)
notes: From Jim Jarmusch's film Paterson (2016). Verified: Padgett's own poem, confirmed in New & Selected Poems; the bank's British spelling ('favourite') differs from the original 'favorite'. Padgett's poem stands as his work per policy.

quote: I'm in the house. / It's nice out: warm / sun on cold snow. / First day of spring / or last of winter. / My legs run up / the stairs and out / the door, my top / half here writing.
author: Ron Padgett
source_work: Ron Padgett, 'Poem', in Collected Poems (2013); used in Paterson (2016)
notes: From Jim Jarmusch's film Paterson (2016). Wording as collected was: I'm in the house. / It's nice out: warm / sun on cold snow. / First day of spring / or last day of winter. / My legs run up / the stairs and out / the door, my top / half here writing. Wording corrected against the source: Padgett's 'Poem' reads 'First day of spring / or last of winter'; the bank inserts a second 'day' ('or last day of winter'). Verse wording corrected against Collected Poems.

quote: When I wake up earlier than you and you / are turned to face me, face / on the pillow and hair spread around, / I take a chance and stare at you, / amazed in love and afraid / that you might open your eyes and have / the daylights scared out of you. / But maybe with the daylights gone / you'd see how much my chest and head / implode for you, their voices trapped / inside like unborn children fearing / they will never see the light of day. / The opening in the wall now dimly glows / its rainy blue and grey. I tie my shoes / and go downstairs to put the coffee on.
author: Ron Padgett
source_work: Ron Padgett, 'Glow', in Collected Poems (2013); used in Paterson (2016)
notes: From Jim Jarmusch's film Paterson (2016). Verified: Padgett's poem 'Glow', confirmed verbatim in Collected Poems; one of the existing poems Jarmusch selected for Paterson.

quote: My little pumpkin, / I like to think about other girls sometimes, / but the truth is / if you ever left me / I'd tear my heart out / and never put it back. / There'll never be anyone like you. / How embarrassing.
author: Ron Padgett
source_work: Ron Padgett, 'Pumpkin', in Collected Poems (2013); used in Paterson (2016)
notes: From Jim Jarmusch's film Paterson (2016). Verified: Padgett's poem 'Pumpkin', confirmed verbatim in Collected Poems (p. 850).

quote: There's an old song / my grandfather used to sing / that has the question, / "or would you rather be a fish?" / In the same song / is the same question / but with a mule and a pig, / but the one I hear sometimes / in my head is the fish one. / Just that one line. / Would you rather be a fish? / As if the rest of the song / didn't have to be there.
author: Ron Padgett
source_work: Ron Padgett, 'The Line', written for the film Paterson (2016)
notes: From Jim Jarmusch's film Paterson (2016). Verified: One of the three poems Padgett wrote for Paterson (per PBS NewsHour); his own work, correctly attributed.

quote: I go through / trillions of molecules / that move aside / to make way for me / while on both sides / trillions more / stay where they are. / The windshield wiper blade / starts to squeak. / The rain has stopped. / I stop. / On the corner / a boy in a yellow raincoat / holding his mother's hand.
author: Ron Padgett
source_work: Ron Padgett, 'The Run', written for the film Paterson (2016)
notes: From Jim Jarmusch's film Paterson (2016). Verified: One of the poems Padgett wrote for Paterson (per PBS NewsHour); his own work, correctly attributed.

quote: Die Erde aus dem Weltraum anzusehen ist ein bisschen, wie wenn ein Kind sich im Spiegel ansieht und sich selbst erkennt.
author: Samantha Harvey
source_work: Dankesrede zur Verleihung des Booker Prize, London, 12. November 2024
notes: German paraphrase of Harvey's acceptance speech, not of the novel Orbital; English original filed alongside. Renders the source loosely: Faithfully shortened: according to AP and ABC, Harvey said "To look at the Earth from space is a bit like a child looking into a mirror and realising for the first time that the person in the mirror is herself."

quote: Western psychotherapy rearranges the furniture in the room, Eastern techniques help you get out of the room.
author: Ram Dass
source_work: Ram Dass, 'Psychotherapy and Meditation: A Forum', Inquiring Mind 5:1 (Summer 1988)
notes: English original of the German line collected in the source note. Verified: Wording confirmed as Ram Dass's, quoted in W. L. Mikulas, The Integrative Helper (2001) and elsewhere; the bank's specific forum citation holds.

quote: To look at the Earth from space is a bit like a child looking into a mirror and realising for the first time that the person in the mirror is herself. What we do to the Earth we do to ourselves.
author: Samantha Harvey
source_work: Samantha Harvey, Booker Prize acceptance speech, 12 November 2024
notes: Verified wording of the remark the source note paraphrased in German. Verified: Confirmed against news coverage of Harvey's 2024 Booker speech for Orbital (e.g. Al Jazeera); the wording matches, allowing for minor transcription of the spoken 'a bit like'.

quote: Choose life. / Choose a job. / Choose a career. / Choose a family. / Choose a fucking big television. / Choose washing machines, cars, compact disc players, and electrical tin openers. / Choose good health, low cholesterol and dental insurance. / Choose fixed-interest mortgage repayments. / Choose a starter home. / Choose your friends. / Choose leisure wear and matching luggage. / Choose a three-piece suite on hire purchase in a range of fucking fabrics. / Choose DIY and wondering who the fuck you are on a Sunday morning. / Choose sitting on that couch watching mind-numbing, spirit-crushing game shows, stuffing fucking junk food into your mouth. / Choose rotting away at the end of it all, pishing your last in a miserable home, nothing more than an embarrassment to the selfish, fucked-up brats you have spawned to replace yourself. / Choose your future. / Choose life.
author: Mark Renton
source_work: Trainspotting (1996); screenplay John Hodge, from Irvine Welsh's novel
notes: Opening monologue; screenplay by John Hodge after the novel by Irvine Welsh. Verified: The 'Choose life' monologue spoken by Mark Renton; screenplay text confirmed against the published Trainspotting screenplay (John Hodge). Character attribution per policy; writer named.

quote: Wo viel Licht ist, ist starker Schatten.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Götz von Berlichingen (1773), Erster Akt, Jagsthausen, Götz
notes: Popular paraphrase runs "Wo viel Licht ist, ist auch viel Schatten"; the text reads "starker Schatten". Verified: The wording matches the text of the play (German Wikiquote, Projekt Gutenberg-DE).

quote: Wer nicht neugierig ist, erfährt nichts.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Der Triumph der Empfindsamkeit (1778, Druck 1787), 5. Akt, Sora
notes: Widely attributed to Goethe; no source in his works has been documented. Verified: Zeno.org gives the sentence word for word as Sora's speech in act 5.

quote: Irrend lernt man.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Brief an August von Goethe, 14. Januar 1814
notes: Verified: Zeno.org and TextGrid attest the sentence word for word at the end of the letter.

quote: Alles Gescheite ist schon gedacht worden, man muss nur versuchen, es noch einmal zu denken.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Maximen und Reflexionen, aus Wilhelm Meisters Wanderjahre, Betrachtungen im Sinne der Wanderer
notes: Verified: The TextGrid edition confirms the wording; only the spelling differs, muß against muss.

quote: Halten Sie immer an der Gegenwart fest. Jeder Zustand, ja jeder Augenblick ist von unendlichem Wert, denn er ist der Repräsentant einer ganzen Ewigkeit.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Johann Peter Eckermann, Gespräche mit Goethe, 3. November 1823
notes: Also cited from Goethe's letter to Carl Friedrich Zelter, 6 June 1825. Wording as collected was: Halte immer an der Gegenwart fest. Jeder Zustand, ja jeder Augenblick ist von unendlichem Wert, denn er ist der Repräsentant einer ganzen Ewigkeit. Wording corrected against the source: Goethe addresses Eckermann formally; the familiar "Halte" is a later reworking (Goethe-Lexicon of Philosophical Concepts, FA 2.12:67-68).

quote: Der Charakter ruht auf der Persönlichkeit, nicht auf den Talenten.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: West-östlicher Divan, Noten und Abhandlungen, "Israel in der Wüste" (1819)
notes: Verified: Zeno.org attests the sentence there word for word; the citation to Maximen und Reflexionen that the bank carried was wrong.

quote: Glücklich allein ist die Seele, die liebt.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Egmont (1788), III. Aufzug, Klärchens Lied "Freudvoll und leidvoll"
notes: Closing line of "Freudvoll und leidvoll", set to music by Beethoven. Verified: The closing line of the song; LiederNet documents the text against the 1788 Leipzig first printing.

quote: Es hört doch jeder nur, was er versteht.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Maximen und Reflexionen, Aus dem Nachlaß, Über Literatur und Leben
notes: Verified: Zeno.org (Berliner Ausgabe, vol. 18, p. 611) attests the sentence word for word.

quote: Lerne alt zu werden mit einem jungen Herzen.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
notes: Popularly attributed to Goethe; no source in his works has been documented. Attribution unverified: Not found in Goethe's digitised works, letters or conversations; even the quotation collections that credit him concede they have no source.

quote: Der Humor ist der Regenschirm der Weisen.
author: Erich Kästner
source_work: Der Humor (Aus der großdeutschen Kunstlehre), in: Die Alpen 17 (1949) und Kurz und bündig (1950)
notes: Renders the source loosely: Faithfully shortened: the line in full reads "Der Humor ist der Regenschirm der Weisen und insofern unsoldatisch."

quote: Lasst euch die Kindheit nicht austreiben!
author: Erich Kästner
notes: Verified: Attested word for word (Kästner, Gesammelte Schriften für Erwachsene, vol. 7); first printed as "Laßt euch die Kindheit nicht austreiben!".

quote: Irrtümer haben ihren Wert; jedoch nur hie und da. / Nicht jeder, der nach Indien fährt, entdeckt Amerika.
author: Erich Kästner
source_work: Der schöpferische Irrtum, in: Kurz und bündig (1950)
notes: Kästner, not Goethe; the source collection reproduced it as "hier und da". Verified: The wording of the four-line epigram matches exactly.

quote: Wege entstehen dadurch, dass man sie geht.
author: Antonio Machado
source_work: Proverbios y cantares XXIX, in: Campos de Castilla (1912)
notes: German rendering of "se hace camino al andar"; commonly misattributed to Kafka or Nietzsche. Renders the source loosely: A condensed German rendering of the line "caminante, no hay camino, se hace camino al andar"; Zitatforschung (Krieghofer) gives Machado as the author and documents the false attributions to Kafka and Nietzsche.

quote: Das Glück ist das Einzige, das sich verdoppelt, wenn man es teilt.
author: Albert Schweitzer
notes: Traditional attribution; no primary source in Schweitzer's published work has been traced. Attribution unverified: Not traceable in Schweitzer's writings; a modern greeting-card variant of the proverb "Geteilte Freude ist doppelte Freude", attached to his name without any citation.

quote: Die höchste Form des Glücks ist ein Leben mit einem gewissen Grad an Verrücktheit.
author: Erasmus von Rotterdam
notes: Attribution unverified: Absent from Wikiquote's Erasmus and In Praise of Folly pages and from the standard English translations of Moriae Encomium, so no passage could be located despite the sentiment fitting the work.

quote: Glücklich ist, wer das, was er liebt, auch wagt, mit Mut zu beschützen.
author: Ovid
notes: Traditional attribution to Ovid. Verified: The Perseus/Alpheios text of Amores 2.5.9 confirms the line, and zitate7 gives this German wording with that Latin.

quote: Glück ist kein Geschenk der Götter, sondern die Frucht innerer Einstellung.
author: Erich Fromm
notes: Attribution unverified: The citation to Die Kunst des Liebens, p. 39 that every quotation site repeats does not hold up: no such statement about happiness and the gods occurs in the text of The Art of Loving.

quote: Fantasie ist eine wunderbare Eigenschaft, aber man muss sie im Zaum halten.
notes: Unattributed in the source collection; no author identified. Attribution unverified: No author and no first attestation could be found; it appears only as an anonymous saying.

quote: Die besten Dinge im Leben sind nicht die, die man für Geld bekommt.
author: Albert Einstein
notes: Popularly attributed to Einstein; not traced to his writings. Attribution unverified: No evidence in Einstein's writings and no entry in Calaprice, The Ultimate Quotable Einstein; a typical Kuckuckszitat out of the saying collections.

quote: C'est un signe de médiocrité que d'être incapable d'enthousiasme.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Attribution unverified: Absent from the complete La Comédie humaine and Théâtre full text; appears only on French quotation aggregators, so unverified.

quote: L'amour n'est pas seulement un sentiment, il est un art aussi.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the Emmanuel de Solis passage of the full text (Gutenberg, La Comédie humaine vol. 14).

quote: L'expérience s'achète par le malheur.
author: Virginie Ancelot
notes: Previously attributed to Honoré de Balzac. Reattributed: Absent from all of La Comédie humaine; the bibliographic survey Dernière gerbe traces it to Virginie Ancelot in 1836.

quote: Le véritable amour ne calcule rien.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in Mme de Mortsauf's death scene in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 7).

quote: L'amour ne connaît pas les distances.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Attribution unverified: Absent from the complete La Comédie humaine and Théâtre full text; found only on aggregator sites, so unverified.

quote: Nous sommes habitués à juger les autres d'après nous, et si nous les absolvons complaisamment de nos défauts, nous les condamnons sévèrement de ne pas avoir nos qualités.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the arrival at Benassis's house in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 13).

quote: Un homme est bien fort quand il s'avoue sa faiblesse.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in Raphaël's account of Foedora in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 14).

quote: Le hasard est le plus grand romancier du monde; pour être fécond, il n'y a qu'à l'étudier.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the Avant-propos (Gutenberg, vol. 1); the original uses a colon where the bank has a semicolon.

quote: Les grands ont toujours tort de plaisanter avec leurs inférieurs. La plaisanterie est un jeu, le jeu suppose l'égalité.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the Butscha and duc scene in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 4).

quote: La résignation est un suicide quotidien.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Renders the source loosely: Lucien's farewell letter to Ève reads "La résignation, mon ange, est un suicide quotidien"; the bank keeps the form without the vocative, which is how the line circulates.

quote: Dans ces grandes crises, le cœur se brise ou se bronze.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Wording as collected was: Dans ses grandes crises, le cœur se brise ou se bronze. Wording corrected against the source: The text reads "ces", not "ses"; verified in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 1 and the standalone edition).

quote: Le temps manque pour tout.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Words occur verbatim in the full text but only as a clause inside a sentence, not as a standalone maxim.

quote: Le génie a cela de beau qu'il ressemble à tout le monde et que personne ne lui ressemble.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim as Mme Graslin's inward reflection in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 13).

quote: L'amour est un trésor de souvenirs.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the embedded tale L'Ambitieux par amour in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 1).

quote: Les gens généreux font de mauvais commerçants.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the David Séchard passage of the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 8).

quote: La gloire est le soleil des morts.
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in Mme Claës's deathbed speech in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 14).

quote: La clef de toutes les sciences est sans contredit le point d'interrogation; nous devons la plupart des grandes découvertes au comment? Et la sagesse dans la vie consiste peut-être à se demander, à tout propos, pourquoi?
author: Honoré de Balzac
notes: Verified: Found verbatim in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 14); only punctuation and capitalisation differ.

quote: L'égoïsme est le poison de l'amitié.
author: Honoré de Balzac
source_work: Illusions perdues, Un grand homme de province à Paris (1839)
notes: Verified: Found verbatim as a clause in Fulgence's rebuke of Lucien in the full text (Gutenberg, vol. 8).

quote: He who has imagination without learning has wings but no feet.
author: Joseph Joubert
source_work: Pensées, essais et maximes (1842), Titre IV
notes: Original: "Celui qui a de l'imagination sans érudition a des ailes et n'a pas de pieds." Verified: Confirmed on Wikisource (Titre IV) and independently traced by Quote Investigator to the 1842 first edition.

quote: There is no excellent beauty that hath not some strangeness in the proportion.
author: Francis Bacon
notes: Verified: A genuine line from Bacon's essay 'Of Beauty', confirmed in many editions.

quote: In order for the light to shine so brightly, the darkness must be present.
notes: Circulated as a Francis Bacon quote, but absent from his works; no author established. Attribution unverified: A modern inspirational line widely (and falsely) attributed to Francis Bacon in gift books; it appears in no work of Bacon's and its true origin is untraceable. The bank's 'Unknown' is correct.

quote: I will never be an old man. To me, old age is always fifteen years older than I am.
author: Bernard Baruch
source_work: The Observer (London), 'Sayings of the Week', 21 August 1955, p. 3 - on his eighty-fifth birthday
notes: Sometimes misattributed to Francis Bacon. Verified: Quote Investigator reproduces the Observer text, 'I will never be an old man. - To me, old age is always fifteen years older than I am. - Mr. Bernard Baruch', reprinted in the paper's 'Sayings of the Year' on 25 December 1955; Newsweek carried it on 29 August 1955. The joke is older than Baruch - a 'ten years' version was credited to John W. Carswell in 1909 and a 'fifteen years' one circulated from a French periodical in 1924 - and he had used it by 1948, but the sentence as the bank has it is his, on the recorded date.

quote: If you correct your mind, the rest of your life will fall into place.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Traditional attribution. Attribution unverified: No chapter corresponds and the idiom "fall into place" is modern English; it appears only in twentieth-century motivational literature.

quote: How do you write a novel? Well, the first thing you do is clean your refrigerator.
notes: Unattributed in the source collection. Attribution unverified: A floating writers' joke that circulates without reliable attribution (sometimes tied loosely to John Braine); no dependable source located.

quote: Khổ thọ và lạc thọ / Như mây trời theo gió / Hơi thở là giây neo / Thuyền về nơi bến cũ
author: Thích Nhất Hạnh
source_work: Present Moment, Wonderful Moment, gatha "Adjusting Posture"
notes: Original of Q0274. Renders gatha 17 of the Vietnamese originals Từng Bước Nở Hoa Sen and Bước Tới Thảnh Thơi.

quote: If we could change ourselves, the tendencies in the world would also change. As a man changes his own nature, so does the attitude of the world change towards him.
author: Mahatma Gandhi
notes: Gandhi's authentic sentence, of which the popular slogan "Be the change you wish to see in the world" is a later loose paraphrase by others.

quote: 故知足不辱，知止不殆，可以長久。
transliteration: gù zhī zú bù rǔ, zhī zhǐ bù dài, kěyǐ chángjiǔ.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Original of Q0289. Stephen Mitchell's free rendering of ch. 44 (Chinese from the Wikisource 匯校版 Laozi), not a translation of any line.

quote: 勝人者有力，自勝者強。
transliteration: shèng rén zhě yǒu lì, zì shèng zhě qiáng.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Original of Q0290. Faithful rendering by Jonathan Star (Tarcher/Penguin, verse 33), matching the Wikisource Chinese text.

quote: 知足者富。強行者有志。
transliteration: zhīzú zhě fù. qiángxíng zhě yǒu zhì.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Original of Q0291. Jonathan Star's verse 33 reorders these two clauses and adds "surely gets something/everything", which is absent from the Chinese.

quote: 功成身退，天之道。
transliteration: gōng chéng shēn tuì, tiān zhī dào.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Original of Q0292. Jonathan Star's verse 9; his added pun "This is the way to Heaven" has no counterpart in the Wikisource Chinese.

quote: 君子求諸己，小人求諸人。
transliteration: jūnzǐ qiú zhū jǐ, xiǎorén qiú zhū rén.
author: Confucius
notes: Original of Q0296. Legge's exact translation of a genuine passage, verified against the Chinese Wikisource text of the Analects.

quote: ای نسخهٔ نامهٔ الهی که توئی / وی آینهٔ جمال شاهی که توئی / بیرون ز تو نیست هرچه در عالم هست / در خود بطلب هر آنچه خواهی که توئی
transliteration: ey noskhe-ye nāme-ye elāhi ke to'i / vey āyene-ye jamāl-e shāhi ke to'i / birun ze to nist harche dar 'ālam hast / dar khod betalab har ānche khāhi ke to'i
author: Majd al-Din Baghdadi
source_work: Quatrain printed as Rumi Rubaiyat no. 1759; ascribed to Majd al-Din Baghdadi in Nuzhat al-Majalis
notes: Original of Q0384. Ganjoor flags this quatrain as attributed to several poets, the earliest anthology naming Majd al-Din Baghdadi, with Baba Afzal Kashani also proposed.

quote: 玄之又玄，眾妙之門。
transliteration: xuán zhī yòu xuán, zhòng miào zhī mén.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Original of Q0479. Witter Bynner's very free 1944 "American version" of ch. 1; Stenudd lists it as a false Lao Tzu quote because the wording is Bynner's.

quote: 我有三寶，持而保之。一曰慈，二曰儉，三曰不敢為天下先。
transliteration: wǒ yǒu sān bǎo, chí ér bǎo zhī. yī yuē cí, èr yuē jiǎn, sān yuē bù gǎn wéi tiānxià xiān.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Original of Q0528. Stephen Mitchell's ch. 67, which recasts 慈/儉/不敢為天下先 as compassion, simplicity and patience.

quote: 知足者富。
transliteration: zhīzú zhě fù.
author: Lao Tzu
notes: Original of Q0540. A standard and accurate rendering of this clause, verified against the Chinese Wikisource text.

quote: 君子恥其言而過其行。
transliteration: jūnzǐ chǐ qí yán ér guò qí xíng.
author: Confucius
notes: Original of Q0612. Legge's translation of a genuine passage, though most modern scholars read it as "is ashamed that his words outstrip his deeds", nearly the reverse.

quote: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā; / Manasā ce paduṭṭhena, bhāsati vā karoti vā; / Tato naṁ dukkhamanveti, cakkaṁva vahato padaṁ. / Manasā ce pasannena, bhāsati vā karoti vā; / Tato naṁ sukhamanveti, chāyāva anapāyinī.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0024. Thomas Byrom's loose rendering of Dhammapada 1-2; fakebuddhaquotes.com treats "with our thoughts we make the world" as a mistranslation of manomayā.

quote: Upadhi dukkhassa mūlanti.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0025. Bodhipaksa (fakebuddhaquotes.com) confirms this as a genuine canonical line, rendered by Bhikkhu Bodhi as "attachment is the root of suffering".

quote: Attadīpā, bhikkhave, viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā.
author: Buddha
source_work: Samyutta Nikaya 22.43 (Attadipa Sutta); parallel at Digha Nikaya 16.2.26
notes: Original of Q0027. Modern loose rendering of the canonical "be your own island, your own refuge"; fakebuddhaquotes.com shows how this passage was Christianised into "do not depend on others" style quotes.

quote: Carañce nādhigaccheyya, seyyaṁ sadisamattano; / Ekacariyaṁ daḷhaṁ kayirā, natthi bāle sahāyatā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0028. Bodhipaksa calls the "walk alone" quotes an interpretive paraphrase rather than a translation of these Dhammapada verses.

quote: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0029. Max Müller's 1881 rendering of Dhammapada 1; the Pali says experiences are preceded by and made by mind, not that we are the result of our thoughts.

quote: Mettañca sabbalokasmi, mānasaṁ bhāvaye aparimāṇaṁ; / Uddhaṁ adho ca tiriyañca, asambādhaṁ averamasapattaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0030. Standard rendering of the Karaniya Metta Sutta verse, Pali per SuttaCentral's Mahāsaṅgīti edition.

quote: Sukhino va khemino hontu, sabbasattā bhavantu sukhitattā.
author: Buddha
source_work: Sutta Nipata 1.8 (Metta Sutta) v. 3 and v. 5
notes: Original of Q0031. Renders sabbasattā bhavantu sukhitattā from the Metta Sutta refrain, verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Udakañhi nayanti nettikā, usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ; / Dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā, attānaṁ damayanti paṇḍitā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0035. Accurate rendering of Dhammapada 80, Pali confirmed on SuttaCentral.

quote: Appamādo amatapadaṁ, pamādo maccuno padaṁ; / Appamattā na mīyanti, ye pamattā yathā matā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0037. Dwight Goddard's deliberately Christianised rendering of Dhammapada 21, per fakebuddhaquotes.com, which turns appamada into "diligence" and adds "short road".

quote: Bāhusaccañca sippañca, vinayo ca susikkhito; / Subhāsitā ca yā vācā, etaṁ maṅgalamuttamaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0038. Faithful rendering of the Mangala Sutta verse on learning, skill, training and good speech, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: Ajjeva kiccamātappaṁ, ko jaññā maraṇaṁ suve; / Na hi no saṅgaraṁ tena, mahāsenena maccunā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0039. Thanissaro's rendering of the Bhaddekaratta verse; Bodhipaksa cites the same line as genuine.

quote: Udabindu yathāpi pokkhare, padume vāri yathā na limpati; / Evaṁ muni nopalimpati, yadidaṁ diṭṭhasutaṁ mutesu vā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0040. Thanissaro's translation of Sn 4.6, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā; / Sacittapariyodapanaṁ, etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0041. Accurate rendering of the famous Ovada Patimokkha verse, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: Dunniggahassa lahuno, yatthakāmanipātino; / Cittassa damatho sādhu, cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0042. Condenses cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ of Dhammapada 35, verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Kayirā ce kayirāthenaṁ, daḷhamenaṁ parakkame; / Sithilo hi paribbājo, bhiyyo ākirate rajaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0044. Eknath Easwaran's rendering of Dhammapada 313, which Bodhipaksa judges close enough to the Pali to count as genuine.

quote: Nāhaṁ, bhikkhave, aññaṁ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi yaṁ evaṁ aguttaṁ mahato anatthāya saṁvattati yathayidaṁ, bhikkhave, cittaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0046. Bodhipaksa calls this a close enough paraphrase of the Anguttara passage on the unguarded mind that it would be unfair to call it fake.

quote: Diso disaṁ yaṁ taṁ kayirā, verī vā pana verinaṁ; / Micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ, pāpiyo naṁ tato kare.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0047. Loose English rendering of Dhammapada 42, whose Pali says a wrongly directed mind harms one more than any enemy could.

quote: Anavassutacittassa, ananvāhatacetaso; / Puññapāpapahīnassa, natthi jāgarato bhayaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0049. Partial and loose rendering of Dhammapada 39, which speaks of a mind unsoaked by desire and of one who is wakeful having no fear.

quote: Viññātasārāni subhāsitāni, sutañca viññātasamādhisāraṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0056. Thanissaro's translation of Sn 2.9 on Access to Insight, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Mātā yathā niyaṁ puttam āyusā ekaputtamanurakkhe; / Evampi sabbabhūtesu, mānasaṁ bhāvaye aparimāṇaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0057. Acharya Buddharakkhita's rendering of the Metta Sutta mother simile, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: Evampi sabbabhūtesu, mānasaṁ bhāvaye aparimāṇaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0058. Renders the Metta Sutta line on unfolding a boundless heart toward all beings, verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Na hi verena verāni, sammantīdha kudācanaṁ; / Averena ca sammanti, esa dhammo sanantano.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0059. Max Müller's translation of Dhammapada 5, which fakebuddhaquotes.com lists among genuine quotes, though "love" renders averena, non-hatred.

quote: Mettā no cetovimutti bhāvitā bhavissati bahulīkatā yānīkatā vatthukatā anuṭṭhitā paricitā susamāraddhā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0060. Bhikkhu Bodhi's translation of SN 20.3, confirmed genuine by fakebuddhaquotes.com and Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Piyavācameva bhāseyya, yā vācā paṭinanditā; / Yaṁ anādāya pāpāni, paresaṁ bhāsate piyaṁ.
author: Vangisa
source_work: Sutta Nipata 3.3 (Subhasita Sutta) v. 454; also Samyutta Nikaya 8.5 and Theragatha 21.1
notes: Original of Q0061. Genuinely canonical but spoken by the monk Vangisa, not the Buddha, as SuttaCentral's text of Sn 3.3 makes clear.

quote: Anūpavādo anūpaghāto, pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro; / Mattaññutā ca bhattasmiṁ, pantañca sayanāsanaṁ; / Adhicitte ca āyogo, etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0064. Thomas Byrom's loose rendering of Dhammapada 185, where "live in your heart" stands for the Pali's remote lodgings and "seek the highest consciousness" for adhicitta.

quote: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā; / Manasā ce paduṭṭhena, bhāsati vā karoti vā; / Tato naṁ dukkhamanveti, cakkaṁva vahato padaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0065. An accurate translation of Dhammapada 1 including the ox-cart simile, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, apassaṁ udayabbayaṁ; / Ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, passato udayabbayaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0066. Faithful rendering of Dhammapada 113, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Nidhīnaṁva pavattāraṁ, yaṁ passe vajjadassinaṁ; / Niggayhavādiṁ medhāviṁ, tādisaṁ paṇḍitaṁ bhaje.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0067. Accurate rendering of Dhammapada 76 on the wise critic as a guide to hidden treasure, Pali per SuttaCentral.

quote: Evamabbhāhato loko, maccunā ca jarāya ca; / Tasmā dhīrā na socanti, viditvā lokapariyāyaṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0070. Close rendering of Sn 3.8 verse 8, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Akkocchi maṁ avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ ahāsi me; / Ye ca taṁ upanayhanti, veraṁ tesaṁ na sammati. / Ye ca taṁ nupanayhanti, veraṁ tesūpasammati.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0072. Modern loose paraphrase matching no standard translation, but structurally the Dhammapada 3-4 teaching that enmity persists only while such thoughts are harboured.

quote: Taṁ nadīhi vijānātha, sobbhesu padaresu ca; / Saṇantā yanti kusobbhā, tuṇhī yanti mahodadhī. / Yadūnakaṁ taṁ saṇati, yaṁ pūraṁ santameva taṁ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0074. Thanissaro's rendering of the Buddha's advice to Nalaka, Pali verified on SuttaCentral.

quote: Natthi rāgasamo aggi, natthi dosasamo gaho; / Natthi mohasamaṁ jālaṁ, natthi taṇhāsamā nadī.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0075. Rendering of Dhammapada 251, where "shark" interprets gaho (a seizer or grasping) and "torrent" renders nadī, river.

quote: Na sīlabbatamattena, bāhusaccena vā pana; / Atha vā samādhilābhena, vivittasayanena vā. / Phusāmi nekkhammasukhaṃ, aputhujjanasevitaṃ; / Bhikkhu vissāsamāpādi, appatto āsavakkhayaṃ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0076. Eknath Easwaran's free rendering of Dhp 271-272, where "extinguish your self-will" stands for appatto āsavakkhayaṃ (not having reached the destruction of the taints); Pali checked against the Mahasangiti edition.

quote: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbe bhāyanti maccuno; / Attānaṃ upamaṃ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0077. Close and complete translation of Dhp 129, verified line by line against the Pali Dhammapada.

quote: Akkodhena jine kodhaṃ, asādhuṃ sādhunā jine; / Jine kadariyaṃ dānena, saccenālikavādinaṃ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0078. Accurate rendering of the first three clauses of Dhp 223; only the fourth (conquer the liar with truth) is dropped.

quote: Yo uppatitaṃ vineti kodhaṃ, visaṭaṃ sappavisaṃva osadhehi; / So bhikkhu jahāti orapāraṃ, urago jiṇṇamivattacaṃ purāṇaṃ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0080. Piyadassi Thera's translation of the opening verse of the Uraga Sutta; Pali confirmed on SuttaCentral and in Anandajoti's edition.

quote: Dhammaṃ care sucaritaṃ, na naṃ duccaritaṃ care; / Dhammacārī sukhaṃ seti, asmiṃ loke paramhi ca.
author: Buddha
source_work: Dhammapada 169 (Lokavagga); the same line closes verse 168
notes: Original of Q0082. Condensation of the verse's second half, loosening dhammacārī ("one who lives by the Dhamma") into "one who acts on truth".

quote: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā; / Manasā ce pasannena, bhāsati vā karoti vā; / Tato naṃ sukhamanveti, chāyāva anapāyinī.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0084. Buddharakkhita's translation of the second half of Dhp 2, verified against the Pali.

quote: Ārogyaparamā lābhā, santuṭṭhiparamaṃ dhanaṃ; / Vissāsaparamā ñāti, nibbānaṃ paramaṃ sukhaṃ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0086. Faithful to Dhp 204 except that the fourth clause (Nibbana the highest happiness) is omitted and vissāsa/ñāti is softened to "faithfulness the best relationship".

quote: Māvamaññetha puññassa, na mantaṃ āgamissati; / Udabindunipātena, udakumbhopi pūrati; / Dhīro pūrati puññassa, thokaṃ thokampi ācinaṃ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0087. Buddharakkhita's translation of Dhp 122 minus its opening line ("Think not lightly of good"), verified against the Pali.

quote: Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccāti, yadā paññāya passati; / Atha nibbindati dukkhe, esa maggo visuddhiyā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0088. Standard translation of Dhp 277, with only the closing "this is the path to purification" left off.

quote: Yaṃ na tumhākaṃ taṃ pajahatha; taṃ vo pahīnaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya bhavissati.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0090. Thanissaro Bhikkhu's translation of the "whatever is not yours" passage of MN 22, verified against the Pali text.

quote: Hatthasaṃyato pādasaṃyato, vācāsaṃyato saṃyatuttamo; / Ajjhattarato samāhito, eko santusito tamāhu bhikkhuṃ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0091. Thomas Byrom's very free rendering of Dhp 362, in which "You are a seeker" stands for tamāhu bhikkhuṃ and "solitude" for eko.

quote: Akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ, ajini maṃ ahāsi me; / Ye ca taṃ nupanayhanti, veraṃ tesūpasammati.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0092. Bodhipaksa traces this to Eknath Easwaran's Words to Live By (1990) and calls it a good paraphrase of Dhp 4, which speaks of stilling hatred rather than finding peace.

quote: Salābhaṃ nātimaññeyya, nāññesaṃ pihayaṃ care; / Aññesaṃ pihayaṃ bhikkhu, samādhiṃ nādhigacchati.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0093. Bodhipaksa rates this "fakeish" because nātimaññeyya means "should not despise" rather than "overrate"; he finds it first in Joseph Gaer's The Wisdom of the Living Religions (1956).

quote: Ekāsanaṃ ekaseyyaṃ, eko caramatandito; / Eko damayamattānaṃ, vanante ramito siyā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0094. Close translation of Dhp 305, verified against the Pali.

quote: Ayoge yuñjamattānaṃ, yogasmiñca ayojayaṃ; / Atthaṃ hitvā piyaggāhī, pihetattānuyoginaṃ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0095. Eknath Easwaran's expansive rendering of Dhp 209, which literally contrasts exerting oneself in the wrong thing with pursuing the goal.

quote: Na tena paṇḍito hoti, yāvatā bahu bhāsati; / Khemī averī abhayo, paṇḍitoti pavuccati.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0096. Accurate translation of Dhp 258, where khemī averī abhayo gives "peaceful, loving, and fearless".

quote: Phuṭṭhassa lokadhammehi, cittaṃ yassa na kampati; / Asokaṃ virajaṃ khemaṃ, etaṃ maṅgalamuttamaṃ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0097. Narada Thera's translation of this Mangala Sutta verse; Pali confirmed on SuttaCentral and in the Aimwell exposition.

quote: Jhāyatha, bhikkhave, mā pamādattha; mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha.
author: Buddha
source_work: Majjhima Nikaya 8 (Sallekha Sutta); same formula at MN 19 and SN 43.1
notes: Original of Q0098. Bodhipaksa's Real Buddha Quotes confirms this as genuine, from the Sallekha Sutta; the Pali stock exhortation is attested at MN 19 and throughout SN 43.

quote: Sahassamapi ce vācā, anatthapadasaṃhitā; / Ekaṃ atthapadaṃ seyyo, yaṃ sutvā upasammati.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0099. Faithful condensation of Dhp 100, "one useful word, hearing which one attains peace".

quote: Uṭṭhahatha nisīdatha, daḷhaṃ sikkhatha santiyā; / Mā vo pamatte viññāya, maccurājā amohayittha vasānuge.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0100. Precisely John D. Ireland's translation of daḷhaṃ sikkhatha santiyā in Snp 2.10, with the Pali as printed by the Vipassana Research Institute.

quote: Saccaṃ bhaṇe na kujjheyya, dajjā appampi yācito; / Etehi tīhi ṭhānehi, gacche devāna santike.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0101. Renders only the middle clause of Dhp 224 (dajjā appampi yācito, "give even a little when asked"), dropping the qualifier "when asked" and the rest of the verse.

quote: Evañce, bhikkhave, sattā jāneyyuṃ dānasaṃvibhāgassa vipākaṃ yathāhaṃ jānāmi, na adatvā bhuñjeyyuṃ, na ca nesaṃ maccheramalaṃ cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭheyya.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0102. Loose rendering of Itivuttaka 26, where the Buddha says beings who knew the fruit of giving as he knows it would not eat without having shared.

quote: Pubbeva dānā sumano, dadaṃ cittaṃ pasādaye; / Datvā attamano hoti, esā yaññassa sampadā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0109. Accurate rendering of the donor's three factors in AN 6.37, verified against SuttaCentral's Pali; only the closing "this is the success of the offering" is omitted.

quote: Mātāpitu upaṭṭhānaṃ, puttadārassa saṅgaho; / Anākulā ca kammantā, etaṃ maṅgalamuttamaṃ.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0110. Narada Thera's translation of this Mangala Sutta verse; Pali confirmed on SuttaCentral and in the Aimwell exposition.

quote: Attānaṃ, bhikkhave, rakkhanto paraṃ rakkhati, paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhati.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0111. Thanissaro Bhikkhu's translation of the conclusion the Buddha draws from the acrobat simile in SN 47.19.

quote: Selo yathā ekaghano, vātena na samīrati; / Evaṃ nindāpasaṃsāsu, na samiñjanti paṇḍitā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0112. Buddharakkhita's translation of Dhp 81, verified against the Pali.

quote: Khantī paramaṃ tapo titikkhā, nibbānaṃ paramaṃ vadanti buddhā.
author: Buddha
source_work: Dhammapada 184 (Buddhavagga); second half cf. a Samyutta Nikaya verse on patience as victory
notes: Original of Q0113. Bodhipaksa rates this "fakeish": The Teaching of Buddha welds Dhp 184 ("enduring patience is the highest austerity") to a Samyutta verse making patient endurance the true victory, whose Pali I did not verify.

quote: Attanā hi kataṃ pāpaṃ, attanā saṃkilissati; / Attanā akataṃ pāpaṃ, attanāva visujjhati; / Suddhī asuddhi paccattaṃ, nāñño aññaṃ visodhaye.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0114. Bodhipaksa traces the wording to Paul Carus's rhymed Karma: A Story of Buddhist Ethics (1894), a very free version of Dhp 165 in which "no one may" was added to fit the rhyme.

quote: Yo sahassaṃ sahassena, saṅgāme mānuse jine; / Ekañca jeyyamattānaṃ, sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0115. Faithful rendering of Dhp 103, verified against the Pali.

quote: Tasmātihānanda, attadīpā viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā. / Handa dāni, bhikkhave, āmantayāmi vo: vayadhammā saṅkhārā, appamādena sampādethā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0116. Conflates two separate passages of DN 16, the "be lamps unto yourselves" exhortation and the Buddha's last words, into a single quotation.

quote: Yogā ve jāyatī bhūri, ayogā bhūrisaṅkhayo; / Etaṃ dvedhāpathaṃ ñatvā, bhavāya vibhavāya ca; / Tathāttānaṃ niveseyya, yathā bhūri pavaḍḍhati.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0119. Substantially faithful to the whole of Dhp 282, with yoga rendered "meditation" as in most published translations.

quote: Tumhehi kiccamātappaṃ, akkhātāro tathāgatā; / Paṭipannā pamokkhanti, jhāyino mārabandhanā.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0120. Exactly Buddharakkhita's translation of the first half of Dhp 276, verified against the Pali.

quote: Ahaṃ nāgova saṅgāme, cāpato patitaṃ saraṃ; / Ativākyaṃ titikkhissaṃ, dussīlo hi bahujjano.
author: Buddha
notes: Original of Q0121. Buddharakkhita's translation of Dhp 320, omitting only the closing "there are many, indeed, who lack virtue".

quote: Bewegung ist alles, die Richtung entscheidet.
author: Manfred Hinrich
notes: Original of Q0003. The German aphorism circulates under Hinrich's name on German quotation sites but no primary publication of his roughly 30000 aphorisms could be located, so the attribution stays unconfirmed.

quote: Von einem gewissen Punkt an gibt es keine Rückkehr mehr. Dieser Punkt ist zu erreichen.
author: Franz Kafka
source_work: Betrachtungen über Sünde, Leid, Hoffnung und den wahren Weg (Zürauer Aphorismen, 1917/18), Nr. 5
notes: Original of Q0130. Verified verbatim as aphorism 5 in the digitised text of Kafka's Zürau aphorisms (digbib.org edition).

quote: Auch glaube ich, daß ein schlichtes und anspruchsloses äußeres Leben für jeden gut ist, für Körper und Geist.
author: Albert Einstein
source_work: Wie ich die Welt sehe, in: Mein Weltbild (1934)
notes: Original of Q0162. Found in a parallel German-English edition of the 1930/1934 essay Wie ich die Welt sehe, where the stored English is the standard translation with the sentence order rearranged.

quote: der Beweis, daß die kompliziertesten Denkleistungen ohne Mittun des Bewußtseins möglich sind
author: Sigmund Freud
source_work: Die Traumdeutung (1900), Kapitel VII, Abschnitt E: Der Primär- und der Sekundärvorgang, die Verdrängung
notes: Original of Q0437. Confirmed against the German text of Die Traumdeutung on textlog.de; the stored English is the standard Strachey rendering.

quote: Ein jeder sieht was er im Herzen trägt.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Faust I (1808), Vorspiel auf dem Theater, Vers 179
notes: Original of Q0488. The Reclam text of Faust I confirms the line, but the English adds in the world and generalises it, so it is a loose rendering rather than a translation.

quote: Was heute nicht geschieht, ist morgen nicht getan
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Faust I (1808), Vorspiel auf dem Theater, Vers 225
notes: Original of Q0503. Confirmed in the Reclam text of Faust I as the Direktor's line, of which the stored English is the familiar loose paraphrase.

quote: Bauen und Denken sind jeweils nach ihrer Art für das Wohnen unumgänglich. Beide sind aber auch unzulänglich für das Wohnen, solange sie abgesondert das Ihre betreiben, statt aufeinander zu hören.
author: Martin Heidegger
source_work: Bauen Wohnen Denken (1951), in: Vorträge und Aufsätze; GA 7, S. 163
notes: Original of Q0588. The passage is genuine (checked against beyng.com's GA 7 page 163), but the stored English replaces listening to one another with listening to the call of the essence of dwelling.

quote: Die Grenzen meiner Sprache bedeuten die Grenzen meiner Welt.
author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
notes: Original of Q0597. Verified against the German text of the Tractatus; the stored English is Ogden's translation of proposition 5.6.

quote: Wahres Genie ohne Herz - ist Unding - denn nicht hoher Verstand allein; nicht Imagination allein; nicht beide zusammen machen Genie - Liebe! Liebe! Liebe! ist die Seele des Genies.
author: Gottfried von Jacquin
source_work: Eintrag in Mozarts Stammbuch, Wien, 11. April 1787
notes: Original of Q0610. The University of Vienna Library documents these words as Emilian Gottfried von Jacquin's entry in Mozart's album, not as Mozart's own.

quote: Plura sunt, Lucili, quae nos terrent quam quae premunt, et saepius opinione quam re laboramus.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0193. Gummere's exact published wording; Latin confirmed in the Latin Library and Tesserae text of Ep. 13.4.

quote: cum timendi sit causa nescire, non est tanti scire, ne timeas?
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0194. Genuine clause per Latin Wikisource and Dickinson College Commentaries, but the popular Latin "Timendi causa est nescire" is a modern rearrangement.

quote: Dum differtur vita transcurrit.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0195. Looser rendering of the same sentence as Q0201 in the Latin Library and Tesserae texts, where "differtur" means postponed rather than awaited.

quote: Vita, si uti scias, longa est.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0196. The Latin Library text of De Brevitate Vitae 2.1 matches this rendering word for word.

quote: Ideo propera, Lucili mi, vivere et singulos dies singulas vitas puta.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0197. Renders "propera... vivere" in the Tesserae text of Ep. 101.10; compare "protinus vive" at De Brevitate Vitae 9.1.

quote: Desines timere, si sperare desieris.
author: Hecato of Rhodes
source_work: quoted in Seneca, Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium 5.7
notes: Original of Q0198. Seneca expressly credits Hecato ("apud Hecatonem nostrum inveni"), the same ground on which Wikiquote lists "Si vis amari, ama" as misattributed.

quote: Divitiae enim apud sapientem virum in servitute sunt, apud stultum in imperio.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0199. The Latin Library text of De Vita Beata 26.1 is the source of this standard English rendering.

quote: quod ratio non quit, saepe sanavit mora.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0200. The Latin Library text says delay "often" heals rather than "only" time, and the line belongs to the Nurse in the tragedy.

quote: Satis longa vita et in maximarum rerum consummationem large data est, si tota bene collocaretur.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0202. Condensation of the Latin Library text, whose condition is that life be well invested rather than well lived.

quote: Qui fortis est sine timore est; qui sine timore est sine tristitia est; qui sine tristitia est beatus est.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0204. Truncates "sine timore est" (free from fear) in a Stoic syllogism Seneca reports, per the Latin Library and IntraText texts of Ep. 85.24.

quote: Confragosa in fastigium dignitatis via est.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0205. The Tesserae text of Ep. 84.13 has this exact Latin, matching Wikiquote's translation.

quote: humanius est deridere vitam quam deplorare.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0206. The Latin Library text of De Tranquillitate Animi 15.2 matches this rendering closely.

quote: Non quia difficilia sunt non audemus, sed quia non audemus difficilia sunt.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0207. Confirmed in the Tesserae and Latin Library texts of Ep. 104.26, which Gummere renders just as here.

quote: Illorum brevissima ac sollicitissima aetas est qui praeteritorum obliviscuntur, praesentia neglegunt, de futuro timent.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0208. Basore's Loeb rendering of the Latin Library text of De Brevitate Vitae 16.1.

quote: Hoc nos pessimos facit, quod nemo vitam suam respicit.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0209. The Tesserae and Latin Library texts of Ep. 83.2 carry this sentence verbatim.

quote: Non refert quam multos sed quam bonos habeas.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0211. The Tesserae text of Ep. 45.1 shows the subject really is Lucilius's shortage of books.

quote: Nusquam est qui ubique est. Vitam in peregrinatione exigentibus hoc evenit, ut multa hospitia habeant, nullas amicitias.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0212. Gummere's wording, with the Latin confirmed in the Tesserae and Latin Library texts of Ep. 2.2.

quote: multis parasse divitias non finis miseriarum fuit sed mutatio
author: Epicurus
source_work: quoted in Seneca, Epistulae Morales ad Lucilium 17.11
notes: Original of Q0213. Seneca introduces it with "ab Epicuro mutuum sumam" in the Latin Library text, so the Latin is his rendering of Epicurus.

quote: Maximum remedium irae mora est.
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0214. Confirmed in the Latin Library text of De Ira 2.29.1, where the same maxim recurs as "maximum remedium irae dilatio est" at 3.12.4.

quote: Rem tene, verba sequentur.
author: Cato the Elder
source_work: fragment quoted in C. Iulius Victor, Ars Rhetorica 1 (p. 374 Halm)
notes: Original of Q0472. The digiliblt edition of Julius Victor cites it as "Catonis praeceptum paene divinum", and the Oxford Classical Dictionary treats it as Cato's.

quote: quae fuit durum pati, / meminisse dulce est
author: Seneca
notes: Original of Q0536. Latin Wikisource confirms Amphitryon's lines 656-657, matching Wikiquote's alternate translation exactly.

quote: omnia mutantur, nihil interit
author: Ovid
notes: Original of Q0563. The Latin Library text of Metamorphoses 15.165, in Pythagoras' speech, matches word for word.

quote: Felix, qui quod amat defendere fortiter audet
author: Ovid
notes: Original of Q0673. The Perseus/Alpheios text of Amores 2.5.9 confirms the line, and zitate7 gives this German wording with that Latin.

quote: Una ciudad avanzada no es en la que los pobres pueden moverse en carro, sino una en la que incluso los ricos utilizan el transporte público.
author: Enrique Peñalosa
source_work: Entretien avec l'agence EFE, publié dans Semana, 13 décembre 2010
notes: Original of Q0007. Spanish Wikiquote sources it to Peñalosa via Semana, and kottke.org documents that the Petro attribution stems from a viral 2012 tweet; the English is itself a loose rendering.

quote: Il est quelquefois sans inconvénient de remettre à plus tard son travail. Mais, s'il s'agit des baobabs, c'est toujours une catastrophe.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Original of Q0022. Located in the baobab passage of ch. 5 in three independent full-text editions including the Gutenberg Australia text.

quote: Tu sais... quand on est tellement triste on aime les couchers de soleil...
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
notes: Original of Q0023. Confirmed verbatim in ch. 6 (the forty-three sunsets passage) across four independent full-text editions.

quote: Mais le génie n'est que l'enfance retrouvée à volonté, l'enfance douée maintenant, pour s'exprimer, d'organes virils et de l'esprit analytique qui lui permet d'ordonner la somme des matériaux involontairement amassée.
author: Charles Baudelaire
source_work: Le Peintre de la vie moderne (1863), III "L'artiste, homme du monde, homme des foules et enfant"
notes: Original of Q0127. The line is Baudelaire's, not Rimbaud's, per the critical text of Le Peintre de la vie moderne (Wuppertal lyriktheorie edition and Wikisource).

quote: Le second, de diviser chacune des difficultés que j'examinerais, en autant de parcelles qu'il se pourrait, et qu'il serait requis pour les mieux résoudre.
author: René Descartes
source_work: Discours de la méthode (1637), deuxième partie, second précepte
notes: Original of Q0459. Confirmed against Wikisource, the Chicoutimi classiques edition and the Université de Lausanne text of the Discours.

quote: Tous les grands hommes sont doués d'intuition. Ils savent sans raisonnement, sans analyse, ce qu'il leur importe de savoir.
author: Alexis Carrel
source_work: L'Homme, cet inconnu (1935), ch. IV (Les activités mentales)
notes: Original of Q0489. Found verbatim in the French Wikisource text of L'Homme, cet inconnu, ch. IV, in the section on intuition.

quote: Car la pensée répugne tellement au malheur qu'elle est aussi incapable de se porter volontairement à le concevoir qu'un animal, sauf exception, est incapable de suicide. Elle ne le connaît que par contrainte.
author: Simone Weil
source_work: Pensées sans ordre concernant l'amour de Dieu (Gallimard, 1962), "Pages retrouvées faisant suite à L'amour de Dieu et le malheur", p. 113
notes: Original of Q0498. Traced via Peter Winch's citation (On Science, Necessity and the Love of God, p. 187) to the French text in the UQAM classiques edition of Pensées sans ordre.

quote: Elle ne le connaît que par contrainte. Il est impossible de croire sans y être contraint par l'expérience que tout ce qu'on a dans l'âme, toutes les pensées, tous les sentiments, toutes les attitudes à l'égard des idées, des hommes et de l'univers, et surtout l'attitude la plus intime de l'être envers lui-même, tout cela est entièrement à la merci des circonstances.
author: Simone Weil
source_work: Pensées sans ordre concernant l'amour de Dieu (Gallimard, 1962), "Pages retrouvées faisant suite à L'amour de Dieu et le malheur", p. 113-114
notes: Original of Q0499. Same locus as Q0498; the English is Winch's accurate translation, and the passage is absent from the shorter Attente de Dieu version of the essay.

quote: Soyons reconnaissants aux personnes qui nous donnent du bonheur, elles sont les charmants jardiniers par qui nos âmes sont fleuries.
author: Marcel Proust
source_work: Les Plaisirs et les Jours (1896), "Éphémère efficacité du chagrin"
notes: Original of Q0515. Confirmed in the full text of Les Plaisirs et les Jours (Atramenta) and corroborated by Proust-Ink's bilingual citation.

quote: Une belle citation est un diamant au doigt de l'homme d'esprit et un caillou dans la main d'un sot.
author: Joseph Roux
notes: Original of Q0539. Sourced to Roux's Pensées with page reference; the English title "Meditations of a Parish Priest" is Hapgood's 1886 translation of that book.

quote: Ceux qui emploient mal leur temps sont les premiers à se plaindre de sa brièveté.
author: Jean de la Bruyère
notes: Original of Q0566. Confirmed on the Wikisource page images of the Flammarion 1880 edition, chapter "Des jugements" (not "De l'homme").

quote: La maison abrite la rêverie, la maison protège le rêveur, la maison nous permet de rêver en paix.
author: Gaston Bachelard
source_work: La Poétique de l'espace (1957), ch. 1 "La maison", PUF Quadrige p. 26
notes: Original of Q0589. Confirmed against the full-text PDF hosted by gastonbachelard.org and a page-referenced quotation (PUF Quadrige, pp. 24-28).

quote: Une œuvre d'homme n'est rien d'autre que ce long cheminement pour retrouver par les détours de l'art les deux ou trois images simples et grandes sur lesquelles le cœur, une première fois, s'est ouvert.
author: Albert Camus
notes: Original of Q0591. Confirmed verbatim in the UQAM classiques full text of L'Envers et l'Endroit, preface, p. 20.

quote: Pour le géomètre pur lui-même, cette faculté est nécessaire, c'est par la logique qu'on démontre, c'est par l'intuition qu'on invente.
author: Henri Poincaré
source_work: Science et méthode (1908), livre II, ch. II
notes: Original of Q0613. Poincaré wrote "logique/invente", not "science/discover"; confirmed on Wikisource and in his 1899 Enseignement mathématique article, so the English is a loose rendering. Accent added to the surname.

quote: Nous connaissons la vérité, non seulement par la raison, mais encore par le cœur.
author: Blaise Pascal
notes: Original of Q0614. Confirmed as the opening of fragment Lafuma 110 in the penseesdepascal.fr critical edition and other scholarly transcriptions.

quote: Il y a au moins un être chez qui l'existence précède l'essence, un être qui existe avant de pouvoir être défini par aucun concept et que cet être c'est l'homme.
author: Jean-Paul Sartre
notes: Original of Q0645. Confirmed in the standard French text of the 1946 lecture, where the formula is stated and then glossed at length.

quote: Não há segurança climática para o mundo sem uma Amazônia protegida.
author: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
source_work: Discours à la COP27, Charm el-Cheikh, 16 novembre 2022
notes: Original of Q0647. Confirmed in the full transcript of Lula's COP27 speech published by G1 and on lula.com.br; it is from COP27, not the 2023 inaugural address.

quote: Celui qui a de l'imagination sans érudition a des ailes et n'a pas de pieds.
author: Joseph Joubert
source_work: Pensées, essais et maximes (1842), Titre IV
notes: Original of Q0695. Confirmed on Wikisource (Titre IV) and independently traced by Quote Investigator to the 1842 first edition.

quote: Πῶς γελοῖος καὶ ξένος ὁ θαυμάζων ὁτιοῦν τῶν ἐν τῷ βίῳ γινομένων.
transliteration: pōs geloios kai xenos ho thaumazōn hotioun tōn en tō biō ginomenōn.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0174. Long renders this sentence almost verbatim; Greek from the Perseus text of the Meditations.

quote: Ἄριστος τρόπος τοῦ ἀμύνεσθαι τὸ μὴ ἐξομοιοῦσθαι.
transliteration: aristos tropos tou amynesthai to mē exomoiousthai.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0176. Hammond translates this chapter word for word as given; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Οἷς συγκεκλήρωσαι πράγμασι, τούτοις συνάρμοζε σεαυτὸν καὶ οἷς συνείληχας ἀνθρώποις, τούτους φίλει, ἀλλ’ ἀληθινῶς.
transliteration: hois synkeklērōsai pragmasi, toutois synarmoze seauton kai hois syneilēchas anthrōpois, toutous philei, all’ alēthinōs.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0177. This is Gregory Hays’s translation of 6.39; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Ἐξάλειψον τὴν φαντασίαν. στῆσον τὴν νευροσπαστίαν. περίγραψον τὸ ἐνεστὼς τοῦ χρόνου.
transliteration: exaleipson tēn phantasian. stēson tēn neurospastian. perigrapson to enestōs tou chronou.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0178. Long has "Confine thyself to the present" in this chapter; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Ἀδικεῖ πολλάκις ὁ μὴ ποιῶν τι, οὐ μόνον ὁ ποιῶν τι.
transliteration: adikei pollakis ho mē poiōn ti, ou monon ho poiōn ti.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0180. Hays: "And you can also commit injustice by doing nothing"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Μηκέθ’ ὅλως περὶ τοῦ οἷόν τινα εἶναι τὸν ἀγαθὸν ἄνδρα διαλέγεσθαι, ἀλλὰ εἶναι τοιοῦτον.
transliteration: mēketh’ holōs peri tou hoion tina einai ton agathon andra dialegesthai, alla einai toiouton.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0181. A circulating form of Hays’s 10.16 ("stop talking about what the good man is like, and just be one"); Greek from Perseus.

quote: Τοῦτον ἰδοὺ τὸν χρόνον σεαυτῷ χάρισαι.
transliteration: touton idou ton chronon seautō charisai.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0183. Hays: "Give yourself a gift: the present moment"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: ἢ ἐπὶ τοῦτο κατεσκεύασμαι, ἵνα κατακείμενος ἐν στρωματίοις ἐμαυτὸν θάλπω;
transliteration: ē epi touto kateskeuasmai, hina katakeimenos en strōmatiois emauton thalpō;
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0185. Long’s text reads "to lie in the bedclothes and keep myself warm"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: Quod tegitur magnum creditur esse malum.
author: Martial
notes: Original of Q0186. A smoothed English version of Martial 3.42, whose Latin reads Quod tegitur magnum creditur esse malum; Latin left out of ORIG_TEXT as it is not Greek.

quote: Vita nec bonum nec malum est: boni ac mali locus est.
author: Seneca the Younger
notes: Original of Q0187. Verified in the Latin Library text of Epistle 99, Vita nec bonum nec malum est boni ac mali locus est; Latin omitted from ORIG_TEXT as it is not Greek.

quote: οὐ δύναμαι τὸν θάνατον ἀποφυγεῖν· τὸ φοβεῖσθαι αὐτὸν μὴ ἀποφύγω
transliteration: ou dynamai ton thanaton apophygein· to phobeisthai auton mē apophygō
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0188. Long’s Discourses 1.27 has "I cannot escape from death. Shall I not escape from the fear of death?"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: καὶ ὡς εὐτελὲς πᾶν τὸ κατεντεινόμενον
transliteration: kai hōs euteles pan to katenteinomenon
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0189. Exactly Hays’s wording in the Fabius Catullinus chapter; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: τάξον τινὰ ἤδη χαρακτῆρα σαυτῷ καὶ τύπον, ὃν φυλάξεις ἐπί τε σεαυτοῦ ὢν καὶ ἀνθρώποις ἐντυγχάνων.
transliteration: taxon tina ēdē charaktēra sautō kai typon, hon phylaxeis epi te seautou ōn kai anthrōpois entynchanōn.
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0190. This is Robert Dobbin’s Penguin rendering of Enchiridion 33; Greek from the Perseus text of the Enchiridion.

quote: μόνον σκέψαι, πόσου πωλεῖς τὴν σεαυτοῦ προαίρεσιν. ἄνθρωπε, εἰ μηδὲν ἄλλο, μὴ ὀλίγου αὐτὴν πωλήσῃς.
transliteration: monon skepsai, posou pōleis tēn seautou proairesin. anthrōpe, ei mēden allo, mē oligou autēn pōlēsēs.
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0191. Long: "consider at what price you sell your own will ... sell it not for a small sum"; no comparable passage in the Meditations.

quote: διὰ τοῦτο, εἶπε, δύο ὦτα ἔχομεν, στόμα δὲ ἕν, ἵνα πλείονα μὲν ἀκούωμεν, ἥττονα δὲ λέγωμεν.
transliteration: dia touto, eipe, dyo ōta echomen, stoma de hen, hina pleiona men akouōmen, hēttona de legōmen.
author: Zeno of Citium
notes: Original of Q0216. Diogenes Laertius credits the two-ears saying to Zeno rebuking a chattering youth, not to Epictetus; Greek from Perseus.

quote: οὐδεὶς ἐλεύθερος ἑαυτοῦ μὴ κρατῶν.
transliteration: oudeis eleutheros heautou mē kratōn.
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0217. English is Crossley’s Golden Sayings XV; Greek is Fragment 35 in Schenkl, though Oldfather groups it among the doubtful fragments.

quote: ταράσσει τοὺς ἀνθρώπους οὐ τὰ πράγματα, ἀλλὰ τὰ περὶ τῶν πραγμάτων δόγματα
transliteration: tarassei tous anthrōpous ou ta pragmata, alla ta peri tōn pragmatōn dogmata
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0218. The opening sentence of Enchiridion 5; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: αἱ περιστάσεις εἰσὶν αἱ τοὺς ἄνδρας δεικνύουσαι.
transliteration: hai peristaseis eisin hai tous andras deiknyousai.
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0219. The standard translation of the chapter’s opening sentence; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: δεῖ τὰ ἐφʼ ἡμῖν βέλτιστα κατασκευάζειν, τοῖς δʼ ἄλλοις χρῆσθαι ὡς πέφυκεν.
transliteration: dei ta ephʼ hēmin beltista kataskeuazein, tois dʼ allois chrēsthai hōs pephyken.
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0220. Elizabeth Carter’s rendering; Long has "make the best use that we can of the things which are in our power".

quote: οὔτε ναῦν ἐξ ἑνὸς ἀγκυρίου οὔτε βίον ἐκ μιᾶς ἐλπίδος ἁρμοστέον.
transliteration: oute naun ex henos ankyriou oute bion ek mias elpidos harmosteon.
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0221. English is Crossley’s Golden Sayings XVI; Greek is Fragment 30 in Schenkl, classed by Oldfather among the doubtful fragments.

quote: οὐδέν, ἔφη, τῶν μεγάλων ἄφνω γίνεται, ὅπου γε οὐδʼ ὁ βότρυς οὐδὲ σῦκον.
transliteration: ouden, ephē, tōn megalōn aphnō ginetai, hopou ge oudʼ ho botrys oude sykon.
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0222. The grape-and-fig passage in Arrian’s Discourses; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: γνῶθι πρῶτον τίς εἶ καὶ οὕτως κόσμει σεαυτόν.
transliteration: gnōthi prōton tis ei kai houtōs kosmei seauton.
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0223. Word for word the standard translation of 3.1.24; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: εἰ τι ἀγαθὸν θέλεις, παρὰ σεαυτοῦ λάβε.
transliteration: ei ti agathon theleis, para seautou labe.
author: Epictetus
notes: Original of Q0226. Long: "If you would have any thing good, receive it from yourself"; Greek from the Perseus text.

quote: ἔλεγέ τε κρεῖττον εἶναι τοῖς ποσὶν ὀλισθεῖν ἢ τῇ γλώττῃ.
transliteration: elege te kreitton einai tois posin olisthein ē tē glōttē.
author: Zeno
notes: Original of Q0232. Hicks’s Loeb wording exactly, though Diogenes Laertius adds that some credit the saying to Socrates; Greek from Perseus.

quote: ἔστι δὲ αὐτὸ τὸ πάθος κατὰ Ζήνωνα ἡ ἄλογος καὶ παρὰ φύσιν ψυχῆς κίνησις ἢ ὁρμὴ πλεονάζουσα.
transliteration: esti de auto to pathos kata zēnōna hē alogos kai para physin psychēs kinēsis ē hormē pleonazousa.
author: Zeno
notes: Original of Q0233. The older English rendering of Zeno’s definition of passion, which Cicero also reports at Tusculans 4.6; Greek from Perseus.

quote: Ἀρχὴ τοῦ μὴ κατοκνεῖν τὰ ἀσχήμονα πράττειν τὸ μὴ κατοκνεῖν τὰ ἀσχήμονα λέγειν.
transliteration: archē tou mē katoknein ta aschēmona prattein to mē katoknein ta aschēmona legein.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Original of Q0234. Greek from Hense’s 1905 Teubner edition, where the word prattein is Gaisford’s supplement printed in angle brackets.

quote: τοὺς δὲ ἀνθρώπους ἀνάγκη τὰ μὴ φανερὰ μηδʼ αὐτόθεν γνώριμα διὰ τῶν φανερῶν καὶ προδήλων ζητεῖν ἀνευρίσκειν, ὅπερ ἔργον ἀποδείξεώς ἐστιν.
transliteration: tous de anthrōpous anankē ta mē phanera mēdʼ autothen gnōrima dia tōn phanerōn kai prodēlōn zētein aneuriskein, hoper ergon apodeixeōs estin.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Original of Q0235. Lutz: "Man must needs seek to find out that which is not plain nor self-evident through the medium of the plain and obvious"; Greek from Hense.

quote: Τοῦ ἀποθανεῖν ὁμοίως ἐπικεκλωσμένου πᾶσιν, οὐ τὸ βραδέως ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐμφανῶς ἀποθανεῖν μακάριον.
transliteration: tou apothanein homoiōs epikeklōsmenou pasin, ou to bradeōs alla to emphanōs apothanein makarion.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Original of Q0236. Greek from Hense’s Fragmenta minora; Cynthia King renders it closely as given.

quote: οὕτω γὰρ μόνως ἔσται τις ἐκ φιλοσοφίας ὠφελημένος, ἂν οἷς παραδέδεκται λόγοις οὖσιν ὑγιέσι τὰ ἔργα παρέχηται συνῳδά.
transliteration: houtō gar monōs estai tis ek philosophias ōphelēmenos, an hois paradedektai logois ousin hygiesi ta erga parechētai synōda.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Original of Q0237. The closing sentence of Discourse 1 in Hense; Lutz translates "only in this way will philosophy be of profit to anyone".

quote: ὥστε ὁ ἀναιρῶν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων γάμον ἀναιρεῖ μὲν οἶκον, ἀναιρεῖ δὲ πόλιν, ἀναιρεῖ δὲ σύμπαν τὸ ἀνθρώπειον γένος.
transliteration: hōste ho anairōn ex anthrōpōn gamon anairei men oikon, anairei de polin, anairei de sympan to anthrōpeion genos.
author: Musonius Rufus
notes: Original of Q0238. Lutz’s translation of Discourse 14 matches almost word for word; Greek from Hense.

quote: ἰδών ποτε μειράκιον ἐρυθριῶν, θάρρει, ἔφη· τοιοῦτόν ἐστι τῆς ἀρετῆς τὸ χρῶμα.
transliteration: idōn pote meirakion erythriōn, tharrei, ephē· toiouton esti tēs aretēs to chrōma.
author: Diogenes
notes: Original of Q0241. The real anecdote has Diogenes tell a blushing youth "Courage, that is the hue of virtue"; the epigram is a later compression.

quote: ἐρωτηθεὶς πόθεν εἴη, κοσμοπολίτης, ἔφη.
transliteration: erōtētheis pothen eiē, kosmopolitēs, ephē.
author: Diogenes
notes: Original of Q0243. Diogenes’ attested answer is the single word kosmopolites; the longer "not an Athenian or a Greek" form comes from Plutarch’s On Exile, where it is Socrates’.

quote: τὸ νικᾶν αὐτὸν αὑτὸν πασῶν νικῶν πρώτη τε καὶ ἀρίστη
transliteration: to nikan auton hauton pasōn nikōn prōtē te kai aristē
author: Plato
notes: Original of Q0264. Greek from the Perseus text of the Laws; the words are spoken by Cleinias in the dialogue’s opening exchange.

quote: πολλὰ τὰ δεινὰ κοὐδὲν ἀν- / θρώπου δεινότερον πέλει.
transliteration: polla ta deina kouden an- / thrōpou deinoteron pelei.
author: Sophocles
notes: Original of Q0462. This is Fitts and Fitzgerald’s 1938 translation of the Ode to Man; Greek from the Wikiquote Sophocles page.

quote: Οὐδὲν οὐδενὶ συμβαίνει ὃ οὐχὶ πέφυκε φέρειν.
transliteration: ouden oudeni symbainei ho ouchi pephyke pherein.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Original of Q0482. An archaic loose rendering of 5.18, which Long gives as "Nothing happens to any man which he is not formed by nature to bear".

quote: πάντα χωρεῖ καὶ οὐδὲν μένει
transliteration: panta chōrei kai ouden menei
author: Heraclitus
notes: Original of Q0508. Wikiquote lists "All is flux, nothing stays still" as a variant translation of this Heraclitean sentence quoted by Plato.

quote: ἔστι τι τὸ ὅλον παρὰ τὰ μόρια
transliteration: esti ti to holon para ta moria
author: Aristotle
notes: Original of Q0519. Greek from the Perseus text; the English condenses Aristotle’s point that a whole is not a mere heap of its parts.

quote: ἐπιστήμῃ γὰρ οἶμαι δεῖ κρίνεσθαι ἀλλʼ οὐ πλήθει τὸ μέλλον καλῶς κριθήσεσθαι.
transliteration: epistēmē gar oimai dei krinesthai allʼ ou plēthei to mellon kalōs krithēsesthai.
author: Plato
notes: Original of Q0555. Socrates argues a decision must be judged by knowledge and not by numbers; Greek from the Perseus text of the Laches.

quote: Caminante, son tus huellas / el camino y nada más; / caminante, no hay camino, / se hace camino al andar.
author: Antonio Machado
source_work: Antonio Machado, "Proverbios y cantares" XXIX, in Campos de Castilla (1912)
notes: Original of Q0001. Checked the Campos de Castilla text in the Biblioteca Virtual Miguel de Cervantes: the poem reads "caminante, no hay camino, / se hace camino al andar", of which the bank line is a faithful English condensation.

quote: Det er vanskeligt at spaa, især naar det gælder Fremtiden.
source_work: Danish saying of unknown authorship, current in Denmark by the mid-twentieth century; quoted by Karl Kristian Steincke in his memoirs Farvel og Tak (1948)
notes: Original of Q0171. Quote Investigator traces the saying to Danish sources and finds no support for the common Niels Bohr attribution, so the bank's "Unknown" is the correct attribution.

quote: Que a minha loucura seja perdoada, pois metade de mim e amor e a outra metade tambem.
author: Oswaldo Montenegro
notes: Original of Q0497. A faithful English rendering of Montenegro's Portuguese poem/song 'Metade'; original supplied.

quote: On ne voit bien qu'avec le coeur. L'essentiel est invisible pour les yeux.
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupery
source_work: Le Petit Prince (1943), ch. XXI (the fox)
notes: Original of Q0601. The fox's line in Le Petit Prince; French original supplied. Widely confirmed.

quote: Es ist nicht genug zu wissen, man muss auch anwenden; es ist nicht genug zu wollen, man muss auch tun.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
source_work: Wilhelm Meisters Wanderjahre (1829), 'Betrachtungen im Sinne der Wanderer'
notes: Original of Q0611. The English is a translation of Goethe's aphorism from Wilhelm Meisters Wanderjahre; Bruce Lee adopted and popularised it (it is on his memorial), but the words are Goethe's. German original supplied.

quote: Omnia tamquam mortales timetis, omnia tamquam immortales concupiscitis.
author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
source_work: Seneca, On the Shortness of Life (De Brevitate Vitae), 3.4
notes: Original of Q0646. The English renders De Brevitate Vitae 3.4; the Latin original is confirmed in editions of Seneca's Opera. Latin supplied.

quote: To be fully alive, fully human, and completely awake is to be continually thrown out of the nest.
author: Pema Chodron
notes: Taken as written in the source note; not checked.

quote: To accomplish great things, we must not only act, but also dream; not only plan, but also believe.
author: Anatole France
notes: Taken as written in the source note; not checked.

quote: Do not go where the path may lead, go instead where there is no path and leave a trail.
author: Ralph Emerson
notes: Taken as written in the source note; not checked.

quote: Das Schicksal besteht aus zwei Tagen / Einer ist sicher einer Gefahr / Und unser Leben hat zwei Hälften / Eine ist trüb eine ist klar / Wage/Sage zu dem der uns geschmäht hat um unseres Schicksals Willen / Hat je das Schicksal einen geprüft der ohne Bedeutsamkeit war / Am Himmel stehen Sterne ohne Zahl / Und doch sind nur Sonne und Mond / Einander verfinsternd ein Paar / Wie schön waren deine Gedanken als schöne Tage erschienen / Hattest du keine Angst vor dem nächsten Tag oder Jahr / Die Nächte erschienen dir friedlich du ließest dich täuschen / Doch in der klarsten Nacht erscheint der schrecklichste Mahr
notes: Taken as written in the source note; not checked. Unattributed in the source note, filed as "Short Prayer".

quote: The greatest way to live with honor in this world is to be what we pretend to be.
author: Socrates
notes: Taken as written in the source note; not checked.

quote: Everything that exists is in a manner the seed of that which will be.
author: Marcus Aurelius
notes: Taken as written in the source note; not checked.

quote: All difficult things have their origin in that which is easy, and great things in that which is small.
